sections.context: Run run_s7vhgvkvc1v6 (2026-05-27) was triggered by a plan-run, hit an Anthropic overloaded_error (529) inside 7 seconds, produced zero model output, but warren finalized the run as `succeeded`. The plan-run machinery then opened a PR with stale branch state, waited for merge, and advanced — propagating a false-success into downstream automation. Any future provider outage (overloaded, rate limit, network) will produce the same silent-success failure mode. Plan-run authors and operators relying on run outcomes need agent_end-with-error to surface as failed so reap's failure-reason inference and downstream gates kick in.
sections.reproduction:
1. Trigger any pi-runtime run while Anthropic returns a 529 overloaded_error (or stub the pi agent_end event payload in src/runs/stream.test.ts to mirror the observed shape: { type: 'agent_end', stopReason: 'error', errorMessage: '{"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"Overloaded"}}', usage: { input: 0, output: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, content: [], willRetry: true }).
2. Observe: detectRuntimeTerminal in src/runs/stream.ts:508 returns 'succeeded' because `env.type === 'agent_end'` is the only check; the error signals in the payload are ignored.
3. Bridge calls reap with outcome='succeeded'; reap.ts:902-905 only invokes inferFailureReason when outcome === 'failed', so the run finalizes as succeeded with zero events of useful work.
4. Expected: detectRuntimeTerminal returns 'failed' for this payload, reap transitions the run to failed, and inferFailureReason populates failure_reason.
sections.root_cause: src/runs/stream.ts detectRuntimeTerminal (lines 501-510) maps `agent_end` → 'succeeded' unconditionally: `if (env.type === 'agent_end') return 'succeeded';`. The claude-code path one line above (`env.type === 'result'`) inspects `env.is_error` and returns 'failed' when true; the pi path has no equivalent guard. Pi's agent_end envelope carries clear error signals (stopReason === 'error', non-empty errorMessage, zero-usage, empty content array) that the function never inspects. Because the bridge hands 'succeeded' to reap, reap.ts:904 skips inferFailureReason and the run records as succeeded despite zero model work.
sections.approach: Extend detectRuntimeTerminal in src/runs/stream.ts to inspect the pi agent_end payload for error signals and return 'failed' when any are present. Authoritative signals, in order of preference: (1) `stopReason === 'error'` on the envelope, (2) non-empty string `errorMessage`. These are emitted by burrow's pi parser whenever pi reports an error condition. Do NOT use zero-tokens or empty-content alone as a failure signal — a legitimately quick noop run could share that shape; require an explicit error marker. Mirror the existing claude-code pattern (`env.is_error === true ? 'failed' : 'succeeded'`) for symmetry. Add a focused unit test in src/runs/stream.test.ts covering the overloaded_error payload and a happy-path agent_end (no error signals) to lock in the discriminator. Skip the optional reap-side safety net suggested in the bug description (downgrade succeeded → failed when no stdout/thinking/tool_use events were observed) — that would touch reap.ts + reap.test.ts in addition to stream.ts + stream.test.ts (4 files) and is a separate, broader hardening. File a follow-up if a second incident proves the runtime-side fix isn't sufficient.

steps.title: Inspect pi agent_end payload for error signals in detectRuntimeTerminal
steps.description: In src/runs/stream.ts, modify detectRuntimeTerminal (around lines 501-510). For the `env.type === 'agent_end'` branch, before returning 'succeeded', check: (a) `typeof env.stopReason === 'string' && env.stopReason === 'error'` → return 'failed'; (b) `typeof env.errorMessage === 'string' && env.errorMessage.length > 0` → return 'failed'. Otherwise return 'succeeded' as today. Mirror the existing claude-code `result` branch one line above for stylistic consistency. Add a short inline comment citing warren-e281 explaining why agent_end can carry an error envelope (pi runtime exits with stopReason='error' and a serialized provider error in errorMessage when the underlying API errors mid-stream, e.g. Anthropic 529 overloaded_error). Do not touch isPiAgentEnd (lines ~520-535) — its purpose is the piStats snapshot trigger, which should still fire on any agent_end (success or failure) so the final usage record gets fetched.

steps.title: Add stream.test.ts coverage for agent_end-with-error and agent_end-success
steps.description: In src/runs/stream.test.ts, add a describe block (or extend an existing one) for detectRuntimeTerminal. Add two tests: (1) 'agent_end with stopReason=error returns failed' — construct a RunEvent with kind='state_change', stream='system', payload={ type: 'agent_end', stopReason: 'error', errorMessage: '{"type":"error","error":{"type":"overloaded_error","message":"Overloaded"}}', usage: { input: 0, output: 0, totalTokens: 0 }, content: [], willRetry: true }, assert detectRuntimeTerminal returns 'failed'. (2) 'agent_end without error signals returns succeeded' — same shape but stopReason='end_turn' (or omitted) and no errorMessage, assert returns 'succeeded'. If detectRuntimeTerminal is not exported, export it for testing or add a thin test-only re-export alongside the existing seam pattern in stream.ts (check how stream.test.ts already accesses internals before adding new exports). Also add a regression assertion that an agent_end-with-error event does NOT cause isPiAgentEnd to return false — the piStats trigger should still fire.

steps.title: Release: run /release per .claude/commands/release.md
steps.description: Run the release command per .claude/commands/release.md. Confirm bun run check:all passes before release.

acceptance: detectRuntimeTerminal in src/runs/stream.ts returns 'failed' for any agent_end event whose payload has stopReason === 'error' OR a non-empty errorMessage.
detectRuntimeTerminal still returns 'succeeded' for agent_end events with no error signals (regression-locked by a test).
isPiAgentEnd still returns true for agent_end events regardless of error state, so the piStats snapshot trigger continues to fire.
New tests in src/runs/stream.test.ts pass under `bun test src/runs/stream.test.ts`.
bun run check:all passes.

name: Map pi agent_end with error payload to failed in detectRuntimeTerminal

sections.context: Of the last 30 PRs (#122–#151), 10 had failing first-pass CI runs. Every failure falls into two classes that share the same shape: the local quality gate the agent ran accepted work that CI then rejected. Class A (10 PRs) is the ci-postgres FK qualifier ("public".X) — never executed by `bun run check:all` because there is no local postgres test matrix, so the migration that aborts in CI passes locally. Class B (PR #151) is `validate:agents-md` flagging gitignored build artifacts; this IS in check:all but the agent skipped the gate and committed anyway. The substrate already exists (warren-5797 landed `qualityGate` in `.warren/config.yaml`, `WARREN_QUALITY_GATE` env injection in `composeRunEnv()`, and the `scripts/hooks/pre-commit` hook), but parity has drifted: pre-commit runs a strict subset of check:all, check:all runs a strict subset of CI (missing `check:duplicates` and the entire ci-postgres workflow), `.warren/config.yaml` for this repo does not set `qualityGate`, and built-in agent prompts (claude-code/sapling/pi) describe the gate as advisory rather than a terminal condition. Net result: a diligent agent following the prompt verbatim will still ship PRs that break CI on first pass, blocking auto-merge and forcing manual intervention.
sections.approach: Collapse the three diverged gate definitions (pre-commit hook, `bun run check:all`, CI workflows) onto a single source of truth, then enforce parity structurally. Five wedges: (1) Extend `check:all` so it runs every CI step locally, including `check:duplicates` and a real `bun run test:pg` that boots a docker postgres via testcontainers-style helper and runs the matrix tests; (2) add `scripts/check-ci-parity.ts` that parses the GitHub workflow YAMLs, extracts each `bun run <X>` invocation, and fails if any step isn't reachable from `check:all` — wire into check:all itself so future CI drift breaks the local gate immediately; (3) set `qualityGate: "bun run check:all"` in this repo's `.warren/config.yaml` so deployed agents pick it up via WARREN_QUALITY_GATE without falling through to fuzzy fallback heuristics; (4) replace the pre-commit hook body with `exec bun run check:all` so a forgetful agent literally cannot commit a red tree; (5) rewrite the operating-contract block in the three coding-agent built-ins from advisory ("fix failures before committing") to terminal ("you are not done until $WARREN_QUALITY_GATE exits zero on the final commit … do not declare the task complete with a red gate"). Optional follow-on: a WARREN_QUALITY_GATE_REQUIRED=1 reap-side check that refuses to push if the last commit lacks a green-gate marker — closes the prompt-bypass loop entirely, but ship the prompt+parity wedges first.

Setting qualityGate in this repo only affects warren-on-warren runs. Other projects warren manages still need their own .warren/config.yaml. Document the convention; not a blocker.

sections.context: warren-4553 introduced per-file (500 line) and per-function line-count guards. 48 files were pinned in scripts/file-size-budgets.json above the threshold, and 8 files were grandfathered with biome noExcessiveLinesPerFunction overrides. The largest offenders — handlers.ts (4233 lines), reap.ts (2114), proxy.ts (912) — impose high cognitive load, slow code review, and make parallel agent development harder. This plan covers the ~8 production files over 700 lines and the 8 biome function-length overrides (6 of which overlap with the production splits). Files barely above 500, acceptance test scenarios, and UI workspace files are deferred to a follow-up seed.
sections.behavior_invariant: Every existing HTTP endpoint, CLI command, and UI page must behave identically after each split. The public API surface (route paths, request/response shapes, status codes, error envelopes) is frozen — only internal module boundaries change. All existing tests must pass with assertion logic unmodified (import paths may change). The file-size ratchet in scripts/file-size-budgets.json must never increase — each step lowers or removes entries for files it touches. No new public exports are introduced; each split re-exports exactly what the original module exported from the new index.ts.
sections.approach: Module extraction into same-name subdirectories. For each monolithic .ts file: (1) create a same-name subdirectory with an index.ts that re-exports the public API — callers update only the import path suffix (.ts → /index.ts), (2) move logic into domain-scoped files inside the subdirectory, (3) split the colocated test file into matching test files, (4) lower or remove the file-size-budgets.json entry, (5) remove the biome noExcessiveLinesPerFunction override if applicable, (6) verify bun run check:all passes. For biome-only overrides on test files without oversized production counterparts (client.test.ts, refresh.test.ts), extract long test functions into smaller blocks or shared test helpers. The handlers.ts split is serialized into 3 steps because each touches the same source file; all other steps are independent and can run in parallel.

sections.context:
An audit of the Warren UI (src/ui, Tailwind v4 + CSS-first @theme tokens, CVA/Radix shadcn-style primitives, react-query) found a competent but flat and inconsistent surface. The declared brand fonts (Inter / JetBrains Mono) are never actually loaded, so most users render system fonts. There is no brand color (--color-primary is just gray). Only colors are tokenized — radius, shadow, spacing, and z-index are raw utilities that drift. Light neutrals are achromatic while dark neutrals are blue-tinted, so the gray ramps don't match across modes, and the dark token set is physically duplicated in two CSS blocks. No @custom-variant dark is defined for v4, so dark:-prefixed status colors track OS preference instead of the manual data-theme toggle. Status state is mapped in 3+ divergent places (StateBadge, PlotStatusBadge, PlanRunStateBadge, plus an ad-hoc statusVariant() in RunDetail) with color collisions and no icons/pulse. There are no loading skeletons/spinners (bare

Loading…

repeated ~10x), no Select/Checkbox/Tooltip/Alert/EmptyState/Toast primitives (raw
sections.approach: Tighten the existing stack rather than migrate it (keep Tailwind v4 @theme, CVA, Radix, react-query). Work in dependency order from foundations up: (1) fix the token layer in index.css — self-host Inter + JetBrains Mono via @fontsource, unify the gray ramp to one cool-neutral hue family across modes, introduce a single muted-green brand/accent hue (desaturated, chroma <~0.12) matching the os-eco ecosystem, tokenize the status palette into semantic vars (--color-success/warning/info/danger/neutral), add --radius-*, tinted --shadow-*, and a --z-* scale, add @custom-variant dark to fix the toggle, collapse the duplicated dark block, and apply tabular-nums to data surfaces. (2) Upgrade existing primitives (Button/Card/Input/Textarea/Badge/Table/Dialog) with token-based hover, active/pressed feedback, deliberate transition durations, and Card elevation variants. (3) Add the missing primitives (Select, Checkbox, Spinner, Skeleton, Tooltip). (4) Collapse all status mapping into one StatusIndicator registry (state -> label + color token + icon + optional running pulse) consumed by every badge wrapper. (5) Add shared state components (Alert/Callout, EmptyState, Toast) and a formatError() util. (6) Add framer-motion as a lightweight motion layer for staggered entry, event-stream item animations, and dialog/skeleton transitions, gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. (7) Promote repeated layout recipes (PageHeader, Field, FilterPill/Toggle group) and sweep ad-hoc rounded-md border containers onto Card variants. (8) Decompose PlotDetail.tsx onto the new primitives. Each phase is independently shippable, gated by bun run check:all (lint/typecheck/coverage/file-size/duplicates/deps/bundle-size), and lands as its own child seed. The final child runs the patch release flow.

sections.context: Warren already ships a Cost Analytics dashboard, but the rich per-run logs (the `runs` token/cost columns plus the `events` table's `tool_use`/`tool_result` trace) are otherwise unmined. The operator wants a dedicated Run Analytics dashboard that answers behavioral questions the cost view can't: how much context (input + cache-read tokens) agents burn on average, which seeds consumed the most context, and — most importantly — where agents get stuck (commands they run repeatedly or that fail, e.g. `ml`, `sd`, `gh`/git, `bun run check:all`). Scouting confirmed the data is recoverable: per-run context lives in `runs.tokens_input/tokens_cache_read/tokens_output/cost_usd`; seed grouping works via `runs.seed_id` (seed-originated runs only); Bash commands land as `tool_use` events at `payload.input.command` with outcomes in correlated `tool_result` events (`is_error` + `content`, joined by `tool_use_id`). Known limitation: claude-code emits a single cumulative token total per run while pi emits per-turn, so per-turn growth curves are pi-only and per-run totals are the cross-runtime baseline.
sections.approach: Mirror the existing Cost Analytics architecture exactly: pure, dialect-agnostic aggregator modules under `src/runs/analytics/` (each with a co-located `*.test.ts`), thin `RouteHandler` factories under a new `src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts` (keeping the grandfathered `lifecycle.ts` from growing), and a TanStack-Query UI page that leans on the existing shadcn components (`Card`, `Table`, `PageHeader`) plus the `CostAnalytics.tsx` filter pattern (`useSearchParams` project + date-range). Two endpoints under the already-registered `/analytics` prefix split the work by cost: `GET /analytics/runs` reads only the `runs` table (fast) for KPIs, time-series, per-agent/per-model breakdowns and top-seeds-by-context; `GET /analytics/behavior` scans `tool_use`/`tool_result` events (heavier, capped) for generalized command mining — ranking ALL commands by frequency/failure/retry with the os-eco toolchain (ml/sd/gh/bun check:all) highlighted — and a derived insights layer. Graphs use recharts (operator-approved new dependency) for time-series and bar charts; the bundle-size ratchet is bumped once with this tracker reference. Phase 1 ships run-level metrics + context + charts; Phase 2 layers behavioral command-mining + insights callouts on top.

alternatives.rejected_because: Event-table scanning for command mining is materially heavier than reading the runs table; splitting lets the fast run-level view render immediately and the heavy behavior view load/cap independently

steps.title: Fix generalizeBun collapsing bun subcommands into 'bun run <sub>'
steps.description: src/runs/analytics/command-mining.ts:194-200 (generalizeBun). For any 'bun <x>' where x is not 'run', the helper treats x as a run-script name and returns `bun run ${x}`. This is wrong for bun's own subcommands: generalizeCommand('bun install') -> 'bun run install', 'bun add foo' -> 'bun run add', 'bun remove x' -> 'bun run remove'. The mislabelled signature then miscategorizes in categorize() as 'other' instead of 'package' (categorize('bun install') is only correct because the unit test calls it with the raw string the pipeline never produces). Fix: in generalizeBun, when the first non-flag arg is a known bun subcommand (install, add, remove, ci, uninstall, update, x, create, init, link, unlink, pm, outdated, upgrade, etc. — at minimum the package-management subcommands already in PKG_SUBS), return `bun ${sub}` (mirroring the git/gh/sd MULTI_SUBCOMMAND treatment) rather than `bun run ${sub}`. Keep 'bun run <script>', bare 'bun <script>', 'bun test', and 'bun run test' family behaviour exactly as-is. Add regression cases to command-mining.test.ts under the generalizeCommand describe block: generalizeCommand('bun install') === 'bun install', 'bun add foo' === 'bun add', and assert categorize(generalizeCommand('bun install')) === 'package'. Correct looks like: the composed generalize->categorize pipeline labels bun package operations as 'package', not 'other'.

steps.title: Fix categorize() substring matching misclassifying scripts
steps.description: src/runs/analytics/command-mining.ts:209-214 (categorize, package-manager branch). It uses generalized.includes('test') and generalized.includes('build') — substring matches against the whole generalized string. So 'bun run latest' is categorized as 'test' (because 'latest' contains 'test'), and 'bun run prebuild' / 'bun run rebuild' as 'build'. Fix: inspect the script token rather than the full string. After generalizeBun the shape is 'bun run <script>' or 'bun test'; match on the script token (e.g. parts[2] for the 'bun run <script>' form, or detect the 'bun test' signature explicitly) using equality or a token-prefix check (script === 'test' || script.startsWith('test:') ; script === 'build' || script.startsWith('build:')) instead of String.includes on the whole command. steps.title: Align worst-success-agent denominator with the rate it reports
steps.description: src/runs/analytics/insights.ts:141-157 (worstSuccessAgent). The MIN_AGENT_TERMINAL_RUNS gate (line 143) and the detail string (lines 153-154) both use `g.succeeded + g.failed` as the terminal-run count, but RunGroupBucket.successRate (src/runs/analytics/run-metrics.ts finalizeGroup) is computed as succeeded / (succeeded + failed + cancelled). When an agent has cancelled runs, the reported rate's denominator silently disagrees with the 'of N terminal run(s)' the callout prints, and the >= MIN_AGENT_TERMINAL_RUNS gate can skip (or admit) an agent based on a count that does not match the rate. RunGroupBucket does NOT expose `cancelled`, so do NOT add a field (that would change the wire shape / public interface — out of scope for this plan; the standalone seed warren-92ad tracks shape questions). Instead, make the displayed/derived count consistent with the rate that is exposed: either (a) reword the detail so it does not assert a specific terminal denominator (e.g. 'succeeded in only X% of its terminal runs'), and gate on a metric available consistently, or (b) derive the count the rate already implies. Pick the option that keeps successRate as the single source of truth and removes the succeeded+failed vs succeeded+failed+cancelled split-brain. Update insights.test.ts to cover an agent bucket with cancelled > 0 and assert the callout text no longer contradicts successRate. Correct looks like: the percentage and any count in the callout are derived from one consistent terminal definition.

sections.context: LEVERET.md §0 promotes the V1 spec for Leveret, warren's pi-backed conversational overseer: the operator chats with Leveret to shape a Plot's intent live, then sends the Plot off so the system plans and dispatches the work. This plan covers the WARREN-side slice only; the burrow pi-chat runtime (drop --no-extensions, hold stdin on agent_end, auto-answer extension_ui_request, EXA_API_KEY passthrough, goldens — §0.0.E/0.3/0.11) lands in a separate burrow plan, and the ../plot agent-actor intent_edited ACL widening (§0.6/0.11) lands in the ../plot repo. Warren must add a durable conversation store (conversations/messages tables + a plots JSON-blob projection), a mode:"conversation" long-lived run kept alive across turns, the leveret builtin shipping the propose_intent extension, a conversation stream bridge that writes intent_edited(actor=leveret) host-side, conversation API + a top-level Leveret UI, a PR-gated send-off (plotSync PR -> PR-merge poller -> auto-dispatched planner -> operator-gated plan-run), and removal of the old mode=interactive/brainstorm respawn-per-turn path while keeping the no-Plot batch path byte-identical.
sections.approach: Follow the §0.12 build-phase ordering, warren-only: (phase 2) land the store first — conversations/messages tables + mode:"conversation" + repos, the plots JSON-blob projection + PlotsRepo + plot-client upsert hook, lifetime exemptions, idle-timeout coordinator, and transcript-replay re-wake; (phase 3) the pi_extensions seeding path, the leveret builtin + propose_intent extension, and the conversation stream bridge that persists turns and writes intent_edited(actor=leveret); (phase 4) conversation API endpoints + the top-level Leveret split-view UI; (phase 5) PR-gated send-off — plotSync PR + close conversation, the PR-merge poller boot-worker that auto-dispatches the planner on merge, and the operator-gated Dispatch-plan popup; (phase 6, last, once parity is proven) retire mode=interactive/brainstorm. Each step reuses an existing warren seam (ProjectsRepo template, src/plot-client/, bootPauseDetector, src/plan-runs/pr-merge.ts, the planner builtin, src/runs/seed.ts pi_skills/pi_prompts, Chat.tsx) so the work stays additive and the existing run/burrow/plan-run/events spine is never rewritten. Cross-repo prerequisites (burrow pi-chat runtime, plot ACL) are tracked as external dependencies, not steps in this plan.

sections.context: The Leveret backend is fully wired — POST /conversations (create + spawn anchoring run), POST /conversations/:id/messages (steer), POST /conversations/:id/send-off (plotSync PR + close), and the rewakeConversation() primitive in src/runs/conversation-rewake.ts all exist. But the UI cannot drive the loop: src/ui/src/api/client.ts conversationsApi only exposes list/get/postMessage (no create, no sendOff, no rewake); LeveretPage has no 'New conversation' affordance (empty state says 'Start one from a Plot' but nothing implements it); the IntentPane 'Send to planner' button is a STUB that only sets a note ('Planner send-off lands in warren-756d / warren-6e45'); and rewakeConversation has no HTTP route, so an idle-finalized conversation (anchoringRunId === null) becomes a read-only dead end. Net effect: an operator literally cannot start or finish a Leveret conversation from the UI. This plan closes those three gaps so the conversation -> intent -> send-off (-> re-wake) loop is fully operable from the UI alone, matching LEVERET.md §0.9.
sections.approach:
Forward-chained: land the two foundations (a backend re-wake route + a frontend API layer) first, then the three UI affordances that depend on them, then test coverage. Reuse existing seams everywhere; introduce no new dispatch/lifecycle logic.

Step 1 (backend re-wake route): Add rewakeConversationHandler to src/server/handlers/conversations.ts wrapping the existing rewakeConversation() primitive (src/runs/conversation-rewake.ts) — resolve the conversation, forward the reusable spawn deps from ServerDeps exactly as createConversationHandler does, start the bridge on the new anchoring run, return the updated conversation row. Register { method: 'POST', pattern: '/conversations/:id/re-wake' } in ROUTE_TABLE (src/server/handlers/index.ts) and add it to the conversations entry of the route-prefix allowlist. Add conversations.test.ts cases (re-wake of a terminal anchoring run rotates anchoringRunId + returns 200; re-wake of a live run surfaces the primitive's 400; unknown conversation 404). Regenerate with bun run gen:docs && bun run gen:openapi and commit docs/http-api.md + docs/openapi.yaml. DONE: route reachable, handler test green, gen:docs:check + gen:openapi:check pass.

In src/ui/src/api/client.ts add conversationsApi.create (POST /conversations, snake_case body project_id/plot_id/title/message/dispatcher_handle), .sendOff (POST /conversations/:id/send-off, optional planner_agent), and .rewake (POST /conversations/:id/re-wake). Step 3 (New conversation dialog): Add src/ui/src/pages/leveret/new-conversation-dialog.tsx modeled on conversation-detail/dispatch-plan-dialog.tsx — Dialog with a required Project select (projectsApi.list), a Plot mode radio (auto-create vs attach), an attach Plot select (plotsApi.list scoped to project, only enabled when project.hasPlot), an optional Title input and optional opening-message Textarea. sections.context: The run-analytics page (src/ui/src/pages/RunAnalytics.tsx) surfaces run counts, success rate, duration, avg context tokens, and cost — but gives no visibility into raw token consumption: how many input/output/cache-read/cache-write tokens warren's runs burn, which models and providers consume them, and how that trends over time. Operators tuning cost and capacity need this to spot expensive models, cache-efficiency regressions, and consumption spikes. All the raw data already exists: runs persist tokens_input/tokens_output/tokens_cache_read/tokens_cache_write (hydrated from events via aggregateUsageFromEvents in src/runs/usage-aggregate.ts), and buildRunMetrics (src/runs/analytics/run-metrics.ts) already groups byModel/byProvider via rendered_agent_json frontmatter extraction. What is missing is token-kind breakdowns in the aggregation, tokens-over-time series (overall and per-model/per-provider), API exposure, and UI charts/tables.
sections.approach:
Extend the existing /analytics/runs pipeline end-to-end rather than building a parallel system — every layer already has the right seam.

BACKEND (steps 1-2, pure functions first): Extend RunMetricsRow and buildRunMetrics in src/runs/analytics/run-metrics.ts so each grouping bucket (byAgent, byModel, byProvider) and the totals carry a token breakdown object { input, output, cacheRead, cacheWrite, total } summed from the run rows (treat null columns as 0; rows are already hydrated by hydrateRunsUsage for terminal runs). Then add tokens-over-time aggregation: reuse the existing daily-bucket logic from buildTimeSeries to emit (a) an overall daily series with per-kind token values and (b) per-model and per-provider daily series, capped at the top N (5) consumers by total tokens with the remainder folded into an 'other' bucket so the UI stays legible. Both steps are pure-aggregation changes with co-located unit tests, no API surface change yet.

API (step 3): Add a `tokens` section to the GET /analytics/runs response in src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts — shape { totals, byModel, byProvider, timeSeries, byModelTimeSeries, byProviderTimeSeries } — wired from the new aggregators using the same filter (from/to/projectId) plumbing. Update docs/openapi.yaml in the same change so gen:openapi:check passes (the OpenAPI schema is kept in sync with ROUTE_TABLE by hand).

UI (steps 4-6): First mirror the new response types into src/ui/src/api/types.ts and the runAnalyticsApi client (src/ui/src/api/client.ts) — the page already fetches /analytics/runs via tanstack-query so no new fetch is needed. Then add two presentation units under src/ui/src/pages/run-analytics/: (1) a TokenConsumption chart component using the existing recharts ChartContainer seam — stacked area of daily tokens by kind, with a segmented toggle to re-stack by model or by provider using the per-dimension series; (2) detailed stats — token KPI cards (total tokens, input/output split, cache-read share) and per-model + per-provider token tables (tokens by kind, share of total, cost-per-1M-tokens derived from existing cost data) following the KpiCards.tsx / Tables.tsx patterns and formatTokens from format.ts.

POLISH (step 7): Empty/sparse-window states (no NaN, no empty-stack rendering glitches), filter-respect verification across from/to/projectId, bundle-size re-baseline via `bun run check:bundle-size:build --update` if the new chart code moves the budget, and a full `bun run check:all` pass.

This order is forward-chained so each child PR passes CI independently: aggregation (pure, tested) → API + OpenAPI (atomic so gen:openapi:check never drifts) → UI types → UI chart and UI stats in parallel → final polish.

The two-tier split (/analytics/runs vs /analytics/behavior) exists for the heavier event-mining path, which tokens are not.

sections.context: Leveret conversations whose anchoring run dies before producing any events render as a blank chat with zero operator-visible signal. Observed on conv_4v2b2rewmq6r: both run_yyrcrhw4et4f and its rewake run_vj66cemfx7q4 failed never_started ('agent pi-chat is not registered' burrow-side), yet the conversation stayed 'active' and the split-view chat was empty even though GET /conversations/:id returns the persisted user message (msg seq 1). Operators are left staring at an empty pane with no clue the run failed, no transcript, and no error. This is a pure UI surfacing bug — the data is already on the wire (the persisted transcript and the failed run row); the conversation detail page just never reads it.
sections.reproduction: 1. Open a Leveret conversation whose anchoring run terminated as state=failed with failureReason=never_started (e.g. burrow rejects the runtime / 'agent X is not registered'). 2. Navigate to /leveret/:id (ConversationDetail). Observed: the left 'Conversation' Card renders the Chat surface empty ('No messages yet.') because Chat only consumes useEventStream(runId) and the failed run emitted zero events; no error banner appears even though anchoringRun.data.state === 'failed'. Expected: (a) the persisted transcript returned by GET /conversations/:id (conversation.data.messages, including the seq-1 user message) renders regardless of run state, and (b) a danger banner names the terminal failure (e.g. 'Anchoring run failed — never_started').
sections.root_cause: src/ui/src/components/Chat.tsx derives its message list solely from useEventStream(runId, follow) — it maps streamed RunEvents (kinds user_message / agent_message) into bubbles and has no notion of the persisted transcript. When the anchoring run is terminal-failed (e.g. never_started), the event stream is empty, so messages.length === 0 and the surface shows 'No messages yet.'. Separately, src/ui/src/pages/ConversationDetail.tsx already fetches the anchoring run (anchoringRun query) and computes isAnchoringRunTerminal, but it never distinguishes state==='failed' from a clean 'succeeded' completion and renders no error affordance — and it discards conversation.data.messages entirely, passing only runId to <Chat>.
sections.approach: UI-only fix, no wire/API changes. (1) Teach Chat to accept the already-fetched persisted transcript and render it merged with the live stream, so messages show regardless of run state. (2) In ConversationDetail, feed conversation.data.messages into Chat and add a danger Alert banner when the anchoring run is terminal-failed. Reuse the existing shared Alert component (variant='danger', as RunDetail.tsx already does for failureReason) for consistency. Keep the change to two source files plus one new Chat regression test — no API signatures, deps, or architecture touched.

steps.title: Add persisted-transcript merge to Chat.tsx
Pass conversation transcript into Chat from ConversationDetail
Render terminal-failed banner in ConversationDetail
Add Chat regression test for transcript render with empty stream
Release: run /release per .claude/commands/release.md

acceptance: src/ui/src/components/Chat.tsx accepts a persisted transcript (e.g. a `transcript?: readonly MessageRow[]` prop) and maps rows to ChatMessage (role user->user, assistant->agent; system/tool rows omitted or rendered distinctly), merging them with live stream events and deduping by (kind, content) so an active conversation does not double-render user turns that appear in both the transcript and the event stream.
When the live event stream is empty (e.g. a never_started anchoring run), Chat still renders the persisted transcript bubbles instead of the 'No messages yet.' empty state.
src/ui/src/pages/ConversationDetail.tsx passes conversation.data?.messages into the <Chat> instance so the seq-1 user message renders on a failed conversation.

ConversationDetail renders a danger Alert (reusing src/ui/src/components/ui/alert.tsx, mirroring RunDetail.tsx) above the chat when the anchoring run is terminal with state==='failed', surfacing anchoringRun.data.failureReason (e.g. 'never_started'). No banner shows for a clean state==='succeeded' completion.

A new Chat regression test (src/ui/src/components/Chat.test.tsx) asserts: (a) transcript rows render when the event stream yields no message events, and (b) a transcript row matching a streamed event is not duplicated.

steps.title: Update comments referencing the retired brainstorm/interactive flow
steps.description:
PR #277 (`Retire mode=interactive/brainstorm`) removed the interactive-turn primitive, the `POST /brainstorm` surface, `src/runs/interactive.ts`, `src/runs/reap/interactive.ts`, and the `src/registry/builtins/brainstorm.ts` built-in. Several doc comments still point at those deleted files / describe the retired flow as if current:

  - `src/plots/formalize.ts:19` — cites `src/runs/interactive.ts` for `agent_message` capture (file deleted).
  - `src/plots/formalize.ts:22` — `The brainstorm agent (\`src/registry/builtins/brainstorm.ts\`)` (built-in retired; current builtins are bugwatch/claude-code/leveret/nightwatch/pi/planner/pr-fixer/sapling — no brainstorm.ts).
  - `src/ui/src/pages/plot-detail/interactive-panel.tsx:33` — cites `src/runs/reap/interactive.ts` for reap-side `agent_message` capture (file deleted; the reap-side interactive `appendAgentMessage` path was retired with #277).
  - `src/ui/src/pages/plot-detail/interactive-panel.tsx:63` — cites `src/runs/interactive.ts` for respawn-per-turn (file deleted).

Fix: update each comment to describe the current state — either repoint to where the equivalent logic now lives (the conversation/leveret path) or drop the dead `src/...` pointer and the retired-flow rationale. Keep this strictly comment-only: do NOT alter `INTERACTIVE_AGENT_NAMES` or any runtime behavior in this step (the planner prompt's `**brainstorm**` wording in `src/registry/builtins/planner.ts` is a separate concern — leave it). Confirm the four edited comments no longer reference any nonexistent `src/...` path, and that lint/typecheck/test stay green.

sections.context: Code-patrol scan of the warren repo on 2026-06-10. Quality gates are green (bun test 2632 pass, biome lint clean, tsc clean, file-size/debt-marker/gen:docs/gen:openapi guards all ok). The scan surfaced no logic bugs, type-safety holes, dead code, or security issues, but it did find documentation that now contradicts the code it describes (comment drift from features that have since landed) plus one cross-call-site error-message-style inconsistency. These are comment/string-only fixes that keep the codebase's heavily-documented modules honest — the same class of drift earlier nightwatch patrols (pl-7580) cleaned up. Each finding is independent and lands as its own small PR.
sections.behavior_invariant: No runtime behavior changes. All edits are to doc comments or to user-facing validation error strings (with their corresponding test assertions updated in lockstep). sections.approach: One step per finding, ordered independents-first. Steps 1-3 are pure comment fixes (zero test impact). Step 4 harmonizes validation error-message phrasing across handler call sites and must update the exact-string assertions in the adjacent *.test.ts files in the same PR. There are no real dependencies among the four fix steps, so they may land in any order as separate PRs; each blocks only the final Release step, which is ordered last.

steps.title: Fix stale 'latent' NOTE in src/runs/analytics/insights.ts
steps.description: src/runs/analytics/insights.ts lines ~26-32 carry a NOTE claiming the `steering-anomaly` / `pause-anomaly` callouts are latent: 'no production code currently does so — the `GET /analytics/behavior` handler calls `buildInsights` without `steering`, so these two kinds never appear in the live endpoint's response today.' This contradicts the code: src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts:209-213 now builds `steering` via `buildSteeringSignals(steeringRows, rows.length)` and calls `buildInsights({ metrics, mining, steering })`, so both callouts are live. Rewrite the NOTE to describe the current wiring (the handler fetches steering/pause events via `EventsRepo.listSteeringAndPauseEventsForRuns`, builds a SteeringSignals bundle, and passes it through) and drop the 'latent / no production caller' framing. Comment-only change; no tests affected.

steps.title: Repoint stale 'Postgres schema not yet wired' comments after dialect-aware openDatabase landed
steps.description: The dialect-aware `openDatabase` (warren-a66e, the 'step 3' those comments forward-reference) has landed: src/db/client.ts:124-131 routes a postgres URL to `openPostgres`, which calls `drizzlePg(pool, { schema: pgSchema })` (line ~185), so the Postgres schema IS now wired into the runtime for the postgres dialect. Update the stale header comments that still claim otherwise: (a) src/db/schema/postgres.ts lines ~19-22 ('This schema is not yet wired into `openDatabase` ... Until then this file is build-only and exercised by the drift test.'); (b) src/db/schema/columns.ts lines ~14-15 ('Step 3 (warren-a66e) adds dialect-aware `openDatabase`; until then, the Postgres tables exist but are unused at runtime.'). While here, sanity-check the related framing in src/db/schema.ts lines ~13-16 ('lit up by step 3' / 'until then the SQLite objects ARE the runtime') and adjust the 'until then' clause to reflect that postgres is now a selectable runtime dialect. Comment-only change; the drift test still guards parity, no test edits expected.

steps.title: Fix 'four dedicated mutators' miscount in src/plot-client/types.ts
steps.description: src/plot-client/types.ts, the doc comment on `AgentAllowedEventType` (lines ~39-46), reads: 'The four dedicated mutators (`editIntent`, `setStatus`, `detach`, plus `question_answered` appends) live only on `UserPlotHandle`'. That miscounts: there are THREE dedicated mutators (editIntent, setStatus, detach) plus one shared append path (question_answered) — not four mutators. This contradicts the sibling file src/plot-client/handle.ts lines ~8-13, which correctly states 'the first three because their dedicated mutators (`editIntent`, `setStatus`, `detach`) ... and the fourth because `append`'s generic parameter excludes it.' Reword the types.ts comment to say 'three dedicated mutators (`editIntent`, `setStatus`, `detach`) plus the shared `question_answered` append path' so the two files agree. Comment-only change.

steps.title: Harmonize 'expected one of' vs 'must be one of ...; got' validation error phrasing across handlers
steps.description: Enum-validation error messages use two divergent styles across handler call sites for the same kind of failure. The 'must be one of <list>; got '<raw>'' form is used in src/server/handlers/burrows.ts:33,42, src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts:56, and src/server/handlers/plots/attachments.ts:250 (merge_method). The 'expected one of <list>' form (no offending-value suffix) is used in src/server/handlers/plots/list.ts:50, src/server/handlers/plots/status.ts:68, and src/server/handlers/plots/attachments.ts:102. Standardize on the more informative '<field> must be one of <list>; got '<raw>'' form (it echoes the rejected value) for these enum-membership rejections, leaving the field-key 'is not recognized; expected one of ...' messages in plots/intent.ts and plots/list.ts alone (different failure: unrecognized key, not bad enum value). Update the exact-string assertions in the adjacent test files (plots/list.test.ts, plots/status.test.ts, plots/attachments.test.ts) in the same PR so the suite stays green. Scope is wording-only on already-thrown ValidationErrors — no status codes, error `code` values, or control flow change.

sections.context: LEVERET.md §0 phases 1, 2, 4, 5, 6 are shipped (burrow pi-chat runtime, conversations/messages store + lifetime exemptions, conversation API + UI, send-off + merge poller code, interactive retirement). The broken core is phase 3: no conversation stream bridge exists (warren-ce65), so propose_intent emissions land as opaque events, the right-pane intent never live-updates, and send-off is gated on hand-typed intent. The ../plot ACL still has EVENT_ACL.intent_edited = ["user"] (plot/src/acl.ts:16), blocking agent-actor intent writes even once the bridge exists. Assistant turns are never persisted to messages (only user turns, src/server/handlers/conversations.ts:156,235), so re-wake replays a user-only transcript. The merge poller is opt-in (WARREN_MERGE_POLLER_ENABLED) so merged send-off PRs do nothing by default. The seeded propose_intent extension (typebox + pi-coding-agent imports in src/registry/builtins/leveret.ts:81-82) has never been proven to load under pi's jiti inside the sandbox. Operator approved widening the plot ACL per LEVERET.md §0.6 on 2026-06-10.
sections.approach: The existing Leveret v1 plan pl-d2d9 already holds the bridge (warren-ce65, its step 9) and the acceptance scenario (warren-9f47) as its only open children, and warren-5e53 lives in pl-247b — re-dispatching those plans resumes exactly there. This plan therefore carries only the NET-NEW work the audit surfaced that no plan tracks: (1) the cross-repo ../plot ACL widening that gates the bridge, (2) persisting assistant turns to messages so re-wake replay carries both sides of the transcript, (3) deployment defaults (merge poller on by default, autoOpenPr token error surfacing, burrow-cli >= 0.3.12 image note). Cross-plan ordering is wired via sd dep: warren-ce65 depends on the ACL child here. Sequence to a working Leveret: run this plan's step 1, then resume pl-d2d9 (bridge + acceptance), with steps 2-3 here landable in parallel. The bridge work itself follows LEVERET.md §0.0.E (propose_intent details ride tool_execution_end, not message_end).

sections.context: Audit (2026-06-10) found warren's logging hygiene is good (pino, no stray console.*, X-Request-ID child loggers on HTTP) but coverage has specific holes that make real operator questions unanswerable: src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts has zero log statements and its rollback swallows finalize/destroy failures with bare catch {} — a run that dies at spawn shows cancelled with no failure_reason, no system event, and no log line; there is no HTTP access log and auth denials are returned silently (cannot see traffic, error rates, or token guessing); warren-af76: the bridge reconnect loop spins forever on burrow socket timeouts without finalizing the run; run-lifecycle code uses an optional-logger pattern (input.logger?.info?.()) so a missed wiring silently drops a subsystem's logs; runId is hand-threaded into log objects instead of bound once via child loggers; docker-compose.yml sets no logging driver options so container logs grow unbounded. Note: cost/token data is NOT a gap — claude/pi usage is already parsed and persisted to runs.cost_usd / tokens_* (src/runs/usage-aggregate.ts, stats.ts).
sections.approach: Quick wins first (spawn instrumentation + durable spawn_failed trail, access/auth-denial logging, log rotation, the af76 correctness fix), then the structural pass (per-run child loggers, non-optional loggers, naming convention) that prevents the same class of gap recurring. Persisting spawn failures mirrors the existing reap_failed system-event pattern (src/runs/reap/run.ts:64-69) so the UI surfaces them with no UI work.

alternatives.name: Adopt OpenTelemetry tracing now
alternatives.rejected_because: Heavyweight for a single-process control plane; structured pino with bound run_id/request_id answers the actual operator questions, and OTel can layer on later

alternatives.name: Add a /metrics Prometheus endpoint in this pass
alternatives.rejected_because: Deferred: the data lives in SQLite and a periodic stats log line covers the home-server case; a metrics endpoint is a follow-up if a real scraper appears

steps.title: Instrument spawnRun (src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts): log placement result, provision + dispatch success and latency, and every rollback branch including the currently-swallowed runs.finalize and burrow-destroy failures, carrying run_id and the caller's request_id

Persist spawn failures durably: emit a spawn_failed system event into the events table and set runs.failure_reason instead of a bare cancelled row, mirroring the reap_failed pattern so RunDetail shows the cause for free

HTTP access log + auth-denial logging in src/server/server.ts handleRequest: one info line per request (method, path, status, duration_ms; request_id already bound) and a warn on every denyResponse; add docker-compose json-file logging driver max-size/max-file rotation

Structural logger pass: bind logger.child({run_id, burrow_run_id, worker}) once in bridge/reap/detector entry points instead of hand-threading fields; make loggers non-optional in run-lifecycle inputs (required narrow logger + noop default); standardize on the dotted subsystem.action event-name convention repo-wide

Defense and visibility: pino redact config for token-shaped fields (GITHUB_TOKEN, bearer values); periodic operational stats log line (runs by state, active bridges, tick durations, cost aggregates) from data already in SQLite

risks: Access logging on the NDJSON streaming endpoints must log at response-start or completion without buffering the stream
Making loggers non-optional touches many call sites and test fixtures at once; the noop default keeps tests quiet but must not mask the new required wiring in production paths
warren-af76 is a correctness fix in the bridge reconnect path — the failure mode (burrow socket timeout vs burrow run genuinely missing) must be distinguished carefully to avoid finalizing live runs
acceptance: A run that fails at spawn shows a spawn_failed system event and a failure_reason in the API/UI, and the log line carrying its run_id and request_id is greppable
Every HTTP request produces exactly one access-log line including status and duration; bad-token requests produce a warn
A burrow socket-timeout during a bridge no longer loops forever: the run reaches a terminal state with a logged resolution trail (warren-af76 closed)
All run-lifecycle log lines carry run_id via child loggers; grep by run_id reconstructs the full lifecycle of any run
docker compose logs are rotation-bounded
bun run check:all passes

sections.context: The operator drives serial plan execution today with os-eco/scripts/run-plan.sh (local claude -p per open child of an sd plan, human-readable .log + raw .jsonl artifacts). Warren's server already has the full surface to replace it in the cloud: POST /plan-runs walks a seeds plan's children serially gated on PR merge, GET /plan-runs/:id returns planRun+children+runs in one round trip, POST /plan-runs/:id/cancel exists, and GET /plan-runs/:id/events?follow=1 is an NDJSON union stream of all children that picks up newly dispatched children mid-stream and carries plan_run.* lifecycle events. A typed WarrenClient SDK already ships in src/client/ (WARREN_BASE_URL + WARREN_API_TOKEN, bearer auth, NDJSON streaming for per-run events) but is missing cancelPlanRun and streamPlanRunEvents, and no CLI command uses it — every existing command opens the DB directly via withCliDb. Zero server work is needed.
sections.approach: Extend WarrenClient with the two missing plan-run methods (sharing the existing NDJSON reader with streamRunEvents) plus a waitForPlanRun mirroring waitForRun, then add a `warren plan run <plan-id>` command under a new `plan` subcommand group (pattern: existing config/db groups) as the first thin-HTTP-client CLI command: probe() for a friendly unreachable error, POST the plan-run, tail the union stream, and exit with the terminal state code. Ship two output modes: raw NDJSON (matching warren run's contract) and a human-readable renderer porting run-plan.sh's jq event filter so tail -f muscle memory transfers. Resume semantics come free from the server (re-POST skips closed children).

alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected by the operator: thin client over HTTP only

alternatives.rejected_because: Deferred: the mandatory PR-merge gate is the operator's existing taste-gate formalized; revisit only if merge ceremony proves too heavy in practice

alternatives.rejected_because: The server already speaks NDJSON and the client reader exists

New CLI command src/cli/commands/plan-run.ts + `plan` subcommand group in src/cli/main.ts: warren plan run <plan-id> --project <prj_id> --agent <name> [--prompt-template --ref --provider --model --plot --no-follow] built on WarrenClient.fromEnv (first command without withCliDb); probe first, POST, print {planRun, children} summary, tail events, map terminal state to exit code (succeeded=0 else 1); SIGINT stops tailing without cancelling, second SIGINT exits (mirroring warren run), explicit `warren plan cancel <id>` for cancellation

Round out the surface: warren plan status <id> (one-shot GET rendering child-state table with cost/duration per child from runs rows) and warren plan list [--project --state]; README Client SDK + CLI docs updates; command tests

acceptance: warren plan run <pl-id> --project <prj> --agent claude-code against a remote warren dispatches the plan-run and live-tails all children's events on one connection, exiting 0 on success and 1 on failure or cancellation
Re-running the same command after a failure resumes from the next open child (server re-POST semantics verified end-to-end)
--output pretty renders a human log equivalent to run-plan.sh's .log format including plan-level lifecycle lines
warren plan status and warren plan list render child states; warren plan cancel cancels an in-flight plan-run

sections.context: The operator runs agents at the root of ~/Projects/kota-monorepo (many intertwined projects, one git repo) more often than inside individual projects. Investigation (2026-06-10) found warren supports this today with zero code changes: a project is one repo, burrow materializes workspaces as git worktrees of warren's host clone, agents run at repo root, and one branch/one PR per run is the natural monorepo shape. Opt-in features light up from root-level .seeds/, .mulch/, .plot/, .warren/. The rough edges are coarseness, not blockers: feature detection probes the clone root only (src/projects/refresh.ts:73-81), there is no sparse/partial-clone support (full checkout per concurrent run), one preview config and one pr-template for the whole repo, and git-hooks arming reads only the root package.json. True multi-repo burrow workspaces were sized at several weeks across burrow SPEC + dispatch + reap + plan-run PR gating and deliberately deferred; ROADMAP R-20 Colonies covers cross-repo policy grouping without joint workspaces.
sections.approach: Onboard kota-monorepo as a single warren project now and validate the full loop (dispatch, plan-run, PR) against it, then land the cheap coarseness fixes only as pain is proven: partial clone + sparse-checkout first if checkout time/disk bites, and an R-20 colonies decision spike for the genuinely separate os-eco repos. Explicitly do not build multi-repo workspaces in this arc.

alternatives.name: True multi-repo burrow workspaces (N clones per sandbox)
alternatives.rejected_because: Deferred: several weeks across the most failure-sensitive paths (burrow SPEC, dispatch, reap, plan-run PR gating), and the monorepo path removes the primary motivation

alternatives.name: Splitting kota-monorepo packages into separate warren projects
alternatives.rejected_because: The projects are closely intertwined and the operator's working habit is monorepo-root runs

steps.title: Onboard kota-monorepo: add as a warren project, place .warren/config.yaml (defaultRole, defaultPrompt, runBranchPrefix) plus .seeds/.mulch/.plot/ at the repo root, dispatch a smoke run and a small plan-run end-to-end, and record the validated setup + any friction as mulch records

Measure and decide on sparse/partial clone: capture clone + per-run worktree checkout time and disk for kota-monorepo under concurrent runs; if it bites, implement --filter=blob:none on warren's clone (src/projects/clone.ts, refresh.ts) and a per-project sparsePaths burrow applies after worktree add (burrow src/provider/local/workspace.ts + sandbox binds); if it does not bite, close with the measurements recorded

R-20 Colonies decision spike for os-eco's separate repos: evaluate the ROADMAP sketch (colonies/colony_members tables, shared scheduling, aggregate dashboard, colony-level agents) against actual cross-repo needs observed after the monorepo + plan-run CLI workflows settle; outcome is a go/no-go note on the roadmap item, not code

risks: kota-monorepo's on-disk size is unverified — if very large, full checkouts per concurrent run could hurt before step 2's measurements land
Root-level .seeds/ means all packages share one issue queue and one PR stream; acceptable by design but per-package scoping pressure may emerge
Sparse-checkout in burrow touches the sandbox bind set and worktree lifecycle — needs burrow-side review against ../burrow/SPEC.md before implementation
acceptance: kota-monorepo is a registered warren project and a plan-run executed against it end-to-end (dispatch, child PRs, merge-gated advancement)
A documented measurement of clone/checkout cost exists with an explicit go/no-go on sparse support
R-20 has a recorded decision note
Any code changes pass bun run check:all (and burrow's gates if sparse lands)

sections.context: warren is the os-eco reference L5 repo and originated the check:ci-parity gate, but its check:all is a 12-gate && chain using verbose names (check:file-sizes, check:debt-markers, check:duplicates, validate:agents-md) that diverge from the canonical terse vocabulary frozen in docs/check-all-standard.md (os-eco-9048) and shipped as the portable runner in templates/l5-toolkit/scripts (os-eco-5db7). warren has no quiet runner (it chains with &&) and no `verify` alias. Conforming warren makes the reference repo match the standard it anchors. Depends on root tracker pl-760e steps 1-2.
sections.approach: Rename warren's verbose gate keys to canonical, swap the && chain for the byte-identical quiet runner, and refactor warren's existing check-ci-parity.ts to import the shared GATES manifest. Patrol scan of 2026-06-12 found one coherent cross-call-site inconsistency: warren parses "is this env flag truthy" (default-off flags) at least five different ways with divergent accepted-token sets and case handling, so the same conceptual flag behaves differently depending on which subsystem reads it.

Default-OFF (truthy) parsers, today:
- src/server/probe.ts:75 — inline `disabledRaw === "1" || disabledRaw === "true"` for WARREN_WORKER_PROBE_DISABLED. Case-sensitive, no trim, accepts only 1/true. `=TRUE`, `=Yes`, `=on` are silently ignored.
- src/server/config.ts:128 — inline `disabled === "1" || disabled === "true"` for WARREN_DISABLE_UI. Case-sensitive, accepts only 1/true (the doc comment at config.ts:20 even says "'1'/'true' to disable"), so `=on`/`=yes`/`=TRUE` are ignored.
- src/supervisor/main.ts:382 `parseBoolEnv` — `raw === "1" || raw.toLowerCase() === "true"` for WARREN_BURROW_NO_AUTH (controls burrow `--no-auth`). Lowercases only `true`, accepts 1/true, not yes/on.
- src/server/main/utils.ts:80 `parseTrueEnv` — trim+lowercase, accepts 1/true/yes (NOT on). Used by detector/poller/idle flags.
- src/preview/eviction/config.ts:74 and src/runs/reap/gc.ts:107 `isTruthy` (byte-identical) — trim+lowercase, accepts 1/true/yes/on.

By contrast the default-ON (falsy/opt-out) parsers already agree on one set — `0/false/no/off` — across src/triggers/config.ts:63, src/plan-runs/config.ts:77, and src/runs/pr.ts:387. The truthy side should reach the same internal consistency. The canonical target token set is `1/true/yes/on`, trimmed and case-insensitive (the broadest existing behavior, symmetric with the falsy `0/false/no/off`).

This is a correctness/consistency finding, not new behavior: an operator setting WARREN_WORKER_PROBE_DISABLED=on or WARREN_DISABLE_UI=TRUE today gets surprising no-ops. No public API signature changes; no new module is required (parseTrueEnv already exists as the reference implementation).
sections.behavior_invariant: Every truthy env-var parse keeps its existing default (absent or empty value => false) and keeps accepting the values it accepts today: `1` and `true` must remain truthy at every call site. The HTTP query-param boolean parser `parseBoolean` in src/server/handlers/index.ts (which intentionally rejects unknown values rather than coercing) is OUT of scope and must NOT change. The default-ON opt-out parsers (triggers/config.ts, plan-runs/config.ts, runs/pr.ts) must NOT change. No route, response shape, or public function signature changes. The only observable difference is that previously-ignored truthy spellings (case variants, surrounding whitespace, and the `yes`/`on` tokens) are now honored uniformly.
sections.approach: Converge all default-OFF truthy env parsers on a single accepted token set — `1`, `true`, `yes`, `on` — compared after `.trim().toLowerCase()`, matching the existing `isTruthy` in eviction/config.ts and reap/gc.ts and symmetric with the falsy `0/false/no/off` set. Use the already-exported `parseTrueEnv` (src/server/main/utils.ts) as the canonical reference: extend it to also accept `on`, then route the divergent inline parsers through the same token logic. Keep changes minimal and local — do not introduce a new shared module or change any signatures; where a call site cannot cleanly import the canonical helper (e.g. the supervisor, which crosses the warren↔burrow boundary), harmonize its inline token set in place. Split the supervisor change into its own step because WARREN_BURROW_NO_AUTH gates burrow's `--no-auth` and lives across the warren↔burrow boundary that AGENTS.md flags for extra review.

sections.context: The scheduler (`src/triggers/config.ts`) and plan-run coordinator (`src/plan-runs/config.ts`) both parse their default-OFF kill switches (`WARREN_SCHEDULER_DISABLED`, `WARREN_PLAN_RUN_DISABLED`) through a local `parseBoolFlag` that uses *deny-list* semantics: `return !['0','false','no','off'].includes(normalized)`. That means ANY unrecognized non-empty value (`2`, `enabled`, `disable`, `garbage`) parses as `true` and disables the subsystem. But the JSDoc env contracts above each loader explicitly promise the *allow-list* set — triggers/config.ts:6 says 'accepts the standard warren truthy set ("1"/"true"/"yes"/"on")' and plan-runs/config.ts:9 says 'same truthy set as WARREN_SCHEDULER_DISABLED ("1"/"true"/"yes"/"on", case-insensitive)'. So the implementation contradicts its own documented contract (doc drift) and silently treats typos/garbage as 'disable', which is the opposite of the fail-safe intent for a default-OFF flag. PR #340 (commit d7d0002d) harmonized the rest of warren's default-OFF flags onto the allow-list `parseTrueEnv`/`isTruthy` form (`raw === '1' || 'true' || 'yes' || 'on'`, see src/server/main/utils.ts:80, src/preview/eviction/config.ts:71, src/runs/reap/gc.ts:104) but these two `parseBoolFlag` copies were missed. The misleading inline comment 'Mirror the truthy set used by WARREN_AUTO_OPEN_PR (mx-b82711)' is the root cause: WARREN_AUTO_OPEN_PR (src/runs/pr.ts:368 `isFalsy`) is a default-ON flag whose opt-out deny-list semantics are correct for IT, but copying that posture to a default-OFF flag inverts the intent. The existing tests (src/triggers/config.test.ts:34-48) only assert the in-set truthy values and the explicit falsy values, never an out-of-set value, so the drift is uncovered.
sections.behavior_invariant: Recognized values keep their current meaning: `WARREN_SCHEDULER_DISABLED` and `WARREN_PLAN_RUN_DISABLED` set to any of `1`/`true`/`yes`/`on` (case-insensitive, surrounding whitespace tolerated) MUST still resolve `disabled: true`, and unset/empty/`0`/`false`/`no`/`off` MUST still resolve `disabled: false`. The only change is that previously-accepted out-of-set garbage values (e.g. `2`, `enabled`, `disable`) now resolve `disabled: false` (default-OFF, fail-safe) instead of `true`, matching the documented contract. Tick-ms parsing, sd-binary handling, and merge-timeout parsing are untouched.
sections.approach: Replace the deny-list body of `parseBoolFlag` in both files with the allow-list form already used by `parseTrueEnv` (`src/server/main/utils.ts:80`): `const t = raw.trim().toLowerCase(); return t === '1' || t === 'true' || t === 'yes' || t === 'on';` (keeping the `undefined`/empty early-outs). Update the inline `// Mirror the truthy set used by WARREN_AUTO_OPEN_PR (mx-b82711)` comment so it no longer points at the default-ON deny-list flag — instead note these are default-OFF opt-in flags sharing the canonical allow-list set from PR #340. Do NOT introduce a new shared abstraction or move the helper across module boundaries (out of scope); keep the change local to each file's existing `parseBoolFlag`. Add regression tests covering an out-of-set value. Keep the two files as independent PRs.

sections.context: Phase 2 of audit population (decision mx-1e041c). The three constitution auditors already run as cron triggers in .warren/triggers.yaml (gatewatch + ratchetwatch mechanical, tastewatch report-only) and file findings as seeds, but nothing synthesizes across them: there is no standing place where findings accumulate, get triaged, and turn into plans. warren-d0ed closes that gap with a Leveret warden — a single long-lived `mode:"conversation"` run bound to a dedicated meta-Plot that ingests findings over the EXISTING POST /conversations/:id/messages steering channel (already 202 today, src/server/handlers/conversations.ts postConversationMessageHandler), synthesizes a weekly digest, and proposes plans through the proven send-off->planner chain (sendOffConversationHandler -> conversation-merge-poller -> conversation-merge-dispatch). This is a deliberately THIN first slice: one standing conversation + weekly digest + plan proposals. Auditor-autonomy-promotion recommendations (from tastewatch's precision table) are explicitly deferred to a tracked follow-up. The whole slice is GATED on the Leveret repair arc (warren-87fe / pl-afed + the bridge warren-ce65 in pl-d2d9): live agent-authored intent (warren-ce65 bridge + warren-df1b plot ACL widening) and a default-on send-off->planner loop (warren-157a merge-poller default) must be working before warden findings can produce real plans. Because those repair-arc seeds are owned by other plans, this plan does not re-create or mutate them; it encodes the gate as a precondition in step 1 and in the acceptance criteria.
sections.approach: Reuse every existing primitive; add no new endpoint or dispatch path. (1) Bootstrap ONE standing meta-Plot and ONE standing Leveret conversation bound to it, created idempotently and resolvable by a stable, well-known identifier (a warren-config knob / well-known title) so other surfaces can find 'the warden conversation' deterministically. (2) Teach the three existing auditor cron procedures to deliver each finding to that conversation over POST /conversations/:id/messages (the 202 steering channel) — a prompt/agent-definition change, not a new code path. (3) Add a warden-digest cron trigger (reusing the existing kind:cron mechanism) that posts a 'synthesize the weekly digest' message to the standing conversation, so Leveret triages the week's accumulated findings and proposes at least one plan via the existing send-off->planner chain. (4) Prove the full loop with a deterministic acceptance scenario. (5) Close out the thin slice: file the deferred autonomy-promotion follow-up, document the warden boundary, and verify warren-d0ed's thin-slice acceptance. Chosen over a bespoke warden endpoint/daemon because the intent's constraints pin reuse of POST /conversations/:id/messages and forbid any new ingestion or dispatch primitive; the standing-conversation model also gives the digest a persistent transcript to triage instead of a per-finding fan-out.

name: Leveret warden — standing audit-triage conversation (thin slice)

sections.context: Warren ships two top-level operator surfaces that are facets of the same object: Leveret (conversations list + /leveret/:id split-view) and Plots (list + /plots/:id three-panel detail + /plots/:id/summary). The data model already makes the Plot the durable spine and the conversation an ephemeral child of it: a conversation is bound to exactly one Plot, send-off CLOSES the conversation, and re-planning spawns a NEW conversation on the SAME Plot. On top of the redundancy, the Plot surface still renders a fully RETIRED intent-shaping path next to the live one: warren-d622 removed mode=interactive (RUN_MODES is now [batch, conversation]) and the POST /brainstorm route, yet the Plots page still shows a 'Start brainstorming' button (plotsApi.startBrainstorm -> dead POST /brainstorm) and PlotDetail still renders InteractivePanel (runsApi.createInteractive with mode:interactive, which the schema rejects) plus an orphaned Formalize (POST /plots/:id/formalize summarizing a brainstorm conversation nothing can create). Operators cannot walk one coherent flow; they bounce between /leveret/:id and /plots/:id and trip over dead buttons. This collapses both surfaces into a single cross-project Workspace and sweeps the dead brainstorm/interactive/formalize code, which also gives R-20 (colony / multi-repo) a natural top-level home to grow into.
sections.approach: Make the Plot the spine and the conversation a facet of it. Introduce one 'Workspace' top-level section: a single cross-project list (one row per Plot, with an active-conversation indicator) and one tabbed detail page (/workspace/:id) that walks the operator's own four-step mental model as tabs — Shape (brainstorm with Leveret: chat + dynamic intent editor + send-off), Plan (convert into plan: planner run + link out to the sd plan + sign-off gate + dispatch), Run (dispatch plan-run: children + PR-merge status + Plot auto-done), and Activity (event log + substrate + summary + past conversations). Reuse the existing sub-component trees verbatim (conversation-detail/* for Shape, plot-detail/* minus InteractivePanel for the rest, dispatch-plan-dialog for Plan, PlanRunDetail content for Run) so this is a re-composition, not a rewrite. Sweep the retired surface in the same arc: delete Formalize end to end, delete the dead UI panels, and remove the dead client methods. Old routes redirect into Workspace so no bookmark/link breaks. Sequenced server-cleanup-first so the UI client sweep compiles against an already-clean server, then list -> shell -> four tabs -> nav/routing collapse -> acceptance -> docs. Chosen over a Plot-centric merge that keeps 'Leveret' as a noun (rejected: conversation is ephemeral, a poor spine) and over a conversation-centric workspace (rejected: a Plot has N conversations over its life).

alternatives.rejected_because: Send-off closes the conversation and re-plan spawns a new one on the same Plot, so a Plot has 1..N conversations over its life — the conversation is a poor durable spine.

alternatives.rejected_because: Leaves the core complaint (two intertwined surfaces, no single walkable flow) unsolved.

alternatives.rejected_because: Operator decision — Leveret already shapes intent live via propose_intent, so a separate summarize-then-apply step is redundant.

alternatives.rejected_because: Operator decision — after intent is shaped, talking to Leveret does nothing, so phase tabs that go quiet/read-only model the lifecycle better than one long scroll.

steps.title: Server sweep — remove the orphaned Formalize endpoint. Delete POST /plots/:id/formalize from ROUTE_TABLE (src/server/handlers/index.ts), the formalizePlotHandler + brainstorm-summarize logic in src/server/handlers/plots/workbench.ts, and src/server/handlers/plots.workbench.formalize.test.ts. Regenerate docs/http-api.md (bun run gen:docs) and docs/openapi.yaml (bun run gen:openapi). Verify no remaining server caller references formalize.

Server sweep — remove residual mode=interactive / brainstorm dispatch remnants left after warren-d622. Audit src/server/handlers/runs/ (parseRunMode + createRunHandler) and src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts for any mode:'interactive' / interactiveAgent handling and the 'brainstorm' interactive built-in remnants; remove dead branches while PRESERVING the 'planner' interactive agent and mode:'conversation'. Remove the vestigial interactiveAgents.brainstormRuntime knob from src/warren-config/schema.ts only if it is unreferenced after the sweep. Update or trim affected tests.

UI API-client sweep — remove the dead client methods and types: plotsApi.startBrainstorm (+ StartBrainstormInput/Response), runsApi.createInteractive, and plotsApi.formalize (+ formalize request/response types) from src/ui/src/api/client.ts and src/ui/src/api/types.ts. Fix every TypeScript reference so bun run typecheck and the src/ui tsc both pass.

Delete the dead UI panels. Remove src/ui/src/pages/plot-detail/interactive-panel.tsx and its usage in PlotDetail.tsx (InteractivePanel — Start brainstorming / Run planner / Formalize, all built on retired mode=interactive). Remove StartBrainstormDialog + the 'Start brainstorming' button from src/ui/src/pages/Plots.tsx. KEEP all still-live plot-detail/ sub-components (intent-panel, substrate-panel, activity-feed, header-controls, run-plan, batch-dispatch). Update affected component tests.

Build the Workspace list page. Add src/ui/src/pages/Workspace.tsx at a new /workspace route: a single cross-project list with one row per Plot (the durable spine), merging today's Plots list and Leveret conversations list. Columns: name, project, status/phase, intent preview, active-conversation indicator, needs-you reasons, last activity. Reuse the Plots server ?status/?filter chip contract. Actions: New Plot (existing dialog) and Start conversation (existing NewConversationButton). Backed by plotsApi.list joined with conversationsApi.list.

Build the Workspace detail shell. Add src/ui/src/pages/WorkspaceDetail.tsx at /workspace/:id (keyed by plotId): a persistent header (PlotNameEditor, StatusTransitionControl, PlotSyncButton, project link, summary link) plus tab navigation Shape / Plan / Run / Activity with tab state in a ?tab= query param. Wire empty tab-panel child components to be filled by steps 7-10. Load the plot via plotsApi.get and reuse the existing 404/refresh-projects CTA.

Implement the Shape tab. Port the live Leveret conversation surface into Shape: the streamed Chat (sendMessage override -> POST /conversations/:id/messages) on the left and the dynamic intent editor (fieldsFromIntent / patchFromFields) on the right, plus RewakeButton and the SendOff action — reusing the conversation-detail/ sub-components. Resolve the Plot's active conversation via conversationsApi.list({plot}); when none is active, render a Start-conversation affordance. After send-off the tab goes read-only/quiet.

Implement the Plan tab (minimal). Once the merge-poller stamps conversation.plannerRunId, show the planner run status and a link out to the generated sd plan, then an operator Sign-off gate that enables the existing DispatchPlanButton (conversation-detail/dispatch-plan-dialog.tsx). No new inline plan renderer — link to the plan and dispatch over the existing /plan-runs path.

Implement the Run tab. Embed plan-run execution for the dispatched plan: children list + per-child PR-merge status + terminal state, reusing the PlanRunDetail content, and surface the Plot's auto-done transition when the final child merges (SPEC §11.P.Plot). Resolve the plan-run from the dispatched plot/plan.

Implement the Activity tab. Move the Plot event-log ActivityFeed (plot-detail/activity-feed.tsx) and the SubstratePanel (attachments) into the Activity tab, plus a link to the read-only Plot summary. Past/closed conversations for the Plot surface here as history entries so the full lifecycle is visible from one place.

Collapse nav + routing. Replace the 'Leveret' and 'Plots' sidebar entries in src/ui/src/components/Layout.tsx with a single 'Workspace' entry and move the needs-you badge onto it. Register /workspace + /workspace/:id; add redirects /plots -> /workspace, /plots/:id -> /workspace/:id, /leveret -> /workspace, and /leveret/:id -> resolve conversation.plotId then redirect to /workspace/:plotId?tab=shape. Delete the now-unused page shells Leveret.tsx, Plots.tsx, ConversationDetail.tsx, PlotDetail.tsx (keeping their reused sub-component trees). Update the router.

Update acceptance + UI tests for the Workspace flow. Adapt scenario 33 (scripts/acceptance/scenarios/33-leveret-conversation-loop.ts) and any UI tests referencing the old /leveret + /plots routes/pages to the new Workspace surface; keep the scenario deterministic, idempotent, and self-cleaning. Assert the full walk: list -> Shape (conversation + intent) -> send-off -> Plan (planner + dispatch) -> Run.

Docs, gates, and bundle re-baseline. Update README + SPEC §11.O/§11.P UI references + LEVERET.md to describe the single Workspace surface and the removed brainstorm/formalize path; regen docs/http-api.md + docs/openapi.yaml; re-baseline bundle budgets (bun run check:bundle-size --update); get bun run check:all green. File a follow-up seed for the R-20 colony/multi-repo tier layered on top of Workspace.

risks: Route-redirect fragility: /leveret/:id is keyed by conversation id, not plot id, so the redirect must resolve conversation.plotId before sending the user to /workspace/:plotId — a naive id passthrough 404s. Covered in step 11.

Reused sub-component coupling: deleting the four page shells (step 11) while steps 7-10 still import their sub-trees (conversation-detail/*, plot-detail/*) risks breaking imports — keep the sub-component directories, only delete the page-level shells.

Server sweep over-reach: the 'planner' agent and mode:'conversation' must survive the interactive/brainstorm removal in step 2; an over-broad delete would break send-off -> planner. Preserve planner explicitly.
Bundle-size ratchet: a re-composition that changes chunking can trip check:bundle-size; re-baseline with the canonical --update (step 13), never hand-edit the budget JSON.
Plot 404-after-commit: the existing refresh-projects CTA must be carried into WorkspaceDetail (step 6) or freshly-committed Plots look broken.
acceptance: A single 'Workspace' top-level nav entry replaces both 'Leveret' and 'Plots'; the needs-you badge renders on it; /plots, /plots/:id, /leveret, and /leveret/:id all redirect into the Workspace surface without 404s.
/workspace shows one cross-project list keyed one-row-per-Plot with an active-conversation indicator; New Plot and Start conversation both work from it.

/workspace/:id presents Shape / Plan / Run / Activity tabs that walk the full flow: shape intent with Leveret, send off, review + sign off + dispatch the plan, watch the plan-run execute, and read activity/summary — all without leaving the page.

The retired surface is gone end to end: POST /plots/:id/formalize, InteractivePanel, StartBrainstormDialog, plotsApi.startBrainstorm, runsApi.createInteractive, and plotsApi.formalize no longer exist; no dead button reaches a removed endpoint.

bun run check:all passes (lint, typecheck, check:agents, dups, deps, size, debt, bundle-size, gen:docs:check, gen:openapi:check, coverage, ci-parity) and the updated acceptance scenario asserts the end-to-end Workspace walk.
A follow-up seed is filed for the R-20 colony / multi-repo tier on top of Workspace.
