sections.context: Plot plot-b11c5999 ("Workspaces Testing") finalized a low-risk cleanup batch capped by a 0.9.1 patch bump. Its goal names four deliverable areas: (1) the full logging/traceability hardening set, (2) workspace chat surface fixes — out-of-order turns, duplicated assistant messages, and unbounded page growth, (3) removal of the leaked .pi/sessions agent transcript from PR #340, and (4) the version bump. Area (1) is already an approved, decomposed plan: pl-f700 (parent warren-3679) with six child seeds c686 → fc6e → af76 → 26c2 → 9f06 → b2dd. A seed can only belong to one plan (plan_id is single-valued), so this plan does NOT re-adopt those six — that would re-parent them out of pl-f700 and gut the approved logging plan. Instead pl-f700 stands as the logging sub-sequence under the same Plot, and this plan covers only the net-new tail. The chat ordering/dedup defect lives in src/ui/src/components/chat-messages.ts: buildChatMessages concatenates two seq-sorted groups (transcript first, then stream) instead of merging on a single unified ordering key, so turns render transcript-first-then-stream rather than chronologically, and the (kind, content) dedupe is loose enough that a streamed assistant turn and its persisted copy can both render. The unbounded-growth defect is in src/ui/src/pages/conversation-detail/conversation-surface.tsx: the conversation Card uses min-h-[60vh] with no upper bound, so Chat.tsx's existing internal `flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto` (Chat.tsx:152/157) never engages and the /workspaces page grows with the transcript. warren-4c8d (gatewatch) documents the exact leaked file from PR #340 and is currently unplanned, so it is adopted here. The version lives in two synced places (package.json + src/index.ts VERSION) plus a CHANGELOG.md section; the release workflow fails on drift.
sections.approach: Walk the net-new tail serially — one seed per PR, each gated on the prior PR merging — mirroring the polish-pass convention and the Plot's stated constraint. Order: chat ordering/dedup fix → chat unbounded-growth fix → leaked-transcript removal → 0.9.1 version bump (last, capping the batch). The whole Plot batch is gated behind pl-f700: the six logging PRs land first, then this tail, so the 0.9.1 bump is the final PR after every logging + chat + transcript PR merges (the version-bump seed records that ordering since a hard cross-plan block edge to warren-b2dd would mutate a seed this run did not create). Chat fixes are split into two seeds because they touch independent files (the pure merge logic vs. the page layout) and are independently reviewable: the ordering/dedup fix is pure, unit-testable logic with a regression test added to chat-messages.test.ts; the growth fix is a layout-only change that bounds the conversation card's ancestor height to engage the existing overflow-y-auto rather than introducing a new scroll container. Transcript removal is adopted from the existing warren-4c8d rather than re-authored. All seeds pass `bun run check:all` before merge.

alternatives.name: Re-adopt the six pl-f700 logging seeds into this umbrella plan as a literal contiguous step sub-sequence
alternatives.rejected_because: A seed's plan_id is single-valued; adopting c686/fc6e/af76/26c2/9f06/b2dd here would re-parent them off the approved pl-f700, gutting that plan and its review state. The Plot already owns the logging sub-sequence via pl-f700; this plan references it for ordering instead of destroying it.

alternatives.name: Fix chat ordering and dedup in one seed with the unbounded-growth fix
alternatives.rejected_because: They touch different files (pure merge logic in chat-messages.ts vs. layout height in conversation-surface.tsx) and have different review surfaces and test strategies. Splitting keeps each PR small, single-concern, and serially reviewable per the batch convention.

alternatives.name: Introduce a new fixed-height scroll container for the workspace chat
alternatives.rejected_because: Chat.tsx already has a working internal overflow-y-auto; the page grows only because no ancestor bounds its height. Bounding the existing ancestor is the minimal fix and avoids a second competing scroll region.

steps.title: Fix workspace chat ordering + dedup in src/ui/src/components/chat-messages.ts: merge transcript + stream bubbles on a single unified ordering key (chronological across the transcript/stream boundary) instead of concatenating the two seq-sorted groups, and tighten buildChatMessages dedupe so a streamed assistant turn and its persisted transcript copy collapse to one bubble; add regression tests to chat-messages.test.ts

Fix unbounded /workspaces growth: bound the conversation card's ancestor height in src/ui/src/pages/conversation-detail/conversation-surface.tsx (min-h-[60vh] → a bounded height) so Chat.tsx's existing internal flex-1 min-h-0 overflow-y-auto engages and the transcript scrolls internally instead of growing the page; no new scroll container

Bump version to 0.9.1: set package.json "version" and src/index.ts VERSION to 0.9.1 in sync (release workflow fails on drift) and add a matching CHANGELOG.md 0.9.1 section summarizing the logging hardening (pl-f700), workspace chat fixes, and leaked-transcript removal; land last, after every pl-f700 logging PR plus the chat + transcript PRs merge

risks: The unified ordering key must be stable when transcript rows and stream events share a seq space or use disjoint seq ranges — verify the merge against a never-started anchoring run (transcript only) and an active run (both present) so neither regresses; the existing chat-messages.test.ts cases must stay green.

Tightening dedupe must not collapse legitimately repeated tool/thinking rows (they intentionally key on event id, not content) — keep that behavior while making user/agent turns collapse across transcript+stream.

Bounding the conversation card height must not clip the input row or the plot-intent column on small viewports; verify both the conversation pane and the sibling intent pane in the lg:grid-cols-2 layout.
Version-bump drift: package.json and src/index.ts must match exactly or the release workflow fails; the CHANGELOG section header must match the X.Y.Z the release job greps for.

Serial gating across two plans (pl-f700 + this one) is advisory, not a hard block edge, since wiring warren-b2dd → step 1 would mutate a seed not created in this run; the version-bump seed and umbrella seed document the ordering so dispatch respects it.
acceptance: On the workspace conversation surface, user and agent turns render in correct chronological order across the transcript/stream boundary (no transcript-first-then-stream reordering).
No assistant message is duplicated when a streamed turn and its persisted transcript copy both exist; the buildChatMessages dedupe is covered by a new regression test in chat-messages.test.ts.

The workspace conversation transcript scrolls internally and the /workspaces page no longer grows unbounded, using Chat.tsx's existing overflow-y-auto via a bounded ancestor height (no new scroll container).
The leaked .pi/sessions agent transcript from PR #340 is removed from the repo (warren-4c8d).
VERSION in src/index.ts and "version" in package.json are both 0.9.1 and in sync, with a matching CHANGELOG.md 0.9.1 section.
Every seed in this plan passes `bun run check:all` (lint, typecheck, size, debt, dups, coverage, etc.) before merge.

sections.context: Plot plot-fbe17883 ('UI Nits') collects a batch of warren UI papercuts. Today sort behavior is inconsistent and duplicated: Runs.tsx ships a bespoke server-driven SortHeader/toggleSort with chevron icons and a 3-state cycle, while Workspace.tsx hand-rolls a client-side .sort() with handleSort/sortIndicator and text ↑↓ arrows and a 2-state toggle. Launching a plan-run is also a manual step: dispatch-plan-dialog.tsx and NewPlanRun.tsx both start planId as useState("") and force the operator to paste the plan id by hand, even though NewRun.tsx already prefills plot_id from location.state. Several pages also have not been reviewed for mobile: wide tables and modals can produce horizontal scroll or trap the user with no way to dismiss. This plan eliminates the duplication and the manual steps so tables and run-launch flows behave consistently.
sections.approach: Land one shared sortable-table primitive (a useSortableTable hook plus a SortableHeader component under src/ui/src/components/ui/) that owns sort key/dir state, the click-to-cycle decision, and a single consistent chevron affordance, with a mode for server-driven sorting (Runs passes sort/dir to the API) and client-side sorting (Workspace sorts in memory). Migrate the existing pages onto it, deleting the per-page bespoke logic so common columns (date/started, status) read and behave identically everywhere. Separately, close the plan-run launch gap by reading the planner's emitted plan id (surfaced via the Plot's sd_plan attachment / planner run) and prefilling the planId field, mirroring NewRun's route-state plot_id prefill. Finally, do a mobile-readiness pass: audit every page for unintended horizontal scroll (the flex-main min-w-0 pattern, mx-a8a1df, plus the Table overflow-auto wrapper) and ensure every modal/popup is dismissible on a touch viewport. Keeping the primitive first lets the two table migrations land as small independent PRs.

sections.context: Warren's UI has accumulated three concrete papercuts that this Plot (plot-9f03348c) targets. (1) Table sorting is inconsistent: Runs.tsx sorts server-side via a local SortHeader component, Workspace.tsx sorts client-side with inline ↑/↓ glyphs and its own SortKey/SortDir state, while Projects, PlanRuns, and Agents tables are not sortable at all. (2) The plan-run dispatch form (NewPlanRun.tsx) forces the operator to hand-type the plan id (`pl-a258`) into a free-text Input with no list to pick from — error-prone and undiscoverable. (3) Several pages (notably Runs.tsx and Workspace.tsx with zero responsive prefixes) break on phone-width viewports because their wide tables overflow and there is no standardized responsive pattern. This is responsive-web polish plus consistency work — no redesign, no native/PWA.
sections.approach: Tackle the three papercuts as independent, parallelizable workstreams that converge on a final release seed. SORTING: extract one canonical sortable column-header primitive into src/ui/src/components/ui/ that consolidates the two existing ad-hoc implementations (Workspace inline glyphs + Runs SortHeader), then wire it into every list table so sort affordances, glyphs, and toggle behaviour are identical everywhere. PLAN_ID PREFILL: add a read-side server endpoint that lists the available seeds plans for a project (shelling out through the existing src/seeds-cli/ helpers, mirroring `sd plan show`/`sd plan list`), expose it through the api client + types, then replace the free-text Plan ID Input in NewPlanRun.tsx with a populated selector that still allows a manual fallback. MOBILE: first standardize the responsive contract (canonical breakpoints targeting ~393px iPhone logical width degrading to ~360px, plus a reusable wide-table-on-mobile pattern — horizontal scroll / stacked), then apply it page-by-page so every page is usable on phones. Finish with the mandatory patch version bump via the .claude/commands/release.md flow. Chosen over a single monolithic 'fix the UI' seed because each papercut touches different modules, reviews independently, and the Plot constraint explicitly permits chunked mobile execution.

alternatives.name: One monolithic UI-polish seed
alternatives.rejected_because: Too large to review as a single PR and conflates three unrelated surfaces (table component, server endpoint + form, responsive CSS); the Plot intent explicitly allows the mobile work to be chunked.

alternatives.name: Client-side-only plan_id autocomplete (no new endpoint)
alternatives.rejected_because: The UI has no existing way to enumerate a project's plans; the plan list lives in `.seeds/plans.jsonl` inside the clone, only reachable server-side via the seeds-cli helpers, so a read endpoint is required to populate any selector.

No production code path or import of pause.ts changes.

sections.context: Plan-runs are welded to a single project: src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts resolves every child through planRun.projectId, and src/plan-runs/dispatch.ts (createPlanRunSpawn) calls spawnRun({ projectId: planRun.projectId }). A meta-repo (e.g. kota-monorepo: a directory of independent child repos coordinated by a Makefile + stack.lock + one-way contracts sync) wants a cross-repo plan whose children live in the meta-repo's .seeds/ but each execute against a DIFFERENT child repo. Today such a plan would clone the meta-repo into every child's workspace, where the actual code does not live. The default plan-run prompt template is literally 'work on sd {seed_id}' (NewPlanRun.tsx:19), which expects the executor to run `sd show <id>` IN ITS workspace — so a meta-repo seed is invisible to a child-repo executor. The unlock: warren already does all seed reads/writes and plot mirroring HOST-SIDE against the project clone it holds (R-01: spawn + reap call updateExtensions; coordinator calls showSeed host-side), so the agent never needs cross-repo access. We only need to stop conflating 'which repo to clone into the workspace' with 'which host clone owns the seed'.
sections.approach: Adopt a warren-side convention (NO seeds core change): a child seed carries extensions.repo (a project slug or git remote URL) naming its execution repo. Split spawnRun's single projectId into an execution project (the repo cloned into the workspace) and a seedProjectId (the coordination project whose host clone owns the sd update + plot append), defaulting seedProjectId = projectId so every existing single-repo run stays byte-identical. The plan-run coordinator keeps reading/closing seeds and appending plot against planRun.projectId (the meta-repo), while per-child dispatch resolves extensions.repo to a registered execution project and clones THAT. Because the executor's workspace has no .seeds/ for the meta-repo seed, warren inlines the seed title+body into the prompt ({seed_body}). The serial merge-gate model is unchanged: each child = one repo = one PR = one merge gate, which matches the meta-repo's own decompose-into-serial-single-repo-steps philosophy. Routing knowledge lives in the meta-repo's per-project .canopy/ planner role + a custom seeds plan template (per-step repo field), backed by a warren pre-dispatch guardrail — never in executor context.

alternatives.name: Multi-repo burrow workspace (clone a collection of repos into one sandbox)
alternatives.rejected_because: It crosses the warren<->burrow boundary (provision N clones, N git remotes for creds, N branch pushes) and breaks warren's single-repo reap/PR/preview pipeline (one prUrl, one merge gate, one preview). Its only real win is a TRULY atomic cross-repo change — which the meta-repo design (no submodules, no workspaces, contract-mediated coupling) deliberately avoids. Keep it as a documented future escape hatch, not this plan.

alternatives.name: Build 'meta-repo infra' into seeds core (a first-class child-repo attachment field)
alternatives.rejected_because: Seeds keeps Issue.extensions schema-stable on purpose and stays generic; coupling it to one warren usage pattern is wrong. extensions is already free-form per consumer (R-01), so the routing rides existing seeds features with zero seeds code.

alternatives.name: Have the executor agent update the meta-repo seed directly
alternatives.rejected_because: It has no access to the meta-repo workspace, and warren already owns the host-side seed write at dispatch and reap. Mid-run follow-ups, if ever needed, route through Plot (the meta-repo is already the coordination substrate).

steps.title: Add a `repo` key to the warren-namespaced seeds extensions schema. In src/seeds-cli/warren-extensions.ts add an optional `repo: z.string().min(1)` field to WarrenExtensionsSchema (the project slug or git remote URL a seed's work targets) and export a typed reader (e.g. readTargetRepo(extensions): string | undefined). Confirm src/seeds-cli/schema.ts SeedShowIssue.extensions (z.record(z.string(), z.unknown())) already round-trips `extensions.repo` through `sd show --json`; add a parse case proving it. No seeds CLI change — this is the warren-owned namespace only. Verify: `bun test src/seeds-cli/warren-extensions.test.ts src/seeds-cli/show.test.ts` green with new present/absent/empty-string cases; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Add a repo->project resolver. New src/projects/resolve-target.ts exporting resolveTargetProject(repos, repoRef): Promise<string> that maps a seed's extensions.repo (a project slug/name OR a git remote URL — normalize trailing `.git`, and ssh `git@host:owner/repo` vs https `https://host/owner/repo` forms) to a registered project id via repos.projects, throwing a typed TargetProjectUnresolvedError (joins the existing warren error family in the projects module) when nothing matches. Pure lookup, no clone, no side effects. Verify: `bun test src/projects/resolve-target.test.ts` covers slug match, https URL match, ssh URL match, trailing-.git normalization, and unresolved -> typed error; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Split spawnRun's single project identity into execution vs coordination. In src/runs/spawn/ add an optional `seedProjectId` input distinct from `projectId`: `projectId` selects the repo cloned into the workspace (execution); `seedProjectId` (default = projectId) selects the host project clone used for the post-dispatch seeds updateExtensions write and any plot append/mirror. Thread it so the seed stamp (role/lastRunId/lastRunAt) and plot operations target seedProjectId, never the execution project. Do NOT change the burrow provisioning path. Verify: existing `bun test src/runs/` stays green and byte-identical for the default (seedProjectId === projectId) case; a new test asserts that when seedProjectId != projectId the sd update runs against seedProjectId while the workspace clones projectId; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Inline seed content into the dispatch prompt so a cross-repo executor needs no in-workspace .seeds/ access. Resolve the seed title+body host-side (seeds-cli `sd show` against seedProjectId) and add a `{seed_body}` substitution alongside the existing `{seed_id}` in the plan-run/run prompt builder; when seedProjectId != execution projectId, auto-inject the resolved title+body even if the template only references `{seed_id}`, so the executor receives the issue text directly. Keep `{seed_id}`-only behavior unchanged when the projects match. Verify: unit tests cover `{seed_body}` substitution and the auto-inject-on-divergent-project path; `bun test` for the prompt builder green; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Wire per-child execution-project routing into the plan-run coordinator + dispatch. In src/plan-runs/dispatch.ts createPlanRunSpawn: for each child read extensions.repo from the seed (showSeed already returns extensions), resolve it to an execution project via resolveTargetProject (fallback to planRun.projectId when the tag is absent), and call spawnRun with projectId = resolved execution project AND seedProjectId = planRun.projectId; load the execution project to derive ref/defaultBranch. Keep coordinator.ts showSeed/close/skip and the plot-append pointed at planRun.projectId (coordination). The merge gate is unchanged (polls the child run's prUrl). Verify: `bun test src/plan-runs/` green incl. new cases for (a) routed child clones the child repo while seed reads hit the meta-repo, (b) untagged child falls back to planRun.projectId, (c) unresolved repo fails that child with a typed reason via the existing plan_failed path; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Persist and surface each plan-run child's execution project. Add a nullable execution_project_id column to plan_run_children in BOTH src/db/schema/sqlite.ts and src/db/schema/postgres.ts (+ the shared constant in src/db/schema/columns.ts), generate migrations for both dialects via the drizzle.config.sqlite.ts / drizzle.config.postgres.ts flows (update both meta/_journal.json), have the coordinator write the resolved id when it dispatches a child, expose it on the plan-run detail API response (ROUTE_TABLE), and render a per-child repo column/badge in src/ui/src/pages/PlanRunDetail.tsx (+ src/ui/src/pages/plan-run-detail/). Regenerate docs/openapi.yaml via `bun run gen:openapi`. Verify: `bun run typecheck`, `bun test`, `bun run gen:openapi:check`, and `bun run build:ui` all green; both dialect journals updated.

Add a pre-dispatch guardrail + doctor check for cross-repo plans. At POST /plan-runs (and/or the first coordinator dispatch) validate that every child carrying extensions.repo resolves to a registered project via resolveTargetProject; reject with a structured 4xx listing the unresolved repo refs rather than dispatching into the wrong workspace. Add a `warren doctor` / readyz `cross_repo_plan_targets` check that walks open plans' children and flags unresolved repo tags. Verify: `bun test` covers reject-on-unresolved + happy path through the handler; the doctor check appears in `warren doctor` output; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Generalize routing to the single-run path. In the POST /runs dispatch handler, when the request carries a seedId, read the seed's extensions.repo and resolve the execution project via the shared resolver (fallback to the request's projectId), passing seedProjectId = the seed's home project and using the {seed_body} prompt injection. Keep the no-seedId / same-project path byte-identical. Verify: `bun test` for the runs handler covers seed-routed dispatch and the unchanged default path; `bun run typecheck` clean.

Author the meta-repo planning surface and document the coordination/execution model. Ship an example cross-repo-planner canopy role for the per-project .canopy/ tier whose system prompt encodes 'one plan step = one child repo, tag each with extensions.repo: <slug>' plus the valid child slugs, AND a custom seeds plan template (plan_templates) with a per-step `repo` field so the planner fills a structured slot instead of remembering. Place examples under docs/ (or a templates dir). Update SPEC (the plan-run section, §11.P) + CLAUDE.md/ROADMAP R-20 with the coordination-project-vs-execution-project contract and the 'no seeds core change' decision. Verify: `bun run gen:docs:check`, `bun run check:agents`, and `bun run lint` green; every referenced path exists.

Add an end-to-end acceptance scenario + freeze the contract. New scripts/acceptance/scenarios/NN-cross-repo-plan-run.ts that registers a meta-repo coordination project plus 2 child execution projects, submits a 2-child plan whose children are tagged extensions.repo, dispatches the plan-run, and asserts: each child clones its tagged repo, opens its own PR, the meta-repo seed is updated host-side (role/lastRunId), and serial merge gating advances child 2 only after child 1's PR merges. Deterministic, idempotent, self-cleaning per scripts/acceptance/lib conventions. Verify: the scenario passes against a live warren+burrow stack; `bun run check:all` fully green.

risks: Executor cannot update the meta-repo seed mid-run (its workspace has no .seeds/ for it). Mitigation: warren owns the host-side write at dispatch and reap; mid-run follow-ups route through Plot, not the agent. Documented as an explicit limitation in step 9.

Migration drift between SQLite and Postgres for the new execution_project_id column (step 6). Mitigation: generate and commit both dialect migrations + journals in the same step; check:all runs ci-parity and the pg acceptance path.
Repo-ref normalization ambiguity (slug vs https vs ssh, trailing .git). Mitigation: the resolver (step 2) has explicit table-driven tests for each form before any caller depends on it.

Bundle-size / openapi gates trip on the step 6 UI + API surface. Mitigation: step 6 verification explicitly runs gen:openapi:check and build:ui; re-baseline bundle via `bun run check:bundle-size --update` only if a legitimate within-cap growth.

Conflating execution vs coordination project could regress ordinary single-repo runs. Mitigation: seedProjectId defaults to projectId; every foundational step asserts the default path is byte-identical.
acceptance: A plan whose children are tagged extensions.repo dispatches each child against its tagged registered project's workspace while reading/closing the seed and appending plot against the meta-repo (planRun.projectId) host-side.
An untagged plan child still dispatches against planRun.projectId exactly as today (no behavior change for existing single-repo plan-runs).
A child tagged with an unresolved repo is rejected pre-dispatch (or fails that child with a typed reason) rather than cloning the wrong repo, and the condition is surfaced by a warren doctor check.
A cross-repo executor receives the seed title+body inline in its prompt and completes work without any in-workspace `sd show` of the meta-repo seed.
Serial merge gating is preserved: child N+1 dispatches only after child N's PR merges, across different repos.
`bun run check:all` is fully green and an end-to-end acceptance scenario exercises the meta-repo + 2-child-repo flow.

sections.context: Seeds plans flip to the `approved` status once a human signs off, but today the only way to launch them is the manual /plan-runs/new form where the operator must already know the plan id. There is no surface that proactively shows which approved plans are sitting un-dispatched. This adds a safe, operator-gated 'Ready to dispatch' tab that lists approved plans with at least one open child and no existing plan-run, each with a one-click dispatch that reuses the existing POST /plan-runs path and dispatch popup. True auto-dispatch (Approach A) is explicitly out of scope.
sections.approach: Read-on-demand, no background dispatcher. A new per-project read endpoint GET /projects/:id/ready-plans composes existing seeds-cli readers (sd plan list / sd plan show / sd list) plus a new plan-runs dedup query to compute readiness: status === 'approved', at least one open (non-closed) child seed, and no plan_run row for that plan id. The UI adds a 'Ready to dispatch' tab to the existing Plan runs page that polls this endpoint and opens a generalized version of the existing dispatch dialog (pre-filled plan id + project, model/provider/prompt editable). Dispatch still goes over the unchanged planRunsApi.create (POST /plan-runs); no new dispatch path is introduced, so the operator-gated SPEC §10.4 approval signal is preserved.

alternatives.name: Background poller that auto-dispatches approved plans (Approach A)
alternatives.rejected_because: Dangerous and against the v1 operator-gated taste signal; needs durable dedup + default agent/model/prompt with no human in the loop. Deferred as an opt-in layer that can reuse this surface's readiness logic later.

alternatives.name: Dedicated new top-level Plans page
alternatives.rejected_because: Heavier nav surface for a feature that is conceptually a pre-stage of plan runs; a tab on the existing Plan runs page keeps it discoverable next to the runs it produces.

steps.title: Add PlanRunsRepo.listDispatchedPlanIds(projectId) returning the distinct set of plan ids that already have a plan_run row for the project (the dedup primitive). Implement as a SELECT DISTINCT plan_id WHERE project_id = ? returning string[]. Add unit tests in src/db/repos/plan-runs.test.ts covering no rows, multiple plan-runs for one plan id collapsing to a single entry, and project scoping. Verify: bun test src/db/repos/plan-runs.test.ts and bun run check:all green.

Add a lean listSeedStatuses(deps, projectPath) reader to src/seeds-cli that shells `sd list --format json`, parses via the existing SeedsListEnvelopeSchema, and returns a ReadonlyMap<seedId, status> for every issue (not just scheduled ones). Re-export from src/seeds-cli/index.ts. Unit-test the parse + map build against a stub spawn: mixed open/closed statuses, empty list, and non-zero exit wrapping in SeedsCliError. Verify: bun test src/seeds-cli and bun run check:all green.

Add a pure computeReadyPlans({ plans, seedStatusById, dispatchedPlanIds }) helper (new module under src/plan-runs) where each plan carries { id, name?, status, children: string[] }. Return only plans with status === 'approved' that have at least one open (non-closed) child seed AND are not in dispatchedPlanIds, each annotated with openChildCount. Unit-test the full truth table: approved+open+undispatched (included), approved+all-children-closed (excluded), approved+already-dispatched (excluded), and non-approved (excluded). Verify: bun test for the new module and bun run check:all green.

Add the GET /projects/:id/ready-plans handler in src/server/handlers/projects.ts gated exactly like listProjectSeedPlansHandler (project 404, hasSeeds → 400, seedsCli configured → 400). Orchestrate: listPlans, filter to status 'approved', resolve each approved plan's children via showPlan, build the status map via listSeedStatuses, fetch dispatched ids via repos.planRuns.listDispatchedPlanIds, then return { plans } from computeReadyPlans (entries { id, name?, status, openChildCount }). Register the route in ROUTE_TABLE (src/server/handlers/index.ts) and regenerate docs with bun run gen:docs and bun run gen:openapi. Add handler tests: a ready plan surfaces, an all-children-closed plan is hidden, an already-dispatched plan is hidden, and a non-seeds project returns 400. Verify: bun run check:all green including gen:docs:check and gen:openapi:check.

Add typed client facades for the new endpoint: src/client/client.ts listReadyPlans(projectId) plus its response type in src/client/types.ts, AND the UI facade projectsApi.readyPlans in src/ui/src/api/client.ts plus a ReadyPlan type in src/ui/src/api/types.ts. Mirror the existing seedPlans facade shape (URL building, AbortSignal passthrough). Add a client unit test asserting the request URL and parsed shape. Verify: bun run check:all green and the UI typechecks via bun run build:ui.

Generalize the operator dispatch popup so it can be opened outside a conversation. Extract the form body of src/ui/src/pages/conversation-detail/dispatch-plan-dialog.tsx into a reusable DispatchPlanDialog accepting { projectId, planId (pre-fillable + optionally locked), plotId?: string | null } and drop the required plannerRunId; keep the conversation caller working by routing its existing planner-run hint through the new planId prop. Dispatch still goes over planRunsApi.create (POST /plan-runs) unchanged. Add or adjust UI tests for the generalized component and the conversation caller. Verify: bun run build:ui and bun run check:all green.

Add a 'Ready to dispatch' tab to src/ui/src/pages/PlanRuns.tsx that toggles between the existing plan-runs table and a ready-plans view. For the selected project the view fetches projectsApi.readyPlans (5s refetch) and renders a table (plan id, name, status, open-child count), each row with a one-click Dispatch button opening the generalized DispatchPlanDialog pre-filled with that plan id + project (+ plot id when the project has .plot/). Match the page's loading/empty/error conventions and prompt the operator to pick a project when none is selected (the endpoint is per-project). Add a UI test covering the tab and one-click open. If the UI bundle grows, re-baseline with bun run check:bundle-size --update. Verify: bun run check:all green.

Add a deterministic, idempotent, self-cleaning acceptance scenario at scripts/acceptance/scenarios/NN-ready-to-dispatch-plans.ts following the scripts/acceptance/lib conventions: register a project with .seeds/, create and approve a plan with one open child, assert GET /projects/:id/ready-plans surfaces it with openChildCount of 1; dispatch a plan-run over POST /plan-runs; assert the plan no longer appears in ready-plans (dedup confirmed). Verify: the scenario passes against a live warren+burrow stack and bun run check:all green.

Document the ready-to-dispatch surface: add a SPEC §11.P note describing the operator-gated, read-on-demand model and the approved + has-open-child + not-dispatched criteria, and state explicitly that background auto-dispatch (Approach A) is deferred. Update README.md and CLAUDE.md/AGENTS.md only if the surface count or structure they describe changed. Verify: bun run gen:docs:check, bun run check:agents, and bun run lint green, and every referenced path exists.

Run the .claude/commands/release.md flow with a PATCH version bump: find the last release tag and review changes since it, bump the version in package.json and src/index.ts (export const VERSION) in lockstep at the patch level, move CHANGELOG.md [Unreleased] entries into a new dated version section, update CLAUDE.md/README.md if command counts or structure changed, then commit. Verify: package.json and src/index.ts VERSION agree, CHANGELOG.md has the new section, and bun run check:all is green.

risks: computeReadyPlans needs each approved plan's child ids; sd plan list strips them in the PlanSummary projection. Mitigation: the endpoint resolves children via showPlan per approved plan (approved plans are few), keeping the compute helper pure and shell-outs in the handler.

Resolving open children per plan could fan out many sd show calls. Mitigation: a single sd list --format json builds one status map joined against plan children, so child status costs one shell-out per project regardless of plan count.

'not dispatched' could be read as 'no active plan-run' vs 'no plan-run at all'. Mitigation: this surface uses 'no plan_run row for the plan id' so dispatching moves a plan out of the tab immediately; resume semantics stay a follow-on concern.

Route additions trip gen:docs:check / gen:openapi:check and the UI tab can trip check:bundle-size. Mitigation: the endpoint and UI steps explicitly regenerate docs/openapi and re-baseline the bundle within cap.

Generalizing the conversation dispatch dialog could regress the existing conversation hand-off. Mitigation: the conversation caller is kept working via the new planId prop and covered by adjusted UI tests in the same step.
acceptance: GET /projects/:id/ready-plans returns only plans that are status 'approved', have at least one open child seed, and have no existing plan-run, each annotated with openChildCount; gates mirror the seeds-plans endpoint (404 / hasSeeds 400 / seedsCli 400).

The Plan runs page has a 'Ready to dispatch' tab that lists those plans for the selected project and dispatches a selected plan via a one-click popup over the existing POST /plan-runs path, with model/provider/prompt editable.
Once a plan is dispatched it no longer appears in the ready-to-dispatch surface (dedup verified end-to-end by an acceptance scenario).
No background auto-dispatch is introduced; dispatch remains fully operator-gated.
bun run check:all is fully green (including gen:docs:check, gen:openapi:check, check:bundle-size, and check:coverage) and an acceptance scenario exercises the surface end-to-end.
The final step ships a patch release via the .claude/commands/release.md flow with package.json and src/index.ts VERSION in agreement and a new dated CHANGELOG section.

sections.context: Patrol scan of warren on 2026-06-22. Quality gates (bun test 2979 pass, bun run lint, bun run typecheck) are all green, so this patrol targets correctness/consistency issues the linter cannot see. All findings cluster in the freshly-landed observability instrumentation (commit 29c09f4a, 'Add observability instrumentation: Sentry + Prometheus Phase 1'): a defense-in-depth secret-scrub gap, a Prometheus metric-naming convention violation, and a readonly-array mutation via double-cast. No feature work, no API-signature changes, no dependency changes.
sections.behavior_invariant: The /metrics endpoint must keep emitting the same set of run-state, cost, token, bridge, and log-rate series (only metric NAMES change for the _total fix); the Prometheus exposition must stay valid v0.0.4 text. The Sentry scrubber must keep redacting every secret-shaped field it already redacts at the top level (existing tests stay green) and additionally redact nested ones. MetricsRegistry accumulation/sorting semantics and the no-op-tracker behavior when SENTRY_DSN is unset must be byte-identical.
sections.approach:
Three small, independently-landable fixes, each with a unit test pinning the corrected behavior. Land the secret-scrub fix first (independent file), then the two metrics.ts fixes serially to avoid same-file merge churn, then a release because two of the three changes are consumer-observable.

FINDING 1 (security + parity + doc drift) - src/observability/error-tracking.ts scrubRecord() ~lines 116-123 and scrubSentryEvent() ~lines 98-110. scrubRecord only redacts TOP-LEVEL keys, but src/observability/log-sink.ts forwardLogToSinks() (~lines 56-66) forwards the raw structured pino log object to Sentry as extra BEFORE pino's serialize-time redact runs, and the central policy in src/server/main/redact.ts (LOG_REDACT_PATHS) explicitly censors one level of nesting via the *.<field> wildcard. So a nested secret like { extra: { config: { token } } } leaks into Sentry's extra even though the same field is censored in the log line, and the module doc comment ('even if a caller attaches a whole config/headers object as context') is false. Fix: make scrubRecord recurse into nested record values one level (matching the pino *.<field> policy); keep top-level behavior identical.

FINDING 2 (consistency / Prometheus naming convention) - src/server/handlers/metrics.ts ~lines 47-56. warren_cost_usd_total, warren_tokens_input_total, warren_tokens_output_total are type:'gauge' but carry the _total suffix Prometheus reserves for counters (promlint: 'non-counter metrics should not have _total suffix'). They are live SUMs over src/db/repos/runs-stats.ts aggregateRunCost and can decrease when runs are reaped, so gauge is correct - drop the _total suffix (warren_cost_usd, warren_tokens_input, warren_tokens_output). The genuine counter warren_log_messages_total keeps its suffix. Update src/server/handlers/metrics.test.ts line ~92.

FINDING 3 (type safety) - src/server/handlers/metrics.ts countersToMetrics() ~lines 73-90 pushes onto existing.samples via a double-cast (existing.samples as {...}[]).push(sample), mutating an array typed readonly PromSample[]. Fix: accumulate samples in a mutable array keyed by metric name, then build each PromMetric once - no cast, no readonly mutation.

sections.context: Nightwatch patrol of 2026-06-23. Quality gates are green: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun run check:debt`, and `bun run check:dups` all pass; no `as any`, `@ts-ignore`, or untracked debt markers exist in non-test `src/`. The patrol found one concrete defect: a non-deterministic test in `src/runs/spawn/plot-append.test.ts` that fails whenever the host environment defines `WARREN_API_TOKEN` / `WARREN_API_URL` (which is exactly the case inside a deployed warren container and in CI sandboxes). The test `omits env from the burrow up call when no plotId is set (warren-e26f)` calls `spawnRun(...)` without passing `serverEnv`, so dispatch falls back to `process.env` (`src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts:441` — `serverEnv ?? process.env`). `injectWarrenCallbackEnv` (`src/runs/spawn/callback-env.ts`) then copies the ambient `WARREN_API_TOKEN` and a derived `WARREN_API_URL` into the burrow up-call env. The test asserts `expect(env).toEqual({ BUN_INSTALL_CACHE_DIR: "/tmp/bun-install-cache" })`, which fails because the env now also contains the leaked callback vars. Verified: with `env -u WARREN_API_TOKEN -u WARREN_API_URL bun test` the file is 10/10 green; with those vars set it is 9/10. This is a test-isolation defect, not a product bug — the token injection itself is intended behavior (warren-f248). No source/behavior change is required.

sections.context: On the deployed instance (warren-deployed.fly.dev, project prj_z07y6ssfjfpk) the scheduler emits scheduler.cron_failed every ~60s with reason 'spawnRun failed: agent not found: warden-digest'. A weekly cron ('0 5 * * 0') is retrying every single tick instead of once per slot, producing continuous log spam and wasted scheduler ticks that mask real signal. Operators running warren without the canopy audit agents registered (CANOPY_REPO_URL unset) hit this for every audit trigger in .warren/triggers.yaml (warden-digest, nightwatch, bugwatch, gatewatch, ratchetwatch, tastewatch). The fix restores correct no-catch-up cron semantics and quiets the noise so the observability surface stays trustworthy.
sections.reproduction:
1. Run warren with a project whose .warren/triggers.yaml has a cron entry (e.g. cron '0 5 * * 0') referencing an agent name that is NOT in the agent registry (no inline built-in, no canopy library entry).
2. Let the scheduler tick (default 60s) past the cron's first elapsed slot.
Observed: scheduler.cron_failed fires every ~60s with reason 'spawnRun failed: agent not found: <role>' — the same elapsed slot is re-dispatched on every tick because the trigger row's lastFiredAt never advances on the failed dispatch.
Expected: the slot is consumed once; the operator sees at most one warning per cron slot and the scheduler does not retry the unregistered agent every tick.
sections.root_cause: In src/triggers/dispatch.ts, dispatchCronTrigger fires when parsed.cron.previousRun(now) > row.lastFiredAt. When the spawn call throws, the catch block returns { kind: 'error' } WITHOUT calling repos.triggers.recordFire / upsert, so lastFiredAt is never advanced (see the comment 'Next tick will recompute prev > last and retry'). For a transient failure (burrow briefly down) retrying is correct, but for a PERMANENT failure — spawnRun throws NotFoundError 'agent not found: <agentName>' from src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts when repos.agents.resolve returns null — the condition prev > last stays true for the entire slot window (a full week for '0 5 * * 0'), so every tick re-attempts and re-fails. The defect is that the dispatcher treats a deterministic, won't-resolve-this-slot failure identically to a transient one.
sections.approach: Distinguish permanent spawn failures from transient ones in dispatchCronTrigger. When the spawn error is an agent-not-found (NotFoundError with the 'agent not found:' shape), consume the cron slot by advancing the trigger row's lastFiredAt+nextFireAt via the existing repos.triggers.upsert (no runId — the existing UpsertTriggerInput already supports lastFiredAt/nextFireAt without lastRunId) and return a distinct skipped/error result carrying the reason. This way the elapsed slot is recorded as handled, so the next tick sees prev <= last and does NOT retry until the next genuine slot — i.e. warn-once-per-slot instead of every-tick spam, while preserving no-catch-up semantics. Transient failures keep the current retry-next-tick behavior (no row advance). Chosen over fix-option (3) 'validate trigger roles at config load' because that is broader (config-load surface, HTTP/UI error plumbing) and over fix-option (1) 'just register the agents' because that is an operator action, not a code fix — the scheduler should be robust to unregistered roles regardless. No public API, dependency, or architectural changes; the change is local to the triggers module.

Warren has exactly four open GitHub issues and all four are confirmed real against main via subagent code inspection. #420 (bug): the reap bookkeeping helpers run a bare `git commit` with no pathspec, so any unrelated pre-staged files get swept into a mislabeled, hook-bypassing chore(warren) commit (observed downstream in kessellab/kessel). #487 (P1 bug): the plan-run auto-done Plot transition is dead in the default flow because nothing promotes a Plot from ready->active, so the SPEC 11.P.Plot documented auto-done never fires (it only skips). #486 (P2 bug): the UI hardcodes `.warren/defaults.json` even when config loads from config.yaml, showing wrong info to operators. #419 (feature): runs cannot target an existing branch and have reap push back to it, so repair/review/verify loops create a new branch instead of updating the one they were dispatched from. This plan closes all four in a single coordinated batch converging on one release-prep step.
sections.approach: Forward-chained, single-agent-sized child seeds, grouped by issue, converging on one terminal release-prep seed. #420 is a self-contained one-file-plus-test fix using `git commit --only -- <pathspecs>`. #487 uses promotion-at-dispatch (promote ready->active via a dedicated fire-and-log seam, leaving the auto-done guard ===active unchanged) because the issue's 'simpler' option of widening the guard is broken by plot-cli's illegal ready->done transition; it splits into a code-seam+wiring seed and a SPEC/acceptance reconcile seed. #486 uses a dynamic sourceFile field threaded loader->API->UI (not a static string swap, which would lie for legacy installs), split server-side then UI-side. #419 uses Option B (minimal reconcile, per maintainer decision): keep today's branch-override semantics and the untouched CI-fixer, and only add the missing pieces -- persist a new runs.target_branch column, expose it via POST /runs, and surface it on the wire types -- because reap already pushes to the target (the burrow branch is the target). Schema/migration lands first, then dispatch/spawn wiring and wire types fan out from it. A final seed bumps VERSION in both files plus CHANGELOG and runs the full gate suite.

sections.context:
Nightwatch patrol of warren on 2026-07-01. All 12 quality gates are green (lint, typecheck, check:dups, check:deps, check:size, check:debt, check:bundle-size, gen:docs:check, gen:openapi:check, check:coverage, check:ci-parity). The scan found one cross-call-site consistency issue in how warren stamps the `ts` field on its own synthetic system events.

Warren's pervasive convention (documented in mulch and the diagnostics module header: 'the functions themselves are pure modulo their injected spawn/exists/burrowClient seams — tests can stub all I/O') is that every clock read flows through an injected `now` seam so tests can pin the clock. ~14 system-event append sites honor this (`ts: now.toISOString()` / `ts: now().toISOString()` / `ts: input.now.toISOString()`), but 5 private `appendSystemEvent`-style helpers set the envelope `ts` from wall-clock `new Date().toISOString()` even though the SAME append's payload timestamp is taken from the in-scope injected `now`. Example (src/runs/pause.ts): `pauseRun(..., now: Date)` builds payload `{ pausedAt: now.toISOString() }` then calls `appendSystemEvent` which writes `ts: new Date().toISOString()`.

Consequences: (1) the event row's envelope `ts` drifts from its payload timestamp (pausedAt/resumedAt/finalizedAt/rewokenAt/dispatchedAt/lastRunAt) — two timestamps on one event that can disagree, a readability wart; (2) tests that pin `now: () => NOW` cannot deterministically assert on `event.ts` (the conversation-idle test already pins NOW and asserts on the event's kind/payload but conspicuously NOT on `ts`), so the determinism the `now` seam exists to provide is silently lost on this one field.
sections.behavior_invariant: The set of system events emitted, their kind/stream/payload/burrowEventSeq, and every dispatch/finalize/persist side effect are unchanged. The ONLY change is the source of the envelope `ts` field: from `new Date().toISOString()` to the already-in-scope injected `now` clock. In production the `now` seam defaults to `() => new Date()`, so persisted and streamed `ts` values remain real wall-clock ISO-8601 timestamps within microseconds of today's values — no consumer-observable shape or ordering change. No public API signature, route table, error envelope, agent definition, or config schema changes; only private module-internal helper functions gain a `now: Date` parameter.
sections.approach: Thread the already-in-scope `now: Date` into each of the 5 private system-event appender helpers and use it for the envelope `ts`, matching the payload timestamp written in the same append. One coherent mechanical change across 5 files (same fix pattern), landing as a single PR so a reviewer sees the consistency applied uniformly. Scoped strictly to sites where `now` is ALREADY a parameter of the calling function — no new seams on exported interfaces. The 3 sites that lack an in-scope `now` (src/server/bridges.ts bridge_fatal catch path, src/runs/stream/budget.ts emitBudgetEvent whose EnforceBudgetCapInput has no now, src/server/bridge-reconnect.ts emitBridgeSystemEvent whose RunWithReconnectInput has no now) are intentionally left untouched — fixing them would require threading a new clock seam across the bridge boundary, which is an architecture change outside patrol scope.

steps.title: Stamp system-event ts from the injected now clock in 5 appendSystemEvent helpers
steps.description:

sections.context: The plan-run merge gate treats a transient GitHub 401/403/429 (auth blip or rate limit) on the PR merge-status poll as a fatal "PR is gone" signal. It fails the whole plan-run with `pr_closed_without_merge` (child path) or `parent_pr_not_merged` (parent-gate path) even though the PR is OPEN/CLEAN/MERGEABLE. This killed plan-run plnr_1bw1cw8ch4n6 at seq 1 on a single intermittent 401 — a follow-up probe saw 1x401 then 6/6 200, /user 200, rate limit healthy. Who is affected: every auto-plan-run whose PR-merge poll hits a transient 4xx stalls terminally and needs a human re-dispatch; the cleanup-batch children of pl-4d2e were collateral. Operators lose trust in plan-run reliability and the failure masks real signal in scheduler logs.
sections.reproduction:
1. A plan-run with an in-flight child at `pr_open` (or a parent-gated first child) whose PR is OPEN and mergeable.
2. The scheduler tick calls `createPrMergeChecker` -> `checkPullRequestMerged` (src/runs/pr-checks.ts) which GETs /pulls/:number. GitHub returns a transient 401 (or 403/429).
3. `checkPullRequestMerged` maps ANY non-200 to `{kind: "http_error", status: 401}` (src/runs/pr-checks.ts lines 117-122; `missing_token` is a separate kind only for an unset GITHUB_TOKEN, so a real 401 surfaces as http_error). `createPrMergeChecker` (src/plan-runs/pr-merge.ts) does NOT retry 4xx — `isTransient` matches only status 0 or >=500 — so the 401 is returned immediately.
4. The coordinator's `pollMergeState` (src/plan-runs/in-flight.ts:319) / `checkParentRunMerged` (src/plan-runs/merge-gate.ts:114) sees `isFatalHttpError(polled)` == true (status >= 400 && < 500) and calls `failChild(..., "pr_closed_without_merge")` / `failParentGate(..., "parent_pr_not_merged")`.
5. Observed: `plan_run.failed` carrying httpStatus:401 at seq 1, plan-run terminal. Expected: 401/403/429 mean "cannot verify right now" -> keep waiting (bounded by the merge-wait budget, warren-3937); only 404/410 (PR genuinely gone) should fail the plan.
sections.root_cause: `isFatalHttpError` in src/plan-runs/merge-gate.ts (lines ~174-182) classifies ANY 4xx (`result.status >= 400 && result.status < 500`) as a fatal "PR is gone" signal. Both consumers gate on it: `checkParentRunMerged` (merge-gate.ts:114 -> reason `parent_pr_not_merged`) and `pollMergeState` (in-flight.ts:319 -> reason `pr_closed_without_merge`). So a transient auth/rate-limit 4xx is indistinguishable from a hard-deleted PR. GitHub's 401/403/429 are "cannot verify right now," not "PR is gone"; only 404 and 410 mean the PR no longer exists. The merge-wait budget (`mergeDeadlineExceeded`, warren-3937) already bounds the wait in both arms, so treating 401/403/429 as "keep waiting" is safe — a permanently-bad token still fails eventually via `child_pr_merge_timeout` / `parent_pr_merge_timeout` rather than hanging forever.
sections.approach: Narrow `isFatalHttpError` (src/plan-runs/merge-gate.ts) to return true only for status 404 or 410 — the only statuses that genuinely mean the PR is gone. 401/403/429 (and any other 4xx) then fall through to the existing keep-waiting arms in both consumers, bounded by the merge-wait budget. Rationale over alternatives: (a) Adding 401/403/429 to pr-merge.ts's `isTransient` retry set would cut wasted ticks but is NOT required for correctness (the coordinator re-polls on the next tick) and would push the change past the 3-file budget (pr-merge.ts + pr-merge.test.ts) — left as a documented follow-up, not done here. (b) Patching only one consumer would leave the other regressable; narrowing the shared `isFatalHttpError` fixes both at once. (c) The fix changes no public API (`isFatalHttpError` is module-internal, confirmed by grep: only merge-gate.ts:114 and in-flight.ts:319 consume it) and needs no dependency or architectural change. The existing child-gate test (coordinator.completion.test.ts:144) uses status 404, which stays fatal, so the fix lands with CI green before the new 401/403/429 regression tests are added.

sections.context:
The `.env.example` is the operator's primary env-var reference — its header advertises itself as the template to copy before `docker compose up`, and the repo's other operator docs (CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, README.md, SPEC.md, ACCEPTANCE.md, CONTRIBUTING.md, ROADMAP.md, docs/*) defer to it for the env surface. It has drifted from the code: 9 operator-tunable `WARREN_*` env vars are read from `env`/`process.env` in non-test source but appear in NO operator-facing doc (verified absent from every file listed above via `grep -rl`). An operator cannot discover or configure these without reading source.

Most acute:
- `WARREN_SD_BINARY` is named in 3 handler error recovery hints ("set WARREN_SD_BINARY (or install sd on PATH) and restart" in src/server/handlers/plan-runs.ts, plot-plan-runs.ts, projects.ts) yet is documented nowhere an operator would look.
- `WARREN_MODEL_SONNET`/`WARREN_MODEL_OPUS` (+`_PROVIDER`) override which model 4 builtin agents (healer, pi, pr-fixer, sapling — all import `MODEL_TIERS` from src/registry/builtins/model-tiers.ts) actually call; an operator has no way to learn these exist.
- The coordinator/poller/probe disable + timeout knobs are the only way to tune or disable the corresponding background workers.

The 9 vars (each verified read-from-env in non-test source AND verified absent from all operator docs):
1. `WARREN_PLAN_RUN_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS` — src/plan-runs/config.ts `parseMergeTimeoutMs` (default `DEFAULT_PLAN_RUN_MERGE_TIMEOUT_MS`; `0` disables the merge-wait gate).
2. `WARREN_MERGE_POLLER_DISABLED` — src/server/main/detector-wiring.ts (`parseTrueEnv`; `1` disables the conversation merge poller).
3. `WARREN_PAUSE_DETECTOR_ENABLED` — src/server/main/detector-wiring.ts (`parseTrueEnv`; opt-in `1` enables the pause/respawn detector).
4. `WARREN_WORKER_PROBE_TIMEOUT_MS` — src/server/probe.ts (per-probe timeout, default 2000ms; documented only in a code comment at probe.ts:61).
5. `WARREN_SD_BINARY` — src/triggers/config.ts (sd CLI binary path; default `sd`; empty string rejected with a ValidationError).
6. `WARREN_MODEL_SONNET` — src/registry/builtins/model-tiers.ts (default `claude-sonnet-4-6`).
7. `WARREN_MODEL_SONNET_PROVIDER` — src/registry/builtins/model-tiers.ts (default `anthropic`).
8. `WARREN_MODEL_OPUS` — src/registry/builtins/model-tiers.ts (default `claude-opus-4-8`).
9. `WARREN_MODEL_OPUS_PROVIDER` — src/registry/builtins/model-tiers.ts (default `anthropic`).

Deliberately EXCLUDED (correctly undocumented — not operator-set):
- `WARREN_API_URL` and `WARREN_QUALITY_GATE` — warren-internal; injected INTO the agent sandbox by src/runs/spawn/callback-env.ts and src/runs/spawn/dispatch.ts, never read from operator env.
- `WARREN_XPROC_STDERR` — test-only (src/burrow-client/integration.cross-process.test.ts).
- `WARREN_UPDATE_GOLDENS`, `WARREN_TEST_DIALECT`, `WARREN_TEST_PG_URL` — test-only.

Note: a broader set of tuning knobs (WARREN_SCHEDULER_*, WARREN_CONVERSATION_IDLE_DISABLED, WARREN_WORKER_PROBE_DISABLED/INTERVAL_MS, WARREN_PLAN_RUN_TICK_MS/DISABLED) is also absent from `.env.example` but IS documented in SPEC.md/CLAUDE.md, so those are out of scope for this step.

sections.context: Nightwatch patrol on 2026-07-04 scanned the repo for inconsistencies, bugs, type-safety, dead code, test gaps, security, and doc drift. All quality gates are green: `bun run lint`, `bun run typecheck`, `bun test` (3084 pass, 16 pg-skip, 0 fail), and `check:dups` / `check:debt` / `check:size` / `check:deps` / `gen:docs:check` / `gen:openapi:check` / `check:ci-parity` all pass. Spot-checks of type-safety (only three production `as unknown` casts, each with a tracker ref), security (SQL is parameterized or hex-derived identifiers; all shell-outs use array-form spawn with no string interpolation), error-code consistency (all `readonly code` strings are snake_case), CLI output consistency (every command routes through `formatError` + `writeJsonLine` with exit codes 0/1/2), and time/parsing math (`parseDurationMs`, `parsePortRange`, pause budget, watchdog heartbeat — all ms-consistent with `Number.isFinite` guards) came back clean. Coverage analysis surfaced two genuine test gaps where production logic sits at 0% line coverage: (1) `src/plots/creator.ts` `defaultPlotCreator` — the production plot-creation seam wired into `ServerDeps` via `src/server/main/deps.ts` — is never exercised because the `POST /plots` handler tests (`plots.create.test.ts`) inject a mock creator, so the real create → optional editIntent → summary-with-fallbacks round-trip is untested; (2) `src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts` `steerRunHandler` and `cancelRunHandler` — the HTTP handlers for `POST /runs/:id/steer` and `POST /runs/:id/cancel` — have both handler bodies at 0% line coverage (`router.test.ts` registers the cancel route with a `noopHandler`; `src/runs/cancel.test.ts` covers the core `cancelRun` function, not the HTTP wrapper; `src/client/client.runs.test.ts` covers the client side against a stubbed fetch).
sections.behavior_invariant: External behavior must remain identical: no production source changes. The warren CLI, every HTTP API response shape and status code, the `POST /plots` create wire shape ({ id, name, status, intent_goal_preview, attachments_count, last_event_ts, last_event_actor }), the steer response shape ({ message }), the cancel response shape ({ state, alreadyTerminal, burrowRun }), and all existing 3084 tests must continue to pass. `bun run lint` and `bun run typecheck` must remain clean. Both steps add test files only — no `src/**/*.ts` production file (excluding `*.test.ts`) is modified.
sections.approach: Close the two gaps independently as small, single-PR test additions; neither step depends on the other. Step 1 adds `src/plots/creator.test.ts` exercising `defaultPlotCreator.create` against a real `UserPlotClient` over a temp `.plot/` dir (mirroring the plot-client test harness) covering: happy-path create + summary where `last_event_ts`/`last_event_actor` fall back to `plot.updated_at` / `user:<handle>` when the event tail is empty; create with a full intent patch (goal + non_goals + constraints + success_criteria) that routes through `hasIntentPatch` → `toEditIntentPatch` → `editIntent`; create with an empty/whitespace-only patch where `hasIntentPatch` returns false so `editIntent` is skipped; and the `client.close()` finally path running even when `create`/`editIntent` throws. Step 2 adds `src/server/handlers/runs.pause-resume.test.ts` exercising `steerRunHandler` and `cancelRunHandler` through the existing handler test harness (`src/server/handlers/runs.test-helpers.ts` — stub `fetch` / repos / broker) covering: steer with the required `body` field only (asserts 200 `{ message }`); steer with optional `priority` + `fromActor` forwarded into `steerRun`; cancel with an empty body (no `reason`); cancel with a `reason` forwarded; cancel of an already-terminal run (`alreadyTerminal: true` passthrough); and the 200 cancel response shape `{ state, alreadyTerminal, burrowRun }`. Both steps reuse the existing dotted-grouping test conventions and helpers so they land consistently with sibling tests.

steps.title: Add unit tests for defaultPlotCreator (src/plots/creator.ts)
steps.description:
File: src/plots/creator.ts, lines 90-117 (`defaultPlotCreator.create`), 119-125 (`hasIntentPatch`), 127-139 (`toEditIntentPatch`). Coverage: 0.00% line / 8.70% branch (uncovered 90-113, 119-123, 127-139).

Problem: `defaultPlotCreator` is the production `PlotCreator` wired into `ServerDeps.plotCreator` by `src/server/main/deps.ts` and is the real implementation behind `POST /plots`. The `POST /plots` handler tests (`src/server/handlers/plots.create.test.ts`) inject a mock creator (one test is literally `propagates creator errors as 500`), so the real create → optional `editIntent` → read+events summary round-trip is never exercised. The untested branches are load-bearing: the event-tail fallback (`tail?.at ?? plot.updated_at`, `tail?.actor ?? \`user:${input.handle}\``), the `hasIntentPatch` guard (empty/whitespace patch must skip `editIntent`), and `toEditIntentPatch`'s conditional spread + array-copy (`[...patch.non_goals]`). A regression in any of these ships undetected.

Fix: add `src/plots/creator.test.ts` that constructs `defaultPlotCreator` and drives `create()` against a real `UserPlotClient` over a temp `.plot/` directory (reuse the plot-client test harness / `mkdtemp` pattern used by sibling plot tests). Cover: (a) happy-path create returns the summary with `last_event_ts`/`last_event_actor` falling back to `plot.updated_at` / `user:<handle>` when the event tail is empty; (b) create with a full intent patch (goal + non_goals + constraints + success_criteria) asserts `editIntent` was applied (read back the plot and check `intent.goal`); (c) create with an empty patch (`{ goal: "", non_goals: [] }`) asserts `editIntent` is NOT called (intent stays at create defaults) — this is the `hasIntentPatch` false branch; (d) `client.close()` runs in the `finally` even when `create` throws (e.g. `name` empty → PlotStore rejects). Use `describe("defaultPlotCreator")` + verb-led `test(...)` per the repo convention.

Correct looks like: `bun test --coverage` shows `src/plots/creator.ts` line coverage rising from 0.00% to ≥90% and both `hasIntentPatch` branches hit. No production file is modified; only the new `src/plots/creator.test.ts` is added.

steps.title: Add HTTP-layer tests for steerRunHandler and cancelRunHandler (src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts)
steps.description:
File: src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts, lines 13-33 (`steerRunHandler`), 35-55 (`cancelRunHandler`). Coverage: 50.00% line / 14.63% branch (uncovered 14-30 and 36-53 — i.e. BOTH handler bodies).

Problem: `steerRunHandler` (`POST /runs/:id/steer`) and `cancelRunHandler` (`POST /runs/:id/cancel`) are registered routes (`src/server/handlers/index.ts:304-305`) but neither handler body is exercised by any test. `src/server/router.test.ts` registers `/runs/:id/cancel` with a `noopHandler` (route-wiring only). `src/runs/cancel.test.ts` covers the core `cancelRun` function, not the HTTP wrapper. `src/client/client.runs.test.ts` covers the WarrenClient side against a stubbed fetch. So the handler-layer work is untested: param extraction (`requireParam(ctx, "id")`), JSON body parsing (`readJsonBody` / `readJsonBodyOrEmpty`), optional-field forwarding (`priority` → `MessagePriority`, `fromActor`, `reason` — each guarded by `optionalString(...) !== undefined` spreads), the `deps.now` injection, and the 200 response shapes (`{ message }` for steer; `{ state, alreadyTerminal, burrowRun }` for cancel). A regression in the optional-field handling or response shape would not be caught.

Fix: add `src/server/handlers/runs.pause-resume.test.ts` (dotted-grouping convention, sibling to `runs.dispatch.test.ts` etc.) that builds each handler via `steerRunHandler(deps)` / `cancelRunHandler(deps)` and invokes the returned `RouteHandler` against a stubbed `ctx`, using `src/server/handlers/runs.test-helpers.ts` for the stub `fetch` / repos / broker. Cover: (a) `steerRunHandler` with only the required `body` field → 200 `{ message }`; (b) `steerRunHandler` with optional `priority` + `fromActor` → assert both are forwarded into the `steerRun` call (stub `steerRun` or assert on the stubbed fetch/burrow call); (c) `cancelRunHandler` with an empty body → no `reason` forwarded, 200 `{ state, alreadyTerminal, burrowRun }`; (d) `cancelRunHandler` with a `reason` → forwarded; (e) `cancelRunHandler` against an already-terminal run → `alreadyTerminal: true` propagates to the response. Use `describe("steerRunHandler")` / `describe("cancelRunHandler")` + verb-led `test(...)`.

Correct looks like: `bun test --coverage` shows `src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts` line coverage rising from 50.00% to 100% and branch coverage from 14.63% to ≥90% (both handler bodies and the optional-field spread branches hit). No production file is modified; only the new `src/server/handlers/runs.pause-resume.test.ts` is added.

acceptance: `bun test` passes (3084+ tests, 0 failures; the new tests are included and green)
`bun run lint` passes with `--error-on-warnings`
`bun run typecheck` passes (`tsc --noEmit`, clean)

`bun test --coverage` shows `src/plots/creator.ts` line coverage rising from 0.00% to ≥90% (`defaultPlotCreator.create`, `hasIntentPatch`, `toEditIntentPatch` all hit, both `hasIntentPatch` branches covered)

`bun test --coverage` shows `src/server/handlers/runs/pause-resume.ts` line coverage rising from 50.00% to 100% and branch coverage from 14.63% to ≥90% (both `steerRunHandler` and `cancelRunHandler` bodies exercised, optional-field spread branches covered)

sections.context: A methodical patrol scan (lint clean, typecheck clean, all 12 quality gates green, 100% line coverage on production source files) surfaced three categories of internal-hygiene issues that the existing gates do not enforce: (1) a dead barrel file and two dead exported symbols whose doc comments claim consumers that do not exist; (2) stale file-path references in comments pointing at modules that were split into subdirectories under pl-9088 / warren-041e / warren-f71c / warren-d0a9 / warren-3f46. None affect runtime behavior or the public API — the package entry src/index.ts exports only VERSION, and grep confirms none of the flagged symbols is imported anywhere in src/, scripts/, or tests. They do, however, mislead future readers (doc comments assert non-existent callers) and pollute the module surface (dead re-exports). This refactor deletes the dead code and corrects the stale path references.
sections.behavior_invariant: No public API, runtime behavior, HTTP wire shape, or test outcome changes. Specifically: (a) src/index.ts still exports only VERSION; (b) every remaining export in src/plan-runs/index.ts and src/supervisor/ still resolves to a real definition; (c) bun run check:all stays 12/12 green (lint, typecheck, check:agents, check:dups, check:deps, check:size, check:debt, check:bundle-size, gen:docs:check, gen:openapi:check, check:coverage, check:ci-parity); (d) no production import path changes — every change is either a deletion of an unimported symbol or a comment edit. The HTTP route table (ROUTE_TABLE), error envelope shapes, and golden snapshots are untouched.
sections.approach: Three independent, comment-and-deletion-only steps that each land as a single PR. No new modules, no extracted abstractions, no dependency changes, no signature changes, no behavior changes. Step 1 deletes the dead supervisor barrel. Step 2 deletes two dead plan-runs symbols (a function and an error class) plus their barrel re-exports, dropping the misleading doc blocks that claimed non-existent consumers. Step 3 rewrites stale post-split file-path references in comments to point at the current locations. The steps are unordered — none blocks another — so they may land in any sequence or in parallel.

steps.title: Delete dead src/supervisor/index.ts barrel
steps.description: src/supervisor/index.ts is a barrel re-exporting ~30 symbols from budget.ts, git-credentials.ts, main.ts, socket.ts, and token-validation.ts. It has zero importers: grep across src/, scripts/, and tests for 'supervisor/index' returns no hits; it is not re-exported from the package entry src/index.ts (which exports only VERSION); and the Dockerfile ENTRYPOINT execs src/supervisor/main.ts directly (Dockerfile:167). The file's own header says it 'exists so callers (tests, the CLI, or future programmatic consumers) can import the typed runSupervisor' — but no such caller ever materialized; supervisor tests import directly from ./main.ts etc. Delete the entire file. The relevant gates afterward are typecheck, check:deps (knip --dependencies), and check:agents; bun run check:all must stay 12/12 green.

steps.title: Remove dead isChildTerminal and PlanRunDispatchError from plan-runs
steps.description:
Two exported symbols in the plan-runs module have no callers, and their doc comments claim consumers that do not exist:

1. isChildTerminal — src/plan-runs/coordinator.ts:412-415. Its doc comment (coordinator.ts:408-411) says 'Exported for the API handler (warren-f923) to compute "is this plan-run still advancing?" without re-loading every child.' But grep across src/ + scripts/ + tests shows ZERO call sites — only the definition at coordinator.ts:412 and the barrel re-export at src/plan-runs/index.ts:28. No handler imports or invokes it.

2. PlanRunDispatchError — src/plan-runs/errors.ts:13-15, plus its doc block at errors.ts:1-11. Its doc says 'the tick loop catches it so one bad row can't tear down the coordinator.' But the tick loop catch block (src/plan-runs/tick.ts:113) catches generic unknown errors via formatError(err) and never throws or instanceof-checks PlanRunDispatchError. Grep confirms the class is never thrown, caught, instantiated, or imported anywhere outside its own definition + barrel re-export (src/plan-runs/index.ts:40).

Fix: delete the isChildTerminal function AND its 4-line doc comment in coordinator.ts; delete the PlanRunDispatchError class AND its doc comment block (errors.ts:1-11) in errors.ts; remove both from the barrel re-exports in src/plan-runs/index.ts (the isChildTerminal entry at line 28 and the PlanRunDispatchError entry at line 40). Before removing, confirm src/server/errors.ts imports only PlanHasNoOpenChildrenError, ProjectLacksPlotError, ProjectLacksSeedsError from ../plan-runs/errors.ts (it does NOT import PlanRunDispatchError). Run bun run check:all — typecheck and check:coverage are the relevant gates.

sections.context: The 2026-07-05..07 OOM crash loop was the second deploy blocker caused by warren + burrow + N sandboxes sharing one kernel and memory pool on a single Fly Machine. The strategic fix is pod-per-run on Kubernetes, where kubelet enforces resources natively and a runaway run kills its own pod, not the control plane. This plan implements the migration on a single long-lived branch (big-bang merge; main is frozen, no live users, Fly machine decommissioned). Full design is in docs/design/k8s-migration-plan.md, docs/design/runtime-provider-contract.md, and docs/design/k8s-migration.md.
sections.approach: Introduce a RuntimeProvider contract (docs/design/runtime-provider-contract.md) that the warren domain depends on, with two backends behind it: LocalProvider (wraps today's burrow socket path — self-host, macOS, local dev) and K8sProvider (new pod-per-run backend — the scale/product path on GKE Autopilot). Burrow is NOT removed; it is demoted to one provider behind the seam. This pays down the framework-lock-in the current ~50-file burrow coupling represents without re-committing it to Kubernetes. Sequencing is five phases as internal branch checkpoints, each leaving `bun run check:all` green: (1) EXTRACT the self-contained git/workspace cluster from burrow into src/workspace/ (Bun-native, no port needed); (2) CONTRACT — define the interface, implement LocalProvider wrapping current burrow behavior, and route the domain through it — CHECKPOINT 2 proves the seam reproduces today's behavior before any K8s code exists; (3) K8S — build K8sProvider (pod dispatcher, pod-watcher, init-container workspace prep, pod-log event bridge with synthesized seq, run_inbox steering, in-pod finalize reap, K8s-native admission control folding warren-b01e/ea4f); (4) RETIRE the multi-worker burrow routing (BurrowClientPool/placement/workers+burrows tables) now obsoleted by both the seam and the K8s scheduler; (5) SHIP — validate on kind/k3d, write manifests+RBAC, deploy to GKE Autopilot, docs, final green + merge. Key grounded decisions baked into the contract: two-call create collapsed to one, baseBranch promoted to a first-class field, provider-owned callback URL (no localhost co-tenancy assumption), provider-guaranteed monotonic seq (synthesized for K8s over pod logs), OOM+lost promoted to first-class terminalReason, lossless event payloads, and the finalize() seam (in-pod reap, NOT a leaky exec()) to solve the reap-vs-shared-filesystem problem pod-per-run creates. Per-step file targets and acceptance are set on each child seed's description.

alternatives.name: Full burrow removal, hard-wire K8s (design doc as originally written)
alternatives.rejected_because: Kills easy self-host + macOS + simple local dev, and replaces burrow lock-in with equally deep K8s lock-in — the exact anti-pattern the runtime contract exists to prevent.

alternatives.name: K3s on Hetzner bare metal for the hosted backend
alternatives.rejected_because: Its rationale (cost + custom runtime classes) lapsed: gVisor/Kata are deferred and LocalProvider covers cheap self-host. Self-run control plane is the least transferable ops burden; GKE Autopilot fits the bursty workload and is more credible/portable.

alternatives.name: exec(handle, argv) on the contract to bridge reap's filesystem dependency
alternatives.rejected_because: Forces a stateful kubectl-exec session into a live pod that breaks on pod/warren restart, and drags host-path + git semantics back across the seam. Replaced by the finalize() seam (in-pod reap emitting mirror deltas).

alternatives.name: K8s Jobs instead of bare Pods
alternatives.rejected_because: Job restart-on-failure re-executes the agent from scratch on OOM, which is wrong; warren's run lifecycle is already a state machine. Bare Pods with restartPolicy:Never let warren see OOMKilled and fail fast.

risks: Checkpoint 2 (step 13) is the make-or-break: if LocalProvider parity is not exact, the contract has a leak that must be fixed before any K8s work — do not proceed to phase 3 on a red checkpoint.

Reap under pod-per-run (finalize, steps 12/20): the current reap reads the workspace off a shared filesystem that pods do not provide; the in-pod finalize + mirror-delta serialization is the riskiest new design and must be proven on a real run in step 25.
seq synthesis for K8s pod logs (step 17): pod logs have no native sequence; a wrong cursor breaks event ordering, dedup, and resume. Highest-risk single K8s implementation detail.
Retire phase (22-24) has high blast radius (~50 files); it must come after checkpoint 2 so the seam has already replaced the callers.
GKE cloud-IAM/VPC surface is new to the operator; if it blocks progress, DigitalOcean/Linode managed is the documented fallback (contract makes the host portable).
acceptance: Warren dispatches, streams, steers, and reaps runs end-to-end through the RuntimeProvider seam with the domain importing neither @os-eco/burrow-cli nor @kubernetes/client-node directly.
Checkpoint 2: with WARREN_RUNTIME=local, warren reproduces today's behavior exactly and check:all is green.

A run dispatched to K8sProvider completes end-to-end on GKE Autopilot; an OOM run fails fast with terminalReason oom_killed within seconds (not the old 45-min watchdog); a steering message reaches the agent within ~5s.
Multi-worker routing (BurrowClientPool, placement.ts, workers + burrows tables) is deleted; supervisor and docker-compose survive only as the LocalProvider self-host path.
The migration branch merges to main with check:all green and coverage floors held.
