sections.context: docs/PHILOSOPHY.md (Amendment 2026-07-17, operating rule 8) declares that plot, conversations (brainstorming/chat/Leveret), and canopy fail the prior test — they have no users — and are to be deleted outright, not re-platformed as extensions. This is sequencing step 2 of the philosophy's standing order; step 1 (burrow-client eviction, pl-829f) is effectively landed. The payoff: ServerDeps shrinks by ~15-18 fields in one stroke (the twelve plot injector fields, planRunPlotAppender, planRunPlotActivator, planSynthesizer, mergePoller, conversationIdleDetector, canopyConfig), RuntimeProvider.finalize() stops enumerating plot, and the agent registry collapses to self-contained built-ins. Scouted scale: conversations touch ~90 files (~40 whole-file deletions, ~10-11k LOC incl. tests), plot ~150 files (~15-17k LOC, only ~10 needing surgical edits), canopy ~1.3k LOC library tier + ~1k LOC shared/project tier + ~2.2k test LOC. Deletion order conversations → plot → canopy is dependency-driven: conversation code calls plotCreator/plotSyncer and stores conversations.plot_id, and the constitutional Audit Warden mechanism (standing Leveret conversation + meta-Plot) leans on both.
sections.approach: Three phases matching the mandated order, each a sequence of PR-sized child seeds that leave `bun run check:all` green — mechanical doc regeneration (gen:openapi, gen:docs, AGENTS.md path fixes, prefix-array parity per warren-abaa) happens inside the code step that breaks it; narrative docs (SPEC, README, CLAUDE.md) get a per-phase sweep step. SPEC.md is amended, not excised: retired sections receive the house-style '> **RETIRED — superseded by …**' banner with the original text preserved verbatim as the V1 design record (exemplar at SPEC.md:249-262). DB removal follows the append-only drizzle convention — new forward drop migrations in both dialects (sqlite + postgres), serialized across steps to avoid journal-number conflicts. Phase A (conversations): first re-point the Audit Warden digest sink off POST /conversations/:id/messages and amend docs/CONSTITUTION.md, then delete backend (src/runs/conversation-*, stream/conversation-turn, handlers, 6 routes, detector wiring, RUN_MODES 'conversation', conversation.idleTimeoutMs config), drop conversations/messages tables, delete UI (relocating the shared DispatchPlanButton out of conversation-detail/ first), sweep docs. Phase B (plot): peel from the edges in — remove plan-run↔plot bridges and the plot-plan-run synthesizer, extract plot from RuntimeProvider.finalize()/reap/spawn on BOTH providers (local + k8s), then delete the core (src/plots/, src/plot-client/, handlers/plots/, twelve ServerDeps fields, plotSync config, @os-eco/plot-cli from package.json + Dockerfile), drop the DB surface (plots table, runs.plot_id, plan_runs.plot_id, projects.has_plot), delete UI, sweep docs and close obsoleted issues. Phase C (canopy): key grounded decision — BOTH the library tier (CANOPY_REPO_URL clone path) and the project tier (.canopy/ scanning, compose.ts, CanopyClient/cn shell-out) die; the surviving registry is src/registry/builtins/ + schema.ts, seeded at boot with no external binary. Delete library tier first (clone.ts, config.ts, refreshAgentRegistry, POST /agents/refresh, register-agent CLI, doctor/readyz canopy checks), then project tier + registry collapse (agents.resolve() → get(), agents.project_id drop migration, cn out of the Dockerfile), then UI + docs. A final cross-cutting step rewrites the bundled-features narrative (warren CLAUDE.md 'bundles five os-eco tools' → mulch/seeds/sapling, README, AGENTS.md, root os-eco CLAUDE.md/README where they overstate 'the substrate warren uses'), and updates docs/PHILOSOPHY.md — sequencing item 2 marked landed with this plan's id, mirroring how item 1 cites pl-829f. Per-step file targets and acceptance live on each child seed's description. Extension (rev 2, 2026-07-21): PHILOSOPHY sequencing step 3 adopted into this plan as steps 16-18 — warren-bb60 (Tier-1 observation event bus on RunEventBroker, warren-ext/v1 versioned payloads), warren-4e74 (healer re-homed as proof consumer), warren-df3e (mulch/seeds mirrors evicted from finalize() so the contract stops enumerating features). Gated on step 8 so the extension surface is cut against the post-deletion kernel. Cron-trigger rip-out deliberately left out pending a rule-8 check on whether the scheduler has users.

alternatives.name: Re-platform the three features behind the extension API instead of deleting
alternatives.rejected_because: PHILOSOPHY rule 8 forbids it explicitly: a feature with no users can't pay for a seam, so building extension API to carry it is speculative abstraction. Deletion keeps the door open — any of these can return as an extension when someone wants it enough to pay for the API it needs.

alternatives.name: Delete only canopy's library tier, keep the project .canopy/ tier
alternatives.rejected_because: The two tiers share CanopyClient, refresh.ts, compose.ts, and the cn shell-out; a library-only cut leaves ~1k LOC of canopy plumbing plus the Dockerfile cn install alive for a tier that also has no users. Rule 8 applies to both; Tier-0 in-repo skills are the sanctioned home for per-project agent customization.

alternatives.name: Excise retired SPEC.md sections outright
alternatives.rejected_because: SPEC.md is the V1 design record; the established convention (SPEC.md:249-262) is a RETIRED banner with the body preserved verbatim. Excision would destroy the historical record and diverge from house style.

alternatives.name: One mega-PR for the whole pass
alternatives.rejected_because: ~25-30k LOC across ~250 files spanning schema migrations, runtime contract surgery, and doc regeneration. Unreviewable, unbisectable, and a single failure blocks everything. Phase checkpoints each leaving check:all green are the pl-829f house pattern.

alternatives.name: Keep the Audit Warden standing conversation until a replacement design exists
alternatives.rejected_because: It would block the entire pass on a design project for a mechanism whose substrate (conversations + meta-Plot) is mandated for deletion. Re-pointing digests at seeds issues (the sink gatewatch already uses) is a small, honest step 1.

sections.context: Today is 2026-07-27, Week 1 Day 1 of the Q3 campaign, with a Show HN launch targeted for Sun 2026-08-16. Engineering is roughly four weeks ahead of the master plan (conversations + plot both fully deleted in Week 0, net -28,978 LOC, ServerDeps 40 -> 28), but the distribution track has not started. Five audits on 2026-07-27 found the gap is not infrastructure, it is exposure-readiness: (1) warren has ZERO HTTP response-body redaction anywhere - src/server/main/redact.ts is pino log redaction only - so GET /runs today returns prompt, renderedAgentJson (the full system prompt), per-run cost and an instance-wide all-time spend total; (2) GET /readyz publishes WARREN_API_TOKEN.length plus filesystem paths and raw DB driver errors including host/port/user; (3) src/server/errors.ts forwards raw Error.message on every 500, so subprocess stderr escapes from any route; (4) the UI embeds the raw bearer token in a clickable href via buildPreviewLoginUrl; (5) GET /runs/:id/inbox is destructive on read and would let anonymous callers drain steering queues. Separately, nothing public exists to point at: no container image is published anywhere (docker-compose builds from source, so the advertised 5-minute self-host is a multi-minute compile), README claims version 0.9.10 and ships a Client SDK example calling listPlots()/getPlot() which no longer exist, ROADMAP.md is a frozen May-2026 artifact with 74 mentions of canopy and zero mentions of k8s, plan-runs, seams, or the event bus, and CHANGELOG [Unreleased] is empty while 16 merged PRs sit unreleased. Finally, autonomous agents keep drifting the wire-type layer because AGENTS.md:209-211 actively instructs them to keep a separate UI type copy: RunFailureReason is missing finalize_failed and evicted in BOTH surface copies, ui/api/types.ts still types the deleted mode 'interactive', and RefreshAgentsResponse.removed is typed {name:string}[] against a server truth of string[]. src/ui (10,904 LOC) is excluded from biome, check:size, check:debt and knip, which is why none of it was caught.
sections.approach: Three tracks in one plan, forward-chained so the long pole starts immediately and the cheap high-visibility work runs in parallel. PHASE 0 (security, steps 1-4) fixes four live disclosure/DoS bugs that are defects on the current private instance regardless of any demo, and step 1 is a hard prerequisite for the projection work. PHASE B1 (release machinery, steps 5-9) makes 'bump the version and everything happens' true - version-bump script, a version-sync gate, the two generated-artifact gates that are in check:all but missing from CI, GHCR publication with semver tags, and release-job hardening - then proves it by cutting v0.11.0 at checkpoint step 10. PHASE A (public instance, steps 11-22) is the critical path to Aug 16: widen AuthOk into a capability-carrying Actor (pure refactor, no behavior change), add a third env-selected AuthProvider implementation, classify every route, then build the response projections and event scrubber that are the actual work, then the UI capability layer, Cloud Armor, an automated leak-regression scenario, and finally the DB cutover and public deploy at checkpoint step 22. PHASE B2 (docs, steps 23-25) and PHASE B3 (SSOT gates, steps 26-31) run alongside. Read-only is deliberately built as the AuthProvider seam rather than a WARREN_READ_ONLY boolean: PHILOSOPHY rule 1 says features pay for seams and the public instance is a real feature paying for a seam already on the roadmap (sequencing step 4), while rule 7 forbids exactly the boolean-conditional shape. Public-instance product scope is 'warren as it is, minus dispatch': anonymous browsing with no token paste, runs/projects/agents/plan-runs and the LIVE event stream all visible, per-run cost deliberately shown because cost-per-merged-PR is the campaign's ownable metric, with renderedAgentJson, localPath, burrowId and the instance-wide cost rollup redacted.

Retained as defense-in-depth alongside Cloud Armor, not as the mechanism.

alternatives.name: Publish a scoped read-only bearer token on the login page instead of true anonymous access
alternatives.rejected_because: Saves 1-2 days by leaving AuthGate untouched, but a demo link that opens a password box loses most of its traffic. Kept as the documented fallback if step 19 slips.

Reusing app.warren.run as the public instance needs zero CI/repo changes; the reverse needs 1-2 days of manifest surgery plus a new global IP and cert provisioning.

alternatives.rejected_because: Reaffirms mulch decision mx-834a3a: 8 of 12 CLI commands only work in-container (they need the local sqlite and burrow socket), so a published package fails confusingly for most installers. 'One container' is also a cleaner distribution claim. The bin field stays (it names the binary on clone/link); README and CONTRIBUTING stop implying a global install.

alternatives.rejected_because: CHANGELOG.md is already 250 KB / 4,743 lines and most commits are agent PRs that do not deserve a line; per-commit enforcement makes the bloat worse. risks: Redaction is the critical path and has no prior art in the codebase - src/server/main/redact.ts is pino-only and no handler has ever projected a response. Steps 14-16 are the highest-uncertainty estimates in the plan; if they slip, fall back to the published read-only token posture (alternatives entry 3) and ship anonymous browsing after launch.

events.payload_json is raw agent transcript - tool_use shell command lines, tool_result file contents, stack traces. The scrubber in step 16 catches known key shapes (sk-ant-, ghp_, github_pat_, AKIA, bearer headers) but an agent echoing a novel secret into a stack trace lands verbatim in a public stream. The org allowlist (step 17) is the structural mitigation: everything on the instance is a public repo. If step 16 cannot be made confident, launch with the event stream limited to terminal runs and add live-follow after.

A misconfigured public instance that registers a private repo is the worst possible outcome. Every default must fail closed: resolveAuth already throws when no token is set, and step 12 must preserve that - a missing or unparseable WARREN_AUTH value must never degrade to public.

GET /runs/:id/inbox is destructive on read (it atomically flips unread to delivered). If it ever slips into the public allowlist, anonymous callers silently drain steering queues - an availability bug, not just a leak. Step 13 must assert this in a test, and step 21 must cover it.

src/db/url.ts:76-79 treats an unrecognized DSN scheme as a bare SQLite path, so a typo during the step 22 cutover yields a silently-empty local database rather than a boot failure. Verify the dialect through /readyz's db_reachable check immediately post-cutover, and keep the existing database untouched as a one-key rollback.

AUTO_MERGE_PAT is a silent single point of failure for the whole pipeline: GitHub suppresses workflow runs from GITHUB_TOKEN-authored pushes, so if that PAT expires, merges to main stop triggering releases with no failed run - just nothing happening. Step 9 should add an expiry check or a heartbeat.

The warren-cb81 workflow_call chain in release.yml is correct and regression-guarded by scripts/deploy-trigger.test.ts. Step 9 must not 'simplify' it into a release: [published] trigger - the test will fail, and correctly.

The control plane is a single replica with strategy Recreate (SSE stickiness plus an RWO PVC), so scaling out under a Show HN spike is not available. Cloud Armor (step 20) and the stream cap (step 4) are the only mitigations.

Step 29 brings 10,904 previously-unlinted LOC under biome and the size ratchet; ui/api/types.ts is 693 lines against a 500-line budget. It must land after step 26 hoists shared types out, and needs a grandfather pass rather than a mass rewrite.
Deletions and rewrites land while the world starts watching. main must stay releasable throughout; every step in this plan leaves bun run check:all green.
acceptance: An anonymous request to app.warren.run can browse runs, run detail, the live event stream, projects, agents and plan-runs with no token, and receives 403 on every POST and DELETE.

No anonymous response body contains renderedAgentJson, localPath, burrowId, previewFailureMessage, an instance-wide cost rollup, a bearer token, a filesystem path, or a raw driver/subprocess error message; per-run costUsd and the user prompt are deliberately present.

GET /readyz, GET /metrics, GET /analytics/cost, GET /runs/:id/inbox, GET /runs/:id/finalize-intent, GET /projects/:id/triggers and GET /projects/:id/warren-config all answer 401 or 403 anonymously, asserted by an automated acceptance scenario that runs in CI.

The public instance holds only allowlisted-org public repositories, enforced at boot and at project registration, and a missing or unparseable WARREN_AUTH value fails closed rather than degrading to public.

Bumping the version in one place produces, with no further human action: synced version strings across package.json, src/index.ts, docs/openapi.yaml and README; a git tag; a GitHub release whose notes come from a CHANGELOG section that must exist; a ghcr.io image tagged with semver; and a GKE rollout verified by a post-deploy /version check.

sections.context: SPEC.md (repo root, 2,976 lines) is the V1 design record, frozen at 'Status: Design phase, last updated 2026-05-13' in a repo now at v0.13.x. A full audit found ~43% of it is retired-feature tombstones (plot, canopy, multi-worker, PR-close webhook), ~10% actively contradicts the current code (§12 calls canopy a hard dependency; claims 3 built-in agents vs the actual 8; §8.1 lists ~17 routes vs the live 39; §7's project tree is a fossil), and it stopped being a living spec — the last new section landed 2026-06-20 and new capabilities since (healer, k8s, analytics) went to CLAUDE.md and docs/design/ instead. The maintainer has decided: delete it. The ~35% that is unique live contract/rationale gets salvaged into dated-topic design records under docs/design/ (the established pattern: k8s-migration.md, runtime-provider-contract.md). An inventory sweep found 228 literal references plus ~30 bare-'§' citations that a naive grep misses; two quality gates (check:prose via scripts/prose-budgets.json, check:agents via AGENTS.md links) hard-fail the moment the file is deleted, so the deletion step must land its reference rewrites in the same commit. At plan end: zero references to warren's SPEC.md remain anywhere in the repo (including bare-'§' citations that meant warren's SPEC), cross-repo SPEC references (../burrow/SPEC.md, ../seeds/SPEC.md, burrow §15.6) are untouched, and the salvaged design records faithfully carry the live contracts that SPEC.md was the sole prose home for (preview §11.L/§11.M, plan-runs §11.P/§11.R, config §11.H, scheduler §11.I, runtime/supervisor §3.3/§5.1-5.3/§9/§10.3/§11.A, composition §4/§11.K, security §11.D, acceptance §3.1/§11.E-G).
sections.approach:
Three phases: SALVAGE (steps 1-8, parallel-safe) lifts each live contract cluster out of SPEC.md into a topic-named record under docs/design/ (matching the existing undated style of k8s-migration.md / runtime-provider-contract.md) or into ACCEPTANCE.md / SECURITY.md where that is the natural home. Salvage is a faithful lift-and-condense of rationale, NOT a rewrite — preserve the decision text, drop only the RETIRED-bannered mass, and note 'Salvaged from SPEC.md (deleted); see git history for the V1-era original' in each new record's header. SWEEP (steps 9-14) rewrites every reference to point at the new homes, using the mapping table below. DELETE (step 15) removes SPEC.md plus its prose-budget entries and runs final verification.

=== REFERENCE-TARGET MAPPING (the contract every sweep step follows) ===
- §11.L, §11.M -> docs/design/preview-environments.md
- §11.P, §11.R -> docs/design/plan-run-coordinator.md (also fixes the §10.4 nonexistent-section cite)

sections.context: Cross-repo plan-run routing (pl-fb43, warren-aed2) shipped steps 1-6 in late June 2026: resolveTargetProject (src/projects/resolve-target.ts), the seedProjectId split in the spawn path, {seed_body} prompt injection (src/runs/dispatch-prompt.ts), per-child routing in the plan-run coordinator, the execution_project_id column (both DB dialects + UI Repo column), and the extensions.repo key in src/seeds-cli/warren-extensions.ts. Owner decision 2026-07-31: excise it entirely. Reasons: (1) the feature is seeds-bound — the routing key lives in seeds extensions.repo and the coordination unit is an sd plan — while ROADMAP Next #3 (IssueTracker, Linear first) demotes seeds to implementation #1 and will re-express any routing tracker-agnostically; (2) it has no payer — the kota-monorepo workflow that motivated it is no longer the owner's workflow, and no external user has asked for it (external demand points at GitHub/Linear/Jira trackers, e.g. issue #662); (3) tested-but-dormant code taxes the spawn path, the most critical path in the system, with a dual-project mental model every future dispatch change must hold. PHILOSOPHY rule 8: delete rather than re-platform. Same pattern as pl-3a79. A 2026-07-31 read-only audit confirmed the exact blast radius: routing lives in src/plan-runs/{coordinator,dispatch,in-flight}.ts, src/runs/spawn/{types,dispatch,util}.ts, src/runs/dispatch-prompt.ts, src/projects/resolve-target.ts, src/seeds-cli/warren-extensions.ts, src/db/schema/{columns,sqlite,postgres}.ts, src/ui/src/pages/plan-run-detail/child-table.tsx, src/ui/src/pages/PlanRunDetail.tsx, src/ui/src/pages/RunDetail.tsx, and the plan_run.* event payloads. {seed_body} is included in the sweep: its only production caller is the plan-run coordinator (coordinator.ts:308), the single-run path never adopted it, and its crossRepo auto-inject only fires under the deleted routing — the pattern is trivial to rebuild when IssueTracker needs it.
sections.behavior_invariant: The default single-project path stays byte-identical at every step: a run or plan-run whose seed lives in its execution project behaves exactly as it did before pl-fb43, end to end (dispatch, prompt rendering, reap, PR, events). All tests that do not reference the deleted routing machinery stay green unmodified; tests that exist solely to cover routing (coordinator.routing.test.ts, resolve-target.test.ts, the routing cases in dispatch.test.ts) are deleted with the feature. bun run verify is green at the end of every step, and the GKE deployment migrates cleanly: the execution_project_id column drop ships as a normal drizzle migration in BOTH dialects. No other behavior changes — this plan removes code, it does not add or alter any surviving behavior.
sections.approach: Consumers-first, strictly forward-chained: each step removes the callers of the machinery the next step deletes, so the tree compiles and bun run verify passes after every merge. Order: (1) strip routing from the plan-run coordinator/dispatch layer — the only production consumers of resolveTargetProject, seedProjectId, and crossRepo; (2) revert the dispatch-prompt builder to the legacy {seed_id}-only replace and delete the module; (3) un-thread seedProjectId from the spawn path; (4) delete the now-unused resolver module and the extensions.repo schema key; (5) remove the UI surface (Repo column, coordination labels, RunDetail note) while the API still returns the field; (6) drop the execution_project_id column from both dialects plus the API response and regenerate the API docs; (7) bookkeeping — ROADMAP tombstone + IssueTracker design-input line + final full-gate verification. Steps are sized for a single agent each; none should exceed ~300 lines of net deletion plus test updates.

sections.context: ROADMAP.md 'Now' carries 'Agent-facing CLI + npm publish [plan: not yet filed]'. The design is already locked in docs/design/2026-07-29-planning-session-record.md §3: an 8-step sequence backed by measured evidence (3 HTTP clients / 1,295 lines; 4 copies of the wire response envelopes with 8 live drifts; 15 hand-rolled poll loops; 21 sleeps; 3 disagreeing event-payload parsers; ~215 lines of plan-run logic trapped in a handler; a split-brain CLI where only the plan group is remote; @os-eco/warren-cli 404s on npm with no files/publishConfig/exports/workflow). Owner decisions D1-D6 are made and not to be relitigated: one npm package (D1); UI shares types only, keeps its own HTTP client (D2); the CLI collapses onto HTTP — a local user is a remote user pointed at localhost; genuinely-local remainder is serve, db migrate-to-postgres, half of doctor (D3); warren run keeps its name (D4); client config holds base URL + token only, never a DB credential (D5); durations render 4.2s/3.1m/1.4h (D6). Serverless warren run is killed. Step 5 of the plan IS AgentRuntimeAdapter phase-1 item 10 (one event-envelope extractor in src/core, three consumers) — extract, don't re-plan. The docker-build CI gate (v0.13.0, warren-3380) unblocked the npm publish step. Agents are the primary consumer of this CLI: the surface must be scriptable (machine output everywhere), pollable (wait/tail), and self-priming (warren prime + an AGENTS.md snippet, exactly how sd prime and ml prime make seeds and mulch discoverable to agents).
sections.approach: Forward-chained in three waves. Wave 1 (steps 1-8) is single-source consolidation that the CLI then stands on: fix the live drift bugs, move the response envelopes into src/core/wire.ts so check:wire-types guards them for free, build the one event-envelope extractor in src/core with the three domain parsers (terminal-detect, usage-aggregate, provider-error) as consumers, layer typed usage readers on it, complete the SDK (cancelRun and the shared envelope types), move plan-run logic to domain, and de-sleep the acceptance harness onto waitForRun. Wave 2 (steps 9-12) is the CLI itself: collapse run/add-project onto HTTP per D3, then define the agent-facing output contract (global --output with NDJSON default, stable exit codes, D6 durations) before adding the new commands show/wait/tail/cancel and the session-bootstrap pair login/prime. prime is modeled directly on sd prime / ml prime: it emits the command reference, env contract, and workflows an agent needs, and ships with the AGENTS.md snippet that tells agents to run it — discoverability is part of the deliverable, not an afterthought. Wave 3 (steps 13-14) makes it public: the generated CLI reference (warren-1caf) so the surface cannot drift from the code, then npm publish infra (files, publishConfig, exports['./client'], a publish job slotted into release.yml's draft→image→promote needs-chain with npm-view idempotency) plus the doc truth pass and the on-the-record reversal of mulch decision mx-834a3a. Every step leaves check:all green; scenario 39 stays green throughout.
