alternatives.rejected_because: Owner decision D1: one package. Fleet precedent is 8/8 single-package, and Node can't load .ts from node_modules, so the split buys a build matrix without buying a consumer.

alternatives.name: Share one HTTP client between CLI/SDK and the UI
alternatives.rejected_because: Owner decision D2: duplicated transport is cheap; duplicated truth is what bit us. The UI keeps its own client and re-exports shared types. This is also why warren-53a7 (NDJSON parser merge) is deliberately not adopted into this plan.

alternatives.name: Keep a serverless local-SQLite warren run path
alternatives.rejected_because: Killed by the sequencing doc (D3). A local user is a remote user pointed at localhost; the split-brain CLI is the bug, not a feature. Genuinely-local remainder: serve, db migrate-to-postgres, half of doctor.

alternatives.name: Stay container-only (standing decision mx-834a3a)
alternatives.rejected_because: ROADMAP ring 1 (the solo self-hoster) requires 'the CLI installs from npm'. The decision predates the agent-facing CLI direction and the docker-build gate; step 14 overturns it explicitly via ml record rather than silently contradicting it.

steps.title: Single-source truth sweep: dead /agents/refresh caller, readFrontmatter UI sites, false dups-allowlist why-strings
Move HTTP response envelopes into src/core/wire.ts and widen check:wire-types DOMAIN_STEMS with project and seed
Acceptance harness adopts SDK waitForRun; at most one sleep remains
One event-envelope extractor in src/core; terminal-detect, usage-aggregate, and provider-error consume it
Typed usage readers over the core envelope extractor (usageShape), pi-wins tiebreak preserved
SDK completion: cancelRun, version probe, and re-exported core envelope types
Plan-run orchestration logic moves from the handler into the src/plan-runs domain
CLI collapses onto HTTP: run and add-project go remote per D3; client config resolution per D5
Agent-facing output contract: global --output ndjson|json|pretty, stable exit codes, D6 durations
New commands: warren show, warren wait, warren tail, warren cancel
warren login and warren prime: agent session bootstrap modeled on sd prime / ml prime, plus the AGENTS.md snippet
npm publish: files/publishConfig/exports, release.yml publish job behind the image, mx-834a3a reversal, doc truth pass

risks: RunDetail.tsx summarizeEvent/piSubKind/extractReapSummary have zero test coverage — the one envelope consumer that can silently drift while the extractor lands. Pin before moving, or scope the extractor to the three tested domain parsers only.

src/ui/tsconfig.app.json includes ../core/wire.ts at file granularity; any new src/core module the UI imports fails the UI build with TS6307, and only bun run build:ui catches it (root typecheck skips src/ui).

The check:all manifest is frozen (byte-identical to the l5-toolkit template). Any new publish/CLI-reference gate must ride inside lint or stay CI-only like docker-build — it cannot take a manifest slot.

npm publishes are effectively irreversible. The publish job needs npm-view idempotency (exact name @os-eco/warren-cli per mx-be6bc5) and must sit in release.yml's needs-chain after deploy so an npm version can never exist without its ghcr image.
Standing mulch decision mx-834a3a ('warren is not published to npm') must be overturned via ml record in step 14, not silently contradicted.

Collapsing warren run onto HTTP changes host-side semantics (it currently spawns locally). The container/supervisor path and warren serve must keep working; doctor splits into client-side and server-side halves per D3.
package.json bin points at raw bun-shebang TypeScript. Fleet precedent (burrow-cli) says publish it as-is with engines.bun — do not invent a build step; document the bun requirement instead.
acceptance: On a machine with only bun installed, npm i -g @os-eco/warren-cli yields working warren and wr binaries that drive a remote warren over WARREN_BASE_URL/WARREN_API_TOKEN; no remote-capable command opens local SQLite (D3), and the published tarball contains src/ only (no .seeds/, deploy/, scripts/, docs/).

Every CLI command emits machine-parseable output (NDJSON default on stdout, --output json|pretty opt-in) with stable documented exit codes; warren run against a remote host completes dispatch→tail→terminal without EROFS.
warren prime emits agent session context (command reference, env contract, workflows) the way sd prime and ml prime do, and the README/AGENTS.md snippet telling agents to run it ships with it.

Exactly one event-envelope extractor exists, in src/core; terminal-detect, usage-aggregate, and provider-error import it; the origin==='agent' provenance gate and the nested message.stopReason fallback hold in all three; all existing pinning tests stay green.
check:wire-types guards the HTTP response envelopes (project and seed stems in DOMAIN_STEMS); import { WarrenClient } from '@os-eco/warren-cli/client' resolves for external consumers.

The npm publish job rides release.yml's draft→image→promote needs-chain: no npm version is ever published without the matching ghcr image, and re-running the workflow on an already-published version is a no-op.
bun run check:all passes at every step's merge, and acceptance scenario 39 stays green throughout.

sections.context: ROADMAP Next item 6 pulled into Now. The Tier-1 lifecycle bus is live and observe-only, but every consumer today is compiled into src/server/main/lifecycle-bus-wiring.ts. There is no loader, no package format, no delivery mechanism across a process boundary, and no distribution channel. ROADMAP forbids designing that mechanism on speculation: build one first-party extension out-of-core, packaged exactly as a third party would package theirs, and let the friction write the spec. The audit log is the chosen flagship (ROADMAP 'Deliberately not in core', old R-16, amended 2026-08-03 so actor kind suffices for attribution): zero external dependencies, deterministic to test, and brutally demanding on delivery guarantees — an audit log that drops events is worthless, so it forces the durability/cursor/catch-up questions the eventual delivery mechanism must answer. v0 builds against warren's EXISTING HTTP surfaces only (PHILOSOPHY rule 5: data formats are API) with zero audit-specific lines in warren core. The design record is docs/design/extensions.md (provisional, pre-spec) and FRICTION.md in the extension is the primary design artifact feeding the future manifest/loader/delivery spec.
sections.approach: Build extensions/audit-log/ as a fully standalone Bun package inside the warren repo: own package.json, own lockfile, own tests, own container image, no imports from src/ in either direction, boundary enforced by check:layers rules landed in the same PR as the scaffold (PHILOSOPHY rule 4: a seam is not done until a gate enforces it). The extension is a collector-store-exporter pipeline: (1) a cursor-tailing collector polls GET /runs and tails per-run NDJSON event streams with a durable cursor in its own SQLite, at-least-once; (2) a normalizer maps lifecycle facts into append-only audit rows with idempotent apply so replays are exact no-ops; (3) a small HTTP surface exports GET /audit-log.jsonl?since= plus /healthz. Every place the HTTP-tail approach hurts (hand-derived wire types from openapi.yaml, missing actor attribution, no global stream, per-run tail fan-out, restart catch-up) is logged in FRICTION.md as it happens — that document is the spec input for the delivery mechanism, the manifest, and the PLUGIN_* env contract. Chosen over designing the loader first because ROADMAP item 6 explicitly forbids speculative mechanism design; chosen over a bus-side core forwarder because that would put delivery-mechanism code into core before the friction is known.

alternatives.name: Design the manifest/loader/delivery mechanism first, then build the extension against it
alternatives.rejected_because: ROADMAP Next item 6 explicitly forbids it: 'Do not design that mechanism on speculation.' The friction from a real out-of-core build becomes the spec. Designing first inverts that and risks freezing a wrong contract (PHILOSOPHY rule 6: API churn kills server-side plugin ecosystems).

alternatives.name: Core audit_log table plus a core writer on the lifecycle bus
alternatives.rejected_because: ROADMAP 'Deliberately not in core': a core audit_log table would make the same data twice, and the litmus test says a feature that observes the run lifecycle is an extension. Also violates the session's success criterion of zero audit-specific lines in core.

alternatives.name: In-process Tier-2 subscriber registered in lifecycle-bus-wiring.ts
alternatives.rejected_because: That is the compiled-in mechanism the flagship exists to replace. It proves nothing about packaging, versioning, or third-party loading, and adds another hardcoded consumer to the array.

alternatives.name: Slack notification sink as the flagship instead
alternatives.rejected_because: Needs an external workspace and webhook credentials, so it cannot run deterministically in tests or CI, and a dropped notification is shrugged off — it never forces the durability and cursor questions the delivery mechanism must answer. Dropped by owner decision 2026-08-04.

steps.title: Scaffold extensions/audit-log/ as a standalone package and enforce the boundary with check:layers
steps.description: Create extensions/audit-log/ as a fully standalone Bun package: its own package.json (name @os-eco/warren-audit-log, private: true for now, scripts: test, typecheck, lint, start), its own tsconfig.json (strict: true, noUncheckedIndexedAccess: true, module/moduleResolution bundler-style matching warren root), its own bun.lock (run bun install inside the directory), src/main.ts entry that prints a startup line and exits 0, a placeholder src/main.test.ts, and a README.md stub. It is NOT a root workspace member — root package.json has no workspaces field; keep it that way. Boundary enforcement, landed in this same change (PHILOSOPHY rule 4): (a) extend the walk in scripts/check-layers.ts to also walk extensions/ when the directory exists — a generic one-line-ish addition beside the existing walk of src/, skipping node_modules and dist; (b) add two rules to scripts/layer-rules.json: rule extensions-are-out-of-core with from ["extensions/"], forbidImports ["src/", "scripts/"], why: an extension consumes warren over HTTP wire formats only, never source imports — it must build and run from a clone of its own directory alone; and rule core-never-imports-extensions with from ["src/", "scripts/"], forbidImports ["extensions/"], why: zero extension-specific lines in core is the flagship success criterion; empty allow lists on both. Add a check-layers test case if the existing test suite (scripts/check-layers.test.ts or similar) covers rules, proving a synthetic cross-boundary import fails. Root gate hygiene so root bun run check:all stays green with the new tree: biome.json files block must exclude extensions/ (the extension lints itself with its own biome config or none for now), .jscpd.json exclude extensions/, knip.json ignore extensions/ (it is not part of the root dependency graph), and confirm check:size and check:debt walks only cover src/ and scripts/ (they do — no change expected, verify). check:agents: this step does not edit AGENTS.md, so no doc changes needed. Exit criteria: root bun run check:all green; cd extensions/audit-log && bun install && bun test passes; a deliberate test import of ../../src/index.ts from the extension makes bun run check:layers fail (demonstrate in the check-layers test, not committed as a live violation).

steps.title: Collector: cursor-tailing client over warren's HTTP API with durable resume
steps.description: Inside extensions/audit-log/ only (the layer gate forbids src/ imports). Read docs/openapi.yaml at the repo root as documentation and hand-derive the minimal local wire types the collector needs (runs list rows, run detail, event rows: seq, kind, stream, at). Create FRICTION.md in the extension root now and log every papercut as it happens — hand-deriving types that src/core/wire.ts already owns is itself the first friction entry; this file is the primary design artifact of the whole plan. Implement src/collector.ts: (1) poll GET /runs on an interval (env WARREN_POLL_MS, default 5000) with Authorization: Bearer $WARREN_API_TOKEN against $WARREN_BASE_URL, both env vars required at startup with a clear exit-1 message when missing; (2) discover runs it has not finished consuming and tail each run's event stream endpoint (see docs/http-api.md for the exact route — the per-run NDJSON/SSE tail the UI uses) from the last durable seq; (3) persist cursors in the extension's own SQLite database via bun:sqlite at $AUDIT_DATA_DIR/audit.db (env AUDIT_DATA_DIR, default ./data), one row per run: run_id, last_seq, terminal_seen; plus a global runs-list watermark; (4) semantics are at-least-once — after a crash anywhere, restart re-reads from the durable cursor and MAY re-deliver, never skips; downstream apply (step 3) is idempotent. Emit collected facts as an in-process typed stream (a callback or async iterator boundary) so step 3 consumes facts without knowing HTTP. Tests: an in-process fake warren built on Bun.serve serving fixture runs and event streams — cover auth header sent, pagination/watermark advance, tail resume from mid-stream seq after a simulated restart, terminal run cleanup, and 401/500 backoff (simple exponential, capped). Do not import anything from warren src/. Exit criteria: extension bun test green; FRICTION.md has at least the wire-types entry; collector survives kill-and-restart in a test without losing or double-finishing a run.

steps.title: Audit store and normalization: append-only rows, idempotent replay
steps.description: Map collected facts into an append-only audit table in the same SQLite database. Actions for v0, derived from what the HTTP surface actually exposes: run.dispatched (run row first seen, carries project_id, agent name, branch, trigger), run.started (queued-to-running transition observed), run.terminal (one per run, with outcome succeeded|failed|cancelled and failure cause when present), branch.pushed (from the run's terminal/reap facts: branch, commits ahead), pr.opened (PR URL present after reap), run.steered (steering/inbox event kinds observed in the event stream). Schema: audit_log(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, at TEXT ISO-8601, action TEXT, run_id TEXT, project_id TEXT, actor_kind TEXT NULL, dedupe_key TEXT, metadata TEXT JSON) with UNIQUE(run_id, action, dedupe_key) and INSERT OR IGNORE so at-least-once delivery from step 2 lands exactly-once in the table; dedupe_key is the event seq where the action derives from one event, or a constant for once-per-run actions. actor_kind stays NULL in v0 — the HTTP surface does not expose it; log that gap in FRICTION.md as a named payload-enrichment requirement for the real delivery mechanism (ties to warren-3754 ActorKind hoist). Table is append-only by construction: no UPDATE or DELETE statement anywhere except the retention prune added in step 4. Tests: golden-style fixture stream replayed twice produces byte-identical table contents; each action derivation covered; malformed/unknown event kinds are counted and skipped, never fatal. Exit criteria: extension bun test green; replay-twice test proves idempotency; FRICTION.md gains the attribution-gap entry and any event-kind ambiguities found while mapping.

steps.title: Export and health surface: GET /audit-log.jsonl, /healthz, retention
steps.description: Give the extension its own small HTTP surface via Bun.serve on $AUDIT_PORT (default 8410): (1) GET /audit-log.jsonl?since=<id> streams audit rows as NDJSON in id order, each line one JSON object including its id so the caller's next cursor is the last id received; no since means from the beginning; the endpoint is the SIEM-ingest surface from the original R-16 sketch. (2) GET /healthz returns JSON: ok, rows total, newest row at, per-run cursor lag summary (runs being tailed, oldest unconsumed age), and the warren base URL it follows (token never echoed). (3) Optional bearer auth: when $AUDIT_API_TOKEN is set, both endpoints require it; 401 otherwise-shaped like warren's error envelope for familiarity, but do NOT import warren code — copy the tiny shape and note in FRICTION.md that error-envelope shape is a wire convention extensions want published as schema. (4) Retention: $AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS unset means keep forever (compliance default); when set, a periodic prune deletes rows older than the horizon — the single sanctioned DELETE, tested. Wire collector + store + server together in src/main.ts as the real entrypoint with graceful SIGTERM/SIGINT shutdown (flush cursors, close db). Tests: since-cursor pagination exactness (no skip, no dup across page boundary), auth on/off, retention prune, healthz shape. Exit criteria: extension bun test green; bun run start with env vars against the fake warren serves both endpoints.

steps.title: Container image, README env contract, and the finalized friction report
steps.description: Package the extension exactly as a third party would. Dockerfile in extensions/audit-log/: oven/bun base pinned to the same major as warren's root Dockerfile, bun install --frozen-lockfile, non-root user, VOLUME for /data with AUDIT_DATA_DIR defaulting to /data in-container, ENTRYPOINT bun src/main.ts, HEALTHCHECK curling /healthz. docker build must succeed from extensions/audit-log/ alone with no reference to the warren repo root — that standalone-buildability IS the packaging claim; if anything forces a root reference, that is a FRICTION.md entry, not a workaround. README.md written for an operator who has never read warren's source: what it is (append-only audit trail of warren run activity, SIEM-exportable), quickstart (docker run with WARREN_BASE_URL + WARREN_API_TOKEN + volume), full env table (WARREN_BASE_URL, WARREN_API_TOKEN, WARREN_POLL_MS, AUDIT_DATA_DIR, AUDIT_PORT, AUDIT_API_TOKEN, AUDIT_RETENTION_DAYS), the export API with a curl example, storage layout, and a clearly-labeled 'the contract this extension wishes it had' section describing the aspirational PLUGIN_* env contract and manifest from PHILOSOPHY's Tier-1 sketch. Add a docker-compose.example.yml showing audit-log alongside a warren container. Finalize FRICTION.md into named sections: delivery (polling vs a global lifecycle stream — cite warren-f566; per-run tail fan-out cost; restart catch-up semantics), wire types (hand-derived vs published JSON schemas), attribution (actor_kind gap, warren-3754), packaging (anything that broke standalone build), each section ending with 'what the future mechanism must provide'. No CI publish workflow in this step — ghcr publishing needs repo-secret decisions, file a follow-up seed instead and say so in the README. Exit criteria: docker build succeeds from the extension directory alone; README env table matches the code exactly; FRICTION.md sections complete.

steps.title: End-to-end smoke with golden export, and the closing docs pass
steps.description: Prove the whole pipeline and pin its output. (1) e2e test inside the extension: boot the fake warren with a scripted full run lifecycle (dispatch, queued-to-running, a handful of agent events including one steering event, terminal success with branch push + PR URL), run collector + store + export server together, then assert GET /audit-log.jsonl output equals an on-disk golden fixture under extensions/audit-log/__golden__/ (the __golden__ directory name matches warren's existing gate exclusions; timestamps normalized via an injectable clock so the golden is stable). Include a second scenario: kill the collector mid-stream, restart, assert the final export is identical to the uninterrupted scenario's golden — the durability claim as a test. (2) A documented manual walkthrough in the README: run the container against a real local warren (docker compose up, dispatch any run, curl the export) — verified once by the implementing agent and written up with real output samples, secrets scrubbed. (3) Closing docs pass in the warren repo: update the status line of docs/design/extensions.md to record that the flagship extension shipped and where FRICTION.md lives; confirm ROADMAP.md 'Now — in flight' entry for this plan is accurate or update it to done-pending-review; run bun run lint at root to prove the prose gate stays green (ROADMAP.md is tracked at zero violations — keep sentences under 25 words, active voice, no semicolons). (4) Record insights: ml record for the packaging pattern and any failure modes hit, evidence-linked to this plan. Exit criteria: both golden scenarios green; root bun run check:all green; README walkthrough section contains real captured output.

risks: check:layers today walks only src/ — step 1 extends the walk to extensions/; if the script's structure resists a clean extension, the reverse-direction rule (extensions must not import src/) silently never fires and the boundary is theater. Verify with a failing-import test, not a clean grep (PHILOSOPHY rule 4).

Root gates may swallow the new tree: biome, knip, and jscpd all walk broadly by default. If step 1's exclusions are wrong, root check:all breaks on extension code — or worse, silently lints it and future extension changes fight root ratchets.

bun install in a fresh git worktree rewrites bun.lock with large unrelated churn (mx-956e6b) — extension agents working in worktrees must commit only extensions/audit-log/bun.lock, never the root lockfile.

docs/openapi.yaml or docs/http-api.md may lag the real wire behavior on the event-tail endpoint; the collector must be built against observed responses from a live/fake server, with any doc drift filed as a warren issue rather than silently coded around.

Per-run tail fan-out may not scale on a busy instance (one connection per active run); acceptable for v0 — the point is to document the cost in FRICTION.md as the case for a global stream (warren-f566), not to solve it.
Golden fixtures with timestamps are flaky unless the clock is injected everywhere a row gets its at value; normalize at write time in tests, never post-process the golden.
acceptance: extensions/audit-log/ builds a container image with docker build run from that directory alone, and the image runs against a warren instance given only WARREN_BASE_URL and WARREN_API_TOKEN.

A full fake-warren run lifecycle produces audit rows for run.dispatched, run.started, run.terminal, branch.pushed, pr.opened, and run.steered exactly once each, byte-identical to the committed golden export, including across a mid-stream collector kill-and-restart.
GET /audit-log.jsonl?since=<id> pages the append-only log with no skips and no duplicates across page boundaries, and /healthz reports cursor lag without echoing credentials.

Zero audit-specific lines in warren core: git grep -i 'audit' over src/ and scripts/ returns nothing new versus the plan's start, and the only core diffs are the generic check:layers walk extension, the two layer rules, and root-gate exclusion entries.
check:layers fails on a synthetic import in either direction across the extensions/ boundary (proven by test), and root bun run check:all is green at every step's merge.

FRICTION.md exists with delivery, wire-types, attribution, and packaging sections, each ending with a 'what the future mechanism must provide' statement — the input the manifest/loader design record will be written from.

sections.context: Warren's GitHub surface is duplicated and credential-unsafe: four REST clients with drifted helper copies, five URL grammars with three failure conventions, four unshared retry policies (two disagreeing in direction), four git-credential mechanisms of which one supplies no credential (broken under K8s), and a static GITHUB_TOKEN captured once at boot and fanned by value through 66 non-test files. Hourly-expiring GitHub App installation tokens cannot be expressed in that shape — createPrMergeChecker holds one captured token across a multi-hour poll loop and treats 401/403 as keep-waiting, so an expired token silently stalls a plan-run. The Forge seam (docs/design/forge-contract.md, owner GO 2026-08-11) consolidates the surface behind one contract, makes credentials minted-per-operation, and keeps PAT mode a permanent peer via capability flags. Downstream, the analytics campaign's merge-watcher blocks on this seam by the 2026-08-08 decision.
sections.approach: Five phases per the design doc, each phase a chain of single-agent PRs. Phase 1 consolidates transport into src/forge/github/ (a decomposed directory, Article II — no grandfathering at birth, tests in the same PR) so the api.github.com literal exists only there, letting phase 2's check:layers rule pair be born green in the same PR as the contract (PHILOSOPHY rule 4). Phase 2 cuts the Forge contract with FakeForge as implementation #2 (production code under src/forge/fake/, WARREN_FORGE=fake, boot-resolved fail-loud registry per §1.1). Phase 3 threads the one Forge instance through boot wiring exactly as runtimeProvider is threaded (warren-c531 precedent), then migrates reap, plan-runs, and CI-fixer, with capability degradations (§5) replacing token-presence conditionals. Phase 4 ships GitHubApp and GitHubPat as peers with the §4 mint-per-operation boundary, the manifest registration flow, and a heartbeat probe (modeled on the proven app-heartbeat job from PR #818). Phase 5 deletes the old paths under Article VI's repo-wide old-path search. Falsification tests hold throughout: FakeForge completes dispatch->reap->push->PR with zero domain-code changes, and acceptance scenario 39 stays green at every commit.

alternatives.name: Forge.token string refreshed by a background timer
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected in the design doc §4: the type invites capture and every call site that copies the string into a config object re-creates today's bug; no gate can catch it.

alternatives.name: A global git credential helper
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected §4: no refresh point, a no-op under WARREN_RUNTIME=k8s where no supervisor runs, and it would have to shell back into warren from inside a pod.

alternatives.name: hasApp boolean conditionals instead of capability flags
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected §5: 'PAT is a permanent peer' survives only if the domain reads a declared flag and degrades; it does not survive a hasApp check scattered through the CI-fixer.

alternatives.name: Building the merge-watcher before the seam
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected by the 2026-08-07 owner ordering decision: it would be a second GitHub client the campaign then has to consolidate. Waiting means it is born a Forge consumer.

alternatives.name: A single src/forge/github/http.ts file
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected: the naive union of the four clients exceeds the 500-line budget; Article II forbids grandfathering at birth, so the tree arrives decomposed.

steps.title: forge p1: scaffold src/forge/github/ transport core (headers, readers, retry, error classifier) + shared recordingFetch helper
steps.description: Create src/forge/github/ as a decomposed tree: http.ts (one GITHUB_API_BASE, one USER_AGENT scheme, one buildHeaders reconciling the drifted copies — note check-runs.ts omits content-type today and both its calls are GETs; readJson/readText/truncate), errors.ts (the ForgeErrorKind classifier from the design doc §2: no_credential/unauthorized/forbidden/not_found/conflict/rate_limited/push_protected/unsupported/network/http_error, with parseRetryAfterMs), retry.ts (ONE transport retry policy: network/status-0/5xx/429 transient, Retry-After honored capped at 60s, bounded attempts — pr-merge.ts's policy is the model; 4xx is fatal). Keep the injected-fetch convention (fetch?: typeof fetch ?? globalThis.fetch). Promote recordingFetch/jsonResponse out of src/runs/pr.test-helpers.ts to a shared neutral home and add route-keyed dispatch (the ci-fixer poller tests need it — see src/ci-fixer/poller.test.ts checkRunsFetch). No caller changes in this PR. Every file under 500 lines, tests in the same PR (coverage floor 91.85% lines). Article I: this PR is a no-behavior-change consolidation and its title must say so.

steps.title: forge p1: migrate src/runs/pr.ts + pr-checks.ts (openPullRequest, findExistingPr, checkPullRequestMerged) onto the transport core
steps.description: Replace the private GITHUB_API_BASE/buildHeaders/readJson/readText/truncate/parseRetryAfterMs copies in src/runs/pr-checks.ts and src/runs/pr.ts with imports from src/forge/github/. Public signatures and result unions (OpenPullRequestResult, CheckPrMergedResult) stay unchanged — downstream consumers (plan-runs/pr-merge.ts, reap/pr-open.ts, ci-fixer/poller.ts) must not need edits. The api.github.com literal must be fully gone from these files after this PR (phase 2's layer rule depends on it). Keep WARREN_GH_FETCH_OVERRIDE working for now — it dies in step 13. Existing tests in pr.test.ts/pr-checks.test.ts keep passing with the exact header assertions (Bearer token, accept header); migrate them to the shared recordingFetch.

steps.title: forge p1: migrate src/runs/pr-annotate.ts onto the transport core + re-clamp the PATCH body
steps.description: Swap pr-annotate.ts's private helper copies for src/forge/github/ imports (api.github.com literal fully gone from the file). Fix the audited clamp hole: annotatePrPreview PATCHes a body it never re-clamps, so a near-limit body plus a preview failure tail 422s — import MAX_PR_BODY_LENGTH from src/runs/pr-template.ts and clamp the recomposed body before the PATCH (domain-side fix per design doc §3). Preserve marker idempotency (warren:preview-start/end), the append-when-markers-absent behavior, and the unchanged-body short-circuit. De-duplicate the local recordingFetch copy in pr-annotate.test.ts onto the shared helper.

steps.title: forge p1: migrate src/ci-fixer/check-runs.ts onto the transport core
steps.description: Swap check-runs.ts's private helper copies for src/forge/github/ imports (api.github.com literal fully gone). fetchCheckRuns keeps its result union and fetchJobLogTail keeps its documented null-on-every-failure contract (it is already the shape the contract's best-effort fetchJobLogTail wants). Reconcile the header drift deliberately: adopt the shared buildHeaders (content-type on writes only, or always — pick once, document in the core). Fix the reversed jsonResponse(body, status) argument-order footgun in check-runs.test.ts by migrating to the shared helper.

steps.title: forge p1: migrate acceptance scenario 35's inline GitHub client into a lib helper + fix the GITHUB_TOKEN passthrough gap
steps.description: Scenario 35 (35-ci-fixer-roundtrip.ts) carries the fourth client copy: its own GITHUB_API constant, inline header literal, parseRepoSlug (a fifth URL grammar that throws AcceptanceError), and the repo's only branch-delete call. Extract a scripts/acceptance/lib/github-cleanup.ts helper (close PR + delete branch, best-effort by contract: cleanup failure logs and never fails a scenario) consuming src/forge/github/ transport. Also fix the verified harness gap (design doc §6.14): bootInProc's env allowlist drops GITHUB_TOKEN, so even operator-run scenario 35 boots a warren whose auto-open-PR config is empty and the opener assertion cannot pass in-proc — decide and implement which side owns the token (recommended: run.ts passes GITHUB_TOKEN via extraEnv only when set, documented in the scenario header). Verify by running scenario 35 against a real repo if credentials are available; otherwise document the residual risk in the PR.

steps.title: forge p2: land the pull-request wire vocabulary in src/core/wire.ts (+ check:wire-types stems, UI labels, re-exports)
steps.description: Add PULL_REQUEST_LIFECYCLES (open/merged/closed_unmerged) to src/core/wire.ts in the house shape: frozen as-const tuple, derived union type PullRequestLifecycle, isPullRequestLifecycle guard, with the RUN_FAILURE_REASONS-style doc block (one paragraph per arm naming detection site and distinctions — merged means merged_at non-null; closed with merged_at null is closed_unmerged, per the plan-run coordinator's truth-source rule). Add stems 'pull' and 'forge' to scripts/check-wire-types.ts DOMAIN_STEMS with the warren-id rationale comment (NOT 'pr' — substring matching would silently widen over Provider/Preview/Priority/Project). Re-export from src/client/types.ts and src/ui/src/api/types.ts, add the human-label map entry in src/ui/src/lib/labels.ts, confirm ../core/wire.ts stays in src/ui/tsconfig.app.json include, and run bun run build:ui to prove TS6307 does not fire. No consumer migrates yet.

steps.title: forge p2: cut the Forge contract + FakeForge + the check:layers rule pair (one PR)
steps.description: Land in ONE PR (PHILOSOPHY rule 4: a seam is not done until a gate enforces it, landed with the contract): (1) src/forge/contract.ts — the ten-method Forge interface and DTOs from the design doc §1/§2 (RepoRef and PullRequestRef opaque, PullRequestDraft as intent, CheckSummary/CheckRun, GitCredential with expiresAt, ForgeResult<T>, ForgeError, ForgeCapabilities), typed per the runtime-contract house style: capabilities as the first member, per-method doc blocks naming which are firm, provider-neutral DTOs, PullRequestLifecycle imported from src/core/wire.ts as an alias-not-relist with the Exact<> mutual-assignability test copied from src/runtime/contract.test.ts. CheckRun lives here (it does not cross warren's HTTP wire). (2) src/forge/errors.ts — UnknownForgeError extending WarrenError plus FORGE_ERROR_HTTP_STATUS modeled on RUNTIME_BACKEND_STATUS_BY_CODE. (3) src/forge/fake/ — FakeForge as full implementation #2: production code (never test-helpers — gates exempt test paths), in-memory PR store, parseRepoRef owning a fake:// or configured-path grammar, capabilities all-true with credentialLifetime static, synthetic job logs. (4) scripts/layer-rules.json — the rule pair modeled on the burrow boundary: a forbidPattern rule on the api\.github\.com literal (from src/, allow src/forge/ with why) and a forbidImports twin banning src/forge/github/ internals plus octokit-family packages outside src/forge/. Both rules born green because phase 1 removed every literal outside the tree. Contract conformance tests run against FakeForge.

steps.title: forge p2: GitHubForge provider (PAT/static mode) + the boot-resolved forge registry
steps.description: src/forge/github/provider.ts: GitHubForge implementing the contract over the phase-1 transport core. parseRepoRef absorbs the five audited grammars (https/scp/ssh clone URLs per src/projects/url.ts's path-safety rules — the [A-Za-z0-9._-]+ segment validation MUST survive into the packed key since it guards /data/projects paths; PR web URLs with query/fragment tolerance; API URLs), never throws, returns null for foreign hosts. openPullRequest is idempotent: the 422-then-search dance moves inside, and the duplicate search must handle the cross-fork head case the audit found (src/runs/pr.ts:164 hardcodes owner:head — design doc §6.13). gitCredential returns the configured static secret with expiresAt null. Capabilities: checkRuns true for classic PAT (document the fine-grained-PAT false), credentialLifetime static, botIdentity false. src/forge/registry.ts: FORGE_KINDS=['github','fake'], DEFAULT_FORGE_KIND='github', WARREN_FORGE env selection, blank=default, unknown throws UnknownForgeError with a recoveryHint listing legal values (copy resolveRuntimeKind), one deps bag, resolved once at boot, hermetic registry tests with throwing factories per src/runtime/registry.test.ts. Registry construction only — threading is step 9.

steps.title: forge p3: thread the Forge instance through boot wiring, ServerDeps, and the handler surface
steps.description: Resolve the Forge ONCE in bootServer at/replacing the loadAutoOpenPrConfigFromEnv site (src/server/main/index.ts:169) and thread the SAME instance to every consumer, exactly as runtimeProvider is threaded (warren-c531: resolved once, flows into bridges, scheduler, plan-run wiring, detectors, ServerDeps). Add ServerDeps.forge (required, readonly, doc naming the resolver). AutoOpenPrConfig survives this step but its token/gitToken fields stop fanning: the nine handler call sites (projects.ts x4, plan-runs.ts x2, alerts.ts, runs/dispatch.ts, runs/pause-resume.ts) and the boot fan-outs switch to minting via forge.gitCredential(ref) immediately before each git spawn, feeding githubCredentialGitEnv — the per-spawn GIT_CONFIG_* env is the re-mint boundary (§4.2). PAT mode makes the mint free. Scenario 39 must stay green: the forge handle must never appear in a public projection, and minted secrets must stay inside the existing redaction paths (log-redact.ts key list gains any new env/field names).

steps.title: forge p3: migrate the reap pipeline (pr_open + pr_annotate_preview) onto Forge
steps.description: runPrOpen (src/runs/reap/pr-open.ts) and runPreviewAnnotate (src/runs/reap/preview.ts + pr-annotate.ts) consume forge.openPullRequest / forge.setPullRequestBody / forge.parseRepoRef instead of parseGitHubUrl + direct clients. The throwing parseGitHubUrl leaves the reap path (parseRepoRef null means the forge does not own the URL: emit reap_failed step=pr_open with a clear detail, never crash the reap). Transport retry now lives in the provider, so the reap-side 1s/2s/4s loop collapses to semantic retry only (the 'No commits between' permanent 422 arrives as a classified conflict). The K8s CloneFetchConfig path mints via gitCredential instead of reading autoOpen.token. Preview annotation gates on capabilities.pullRequestBodyEdit and reports a skipped sub-step (today it is silent). Best-effort semantics preserved: no forge failure ever marks the run failed. Reap tests keep testing at the semantic seam (fakeOpenPr becomes a FakeForge or a contract-typed stub).

steps.title: forge p3: migrate the plan-run coordinator onto Forge (merge gate, reopen-PR, child-seed close)
steps.description: createPrMergeChecker (src/plan-runs/pr-merge.ts) is replaced by forge.getPullRequest: the closure-captured token dies, PullRequestState.lifecycle/mergedAt drive the gate, and isFatalHttpError's status===404||410 leak becomes a switch on ForgeErrorKind not_found (design doc §0's leak test names this line). Decide and encode the unauthorized policy: today 401/403 silently keep waiting for the whole merge budget — under the seam, unauthorized should surface a loud per-project notice while still not failing the plan (the operator can fix credentials without losing progress; no_credential keeps today's stall-and-log semantics). createReopenPr in plan-run-wiring.ts migrates onto forge.openPullRequest (its private parseGitHubUrl call dies). closeMergedChildSeed's direct env.GITHUB_TOKEN read is replaced by a gitCredential mint at the fetch/push spawn. mergedAt semantics preserved exactly: merged_at non-null is the truth source; closed with null merged_at is closed_unmerged; a null parseRepoRef keeps the wait-indefinitely-on-manual-merge behavior for foreign-host PRs.

steps.title: forge p3: migrate the CI-fixer + scheduler onto Forge with checkRuns/jobLogs capability degradations
steps.description: The CI-fixer poller consumes forge.listChecks / forge.fetchJobLogTail; bootScheduler stops receiving githubToken (the forge handle replaces all four fan-outs in scheduler.ts, including createProjectCloneHealer's clone credential which becomes a per-spawn mint). Implement the §5 degradations: capabilities.checkRuns false makes the poller stay idle with ONE notice per project (new CiFixerSkipReason 'unsupported' alongside disabled/not_failing/cooldown/max_retries; the ProjectHealTracker notice-gate is the rate-limit precedent) — today an unsupported forge is indistinguishable from a network blip and would log per-PR per-tick forever. jobLogs false keeps the existing prompt fallback (dispatch.ts already says 'No CI log could be fetched'). The local CheckRun type in check-runs.ts becomes a re-export of the contract's CheckRun. extractJobId's details_url regex moves inside the GitHub provider (a check-run id must not cross the seam, §0).

steps.title: forge p3: FakeForge end-to-end acceptance (falsification test 1) + delete WARREN_GH_FETCH_OVERRIDE
steps.description: The campaign's falsification test 1 becomes an acceptance scenario: a project on a FakeForge-owned URL completes dispatch -> reap -> push -> PR (FakeForge records the openPullRequest and the scenario asserts the PR ref and lifecycle transitions) with zero domain-code changes — the scenario boots warren with WARREN_FORGE=fake and nothing else special. Migrate scenarios 26 and 36 off WARREN_GH_FETCH_OVERRIDE=merged onto FakeForge (whose getPullRequest can be told to report merged), then delete the override: GH_FETCH_OVERRIDE_ENV/readGhFetchOverride in pr-checks.ts, the stub-token synthesis in loadAutoOpenPrConfigFromEnv, and every mention. Also verify scenario 39 end-to-end under the forge wiring and add a FakeForge-URL leak probe to its vocabulary if the fake's webUrl shape could leak.

steps.title: forge p4: empirical spike — answer Q1-Q4 against the live GitHub API and amend the design doc
steps.description: Settle the four questions GitHub does not document (design doc §7), each with a recorded transcript/evidence in the doc: Q1 does the App manifest redirect_url accept a loopback address (the whole self-hosted registration story depends on it — a NAT deployment has no public URL); Q2 does POST /app-manifests/{code}/conversions require authentication, and is the code single-use; Q3 does a fine-grained PAT reach PUT /pulls/:n/merge (read X-Accepted-GitHub-Permissions); Q4 can an App approve a PR it authored. Use a throwaway App/repo. Amend docs/design/forge-contract.md §7 with the answers and their consequences for the manifest flow design (step 17). No warren code changes. This step has no code dependencies and can run any time before phase 4 locks.

steps.title: forge p4: close the three no-credential push sites via per-spawn minted credentials
steps.description: clone-apply.ts:191 (pushCloneDeltasToOrigin — annotated K8s-only, which is exactly the topology where the supervisor rewrite it relies on does not exist), reap/salvage.ts:69 (rescue-ref push, no env at all), and runtime/local/finalize.ts:401 (the primary run-branch push) all push with no credential today, working only under the LocalProvider because of the supervisor's global gitconfig rewrite. Route each through forge.gitCredential minted immediately before the spawn, rendered via githubCredentialGitEnv, composed with gitRepoContextScrubEnv (key families do not overlap — mx-4c6cdf). This fixes a live K8s bug independent of App mode and is a precondition for deleting the supervisor rewrite in phase 5. Anonymous behavior when no credential is configured must stay unchanged (empty mint result -> empty env).

steps.title: forge p4: GitHubApp provider — JWT mint, installation-token cache, capability flags, heartbeat
steps.description: src/forge/github/app-credentials.ts (or sibling): sign an RS256 JWT from the deployment's private key, POST /app/installations/:id/access_tokens, optionally down-scoped to the single repository and minimum permissions; cache until expiresAt minus a safety margin, re-mint after. No token-length assumption (the ghs_APPID_JWT stateless format is rolling out — §6.9). GitHubForge gains an App credential mode: credentialLifetime short-lived, botIdentity true (resolve the App's bot login/noreply email for GitIdentity), checkRuns true. Config surface: app id + private key via env/deployment config, documented. The heartbeat: a runtime liveness probe that mints on an interval and surfaces a loud health signal on failure (the CI app-heartbeat job from PR #818 is the model: a successful mint is the whole proof) — name it to avoid colliding with the run-heartbeat watchdog vocabulary. Unauthorized results from a dead key must be loud (per-project notice path from step 11), never a silent stall. New secret shapes (ghs_ tokens) added to the log-redaction key list and the event scrubber.

steps.title: forge p4: manifest registration flow + operator docs
steps.description: The self-hosted App registration story, shaped by the step-14 answers: a warren-guided GitHub App manifest flow (create-from-manifest, capture the conversion code, store app id + private key in the deployment's config) so each deployment registers its own App — the App is a credential mechanism, not an identity provider (ROADMAP decision 2026-08-03). If Q1 answered that loopback redirect works, the CLI/UI can drive it locally; if not, implement the documented fallback (manual registration per docs/project-setup.md §2 style, which stays the PAT-mode-adjacent path regardless). Deliverables: the registration surface, docs/ operator guide covering both App and PAT modes as peers, and the .env.example / deployment config entries. Update docs/project-setup.md cross-references.

steps.title: forge p4: K8s token windows under App mode + resolve the Secret-fallback question
steps.description: The three K8s windows each get their own mint (§4.1): init-container clone (mint at pod-spec time), finalize push (already refresh-ready — the pod fetches the token over the authenticated callback per provider.ts:461-479; wire that fetch to a fresh forge mint), and reap-side fetch + PR open (mint per step). Then settle the open §4.1 decision: the Secret-mounted fallback (finalize-entrypoint.ts:145) and the no-intent salvage window read a long-lived Secret that breaks under App mode — either route them through the authenticated callback (preferred if the callback is reachable in those windows) or ship a documented PAT-only degradation for the salvage fallback, recorded in the design doc and RUNBOOK-K8S. Agent containers keep never holding the push token (AGENT_SCRUBBED_ENV_KEYS stays). Acceptance: a K8s-topology run under App mode completes clone, finalize push, and PR open with a token minted in each window, and a >1h run does not 401 on finalize.

steps.title: forge p5: delete the old paths (supervisor rewrite, static-token config fields, dead vocabulary)
steps.description: With every push site minting per-spawn (steps 9, 15, 18) and every REST call behind the seam: delete the supervisor's global insteadOf rewrite (src/supervisor/git-credentials.ts + its main.ts call), drop AutoOpenPrConfig.token/.gitToken and every remaining by-value token field (scheduler githubToken, TickCiFixerDeps.githubToken, SpawnRunInput.githubToken where superseded), and remove the x-access-token literals outside src/forge/. Article VI applies in full: repo-wide search for old paths including Dockerfile entrypoints, workflow YAML, supervisor spawn paths, docs, and acceptance scenario 12's deliberate GITHUB_TOKEN blanking (which exists only to suppress the rewrite being deleted). Green gates are not a working deployment: verify a local-topology container boot and dispatch end-to-end before merge. Update AGENTS.md (boundary docs), docs/http-api.md via gen:docs, and the CHANGELOG.

risks: Scenario 39 regression: the forge handle or a minted token leaking into a public projection — the scenario runs per-PR and its UNREDACTED_BEARER probe will catch a raw ghs_ token, but new field names must be added to the redaction lists proactively.
The phase-2 layer rule cannot be born green if any phase-1 step leaves an api.github.com literal outside src/forge/ — each phase-1 PR must grep for the literal before merge.

check:layers does not walk scripts/, so scenario 35's migrated helper is unenforced until WALK_ROOTS widens — widening is a deliberate decision, not a default (the walk was deliberately narrowed once).
Coverage ratchet: src/forge/ lands as a fresh tree against a 91.85% line floor; any step that lands code without tests in the same PR fails check:coverage.
Article IX: any step touching .github/workflows/auto-merge.yml or src/registry/builtins/ cannot auto-merge and needs a human merge.

The K8s Secret-fallback decision (step 18) may force a documented PAT-only degradation for the salvage window; treating it as blocking-perfect would stall phase 4 — the doc explicitly allows the degradation path.

createPrMergeChecker's replacement changes 401 semantics from silent-wait to loud-notice; a mis-specified policy could fail plans that today survive an operator fixing credentials mid-run — the step preserves no-progress-loss on no_credential.
parseRepoRef must preserve src/projects/url.ts's segment validation or /data/projects path safety regresses (mx-e741b0).
acceptance: Falsification test 1: an acceptance scenario boots warren with WARREN_FORGE=fake and a FakeForge project completes dispatch -> reap -> push -> PR with zero domain-code changes.
Falsification test 2: acceptance scenario 39 (public-instance leak guard) is green at every commit of the campaign.
check:layers carries the forge rule pair and fails a direct api.github.com literal or a src/forge/github/ internal import outside src/forge/.

No configuration object holds a GitHub token: AutoOpenPrConfig.token/.gitToken and the by-value githubToken fields are deleted; every git spawn mints via forge.gitCredential immediately before the spawn.
GitHubApp and GitHubPat run as peers behind capability flags: checkRuns false under fine-grained PAT idles the CI-fixer with one notice per project instead of per-PR errors.
The supervisor's global gitconfig rewrite is deleted and a local-topology container deploy still clones, pushes, and opens PRs.
A K8s run longer than one hour under App mode completes its finalize push and PR open without a 401.
The heartbeat probe surfaces a dead App credential loudly (the PR #818 lesson) rather than a silent merge-gate stall.
bun run check:all is green at every step's merge; docs/http-api.md, docs/openapi.yaml, and docs/cli-reference.md regenerate clean where surfaces changed.

sections.context: docs/design/agent-analytics.md names the thesis: the durable asset of a control plane is the outcome-joined telemetry corpus its dispatch loop produces, not the dispatch loop itself. Warren already ships a descriptive analytics layer (GET /analytics/runs|cost|behavior, six insight callouts, RunAnalytics/CostAnalytics UI), but its depth is capped by verified data problems at HEAD ae3d9c63 (v0.15.0): no created_at on runs so queue wait is unmeasurable; model/provider re-parsed from rendered_agent_json per query; events.origin dropped at write; commits_ahead and diff stats never persisted; no tool-call rollup so every behavioral query re-parses raw payload_json under a silently-truncating 20k-row cap (src/db/repos/events.ts:19); and success still means 'exited 0' because pr_merged_at exists only on plan_run_children — a standalone run's PR outcome is never recorded. The ordering precondition is met: the Forge campaign (pl-d1c9) shipped in v0.15.0, and src/forge/contract.ts:91-97 + :214-217 already expose PullRequestState (open|merged|closed_unmerged, required mergedAt) with the merge-watcher named as an intended consumer. This plan is the owner go the design record says it awaits, scoped to its phases 0-3.
sections.approach: Follow the design record's philosophy-compliant split (§6): capture fidelity is core (facts as columns, recorded not interpreted), normalization is harness-keyed registries in src/core, interpretation grows in the in-core insight miner first — the Tier-1 observer extension and the LLM judge layer stay phase 4 and out of this plan. Forward-chained in four tiers: (1) independent capture roots — created_at, model/provider columns, events.origin, reap-time diff facts — each paid for by a named insight; (2) the merge watcher, generalizing the already-Forge-native plan-run poller (src/plan-runs/pr-merge.ts) into a post_reap lifecycle-bus subscriber (whose payload already carries outcome, branchPushed, commitsAhead, prUrl — src/runs/lifecycle-bus.ts:117) that writes pr_state + pr_merged_at onto runs, flipping every success metric to landed-work semantics; (3) toolShape/fileShape extractor registries in the established usage-shape.ts pattern (deliberately NOT gated on the unstarted AgentRuntimeAdapter seam, GH#846 — usageShape landed pre-adapter the same way and counts as paid-up material for it), feeding a tool-calls rollup that retires the 20k-row cap; (4) insight expansion on the new data (per-directory difficulty, context waste, steering-outcome deltas, cost per merged PR — every insight with denominators and confidence) and the UI surfacing on RunAnalytics, with every new wire field classified in the public-projection allowlists. Sapling coverage is explicitly out: sapling is being retired (separate seed), which shrinks KNOWN_RUNTIME_IDS to claude-code + pi, both already covered by USAGE_SHAPES.

alternatives.name: Gate the plan on AgentRuntimeAdapter phase 1 landing first
alternatives.rejected_because: The seam is published as good-first-challenge GH#846 (warren-c80e) and unstarted; blocking on it stalls the campaign on contributor timing. The registry pattern usageShape established in src/core/usage-shape.ts is the same home toolShape/fileShape need, and the adapter later folds all three in. Only insight-ordering matters, and in-plan blocks encode it.

alternatives.name: Ship the deep analytics engine as a Tier-1 observer extension now
alternatives.rejected_because: Phase 4 per the design record: it wants the durable global lifecycle stream (warren-f566) and the FRICTION.md surfaces (scoped observer credential, wire-schema artifact). In-core-first proves the insights on our own fleet before packaging work, per §11 phase 3.

alternatives.name: Include the LLM judge layer (§12) in this plan
alternatives.rejected_because: The judge is a phase-4 resident and §12.6 requires the verdict schema and behavioral taxonomy to get an owner cut before the first judgment runs — a corpus of verdicts under a throwaway schema is worth less than no corpus.

alternatives.name: Fill the sapling usageShape hole for full-harness coverage
alternatives.rejected_because: Sapling has no users and is being retired from the project (standalone seed, outside this plan). Covering it would be dead work.

steps.title: Record the owner go: amend agent-analytics.md status + add the ROADMAP campaign entry; fix the stale forge-contract.md status header and the stale no-cascade comment in src/db/repos/runs.ts
runs.created_at: persist the queued instant at insert (sqlite + pg schema, migration, RunsRepo.create), surface it on run rows and queue-wait in /analytics/runs
runs.model + runs.provider as real columns written at dispatch from rendered frontmatter; analytics group-bys read the columns instead of re-parsing rendered_agent_json per query
Persist events.origin: add the column, thread origin through the stream-bridge append path, and classify it in projections
Persist reap-time outcome facts on runs: commits_ahead column plus parsed diff stats (files_changed, insertions, deletions) from the reap pipeline
Merge watcher: generalize plan-run PR polling into a post_reap lifecycle-bus subscriber that polls Forge and writes pr_state + pr_merged_at onto runs

Landed-work semantics: extend run metrics with merged-PR rate per agent/model/provider bucket, flip RunAnalytics KPIs, add a PR lifecycle badge to run detail, classify every new field in the public allowlists

toolShape + fileShape extractor registries in src/core (usage-shape.ts pattern, keyed by RuntimeId), and route command mining through toolShape so /analytics/behavior stops hardcoding the Anthropic payload shape
Tool-calls rollup table extracted via the shape registries, so behavioral queries read structured rows and retire the silently-truncating 20k-row DEFAULT_TOOL_EVENT_CAP re-parse
Insight: per-directory difficulty map — failures, retries, and steering joined to fileShape-extracted paths, aggregated by directory, shipped with denominators and confidence
Insight: context-waste proxy — tool_result byte share against run context tokens from the rollup, shipped with denominators and confidence
Insights: steering-outcome deltas and cost-per-merged-PR, joined on pr_state, shipped with denominators and confidence
UI: render the new insight kinds and a per-directory struggle view on RunAnalytics, classify every new field in the public-projection allowlists

risks: Rule-1 sprawl: 'analytics' invites speculative capture. Discipline: every column and field in this plan is named by the insight paying for it; anything else waits for its payer.

Mixed-semantics window: historical runs predate created_at, model/provider columns, and pr_state. Aggregates must label pre-migration rows unknown and exclude them from denominators — never count them as zero or failure.

Merge-watcher polling pressure: a fleet of stale open PRs must not hammer the forge rate limit. Reuse the pr-merge.ts backoff and terminal-stop discipline (merged/closed_unmerged/unparseable stop polling).

Public-projection leaks: every new aggregate field must be absent from the public body until classified (the 'as const satisfies' allowlist pattern in src/server/handlers/runs/analytics.ts:175-248); acceptance scenario 39 and the projection tests are the guard.

Rollup backfill cost: extracting tool calls from a large events table must not block boot; backfill incrementally or cap to a window, and the rollup still cascades on project delete — retention survival remains a phase-4 extension concern, not this table's job.
bun install in a fresh git worktree rewrites bun.lock with unrelated churn (mx-956e6b) — agents working children in worktrees must not commit lockfile noise.
acceptance: A standalone run whose PR merges shows pr_state=merged with a merged-at timestamp on GET /runs/:id and a lifecycle badge in the run-detail UI, without being a plan-run child.
/analytics/runs reports merged-PR rate alongside exit-code success for totals and every agent/model/provider bucket, computed from run columns with no rendered_agent_json re-parse in the query path.
Every new run row carries created_at, model, and provider at insert; queue wait is derivable as started_at minus created_at.
/analytics/behavior reads the tool-calls rollup; no behavioral query path re-parses raw payload_json under DEFAULT_TOOL_EVENT_CAP, and truncation (if any remains) is reported, never silent.

Per-directory difficulty, context-waste, steering-outcome, and cost-per-merged-PR insights render on RunAnalytics, each carrying denominators and confidence; every new wire field is classified public-or-redacted and the public-projection tests plus acceptance scenario 39 pass.
docs/design/agent-analytics.md status records the owner go and this plan id; ROADMAP lists the campaign; bun run check:all passes 12/12 on every child PR.

sections.context: The §12.6 owner cut landed 2026-08-15 (docs/design/agent-analytics.md, commit e1c44e3b): rubric v1 is the full 15-class behavioral taxonomy (§12.4) and the verdict shape is locked (§12.3) — multi-label with low/medium/high confidence bands (never a float), clean exclusive of all other classes, at least one event-sequence range per non-clean class plus an optional note capped at 200 chars, provenance (judge model id, rubric-version hash, judged-at, judgment cost), and append-only re-judging under new rubric versions. With that cut recorded, nothing gates the judge's birth except building it (§12.6). The placement decision is extension-first with a named in-core exit at the phase-4 boundary (§12.1). The judge is a function, not a run (§12.2): it executes no code, needs no sandbox, and judge runs must not pollute the corpus they analyze — its whole tool surface is 'page the transcript, emit a verdict'. Prior art is the audit-log observer (pl-116e, extensions/audit-log/): standalone package, hand-rolled client over docs/openapi.yaml, bounded-page event tailing (FRICTION §1), append-only SQLite store with deterministic dedupe keys and ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING replay safety, cursor-after-sink checkpointing, and a token-gated JSONL export. Per §12.6 this work does NOT wait on warren-f566 (the global lifecycle stream): the judge is born tailing today's HTTP surface the way audit-log was, logging new friction into extensions/audit-log/FRICTION.md, and joins as payer #3 for the stream when it lands. Phase-1 data the judge joins against already shipped in pl-103e: pr_state/pr_merged_at ground truth, events.origin, the tool-calls rollup.
sections.approach: Build extensions/judge/ as the second Tier-1 observer, cloning the audit-log conventions wholesale: own package.json/bun.lock/tsconfig/Dockerfile, zero src/ or scripts/ imports (check:layers holds both directions), all warren reads over the published HTTP surface with the operator token, own SQLite store on its own volume. The judge loop itself is a bounded two-tool agent loop driven by the pi SDK (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent — §12.2's named natural in-ecosystem driver, already warren's default-runtime pin) with its default coding-agent toolset stripped to nothing (createAgentSession with noTools: 'builtin' + customTools) and a report_verdict tool whose terminate: true result ends the loop — schema-validated at the tool layer and prompt-enforced as the mandatory final action, since the session API surfaces no provider tool_choice forcing (verified against the SDK 2026-08-15). Provider-agnostic by owner call (2026-08-15): the judge model is a JUDGE_PROVIDER/JUDGE_MODEL env pair defaulting to a cheap tier (anthropic / claude-haiku-4-5), never a hardcoded vendor, so cheaper or higher-quality models — including cross-provider — swap in without a code change; provider and model id are both recorded in provenance. Coverage is total per §12.1: every terminal run gets judged or gets a visible unjudged marker; cost is controlled by model choice and budget gates, never by sampling. Validation is enforced at the wire-type layer before any write: clean exclusivity, evidence-range presence, note cap, band enum — a malformed verdict is retried against the model then marked unjudged, never stored partially. Re-judging appends under a distinct rubric-version hash; the calibration pass (§12.5) is a strong-model re-judge over a random sample whose agreement rate is itself a stored, queryable metric. Forward-chained in three tiers: (1) scaffold + locked wire types, then the three independent legs — read client, verdict store, rubric prompt; (2) the judge loop joining all three, then the collector daemon that drives it with budget gates; (3) calibration re-judge and the export/smoke/docs cap. Every step is one agent-sized PR against the extension package only.

alternatives.name: Drive the loop directly with @anthropic-ai/sdk (the rev-1 choice)
alternatives.rejected_because: Overruled by owner call 2026-08-15: a direct Anthropic SDK dependency hardcodes a vendor into the judge's engine, and the cost story (§12.1) rests on freely swapping cheaper or higher-quality models — including cross-provider for the calibration strong judge. §12.2 already names the pi SDK the natural in-ecosystem driver, and warren's own model tiers treat provider as a swappable dimension (WARREN_MODEL_*_PROVIDER). The rev-1 concern — pi is a coding-agent harness the judge must strip down — is carried as a named risk with a fallback (a thin provider-agnostic completion layer), not a reason to bind the corpus engine to one vendor.

alternatives.name: Ship the judge as a ninth builtin agent dispatched through the run primitive
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected by the design record itself (§12.2): a judge executes no code and needs no sandbox, and judge runs would pollute the corpus they analyze or need a recursion guard to exclude themselves.

alternatives.name: Wait for warren-f566 and subscribe to the global lifecycle stream instead of polling
alternatives.rejected_because: §12.6 explicitly frees the judge from that dependency — audit-log already proved the poll-and-page pattern against today's surface with the friction logged. Waiting stalls the verdict corpus for a delivery optimization; when the stream lands the judge migrates and becomes payer #3.

alternatives.name: Sample runs to control judge cost
alternatives.rejected_because: Overruled by the recorded owner decision (§12.1): judges run on every run because an unjudged run is a hole in the corpus and the join only compounds if coverage is total. Cost is controlled by model choice and visible budget skips, not coverage.

alternatives.name: Store verdicts in a core table for easy joining with run analytics
alternatives.rejected_because: PHILOSOPHY's litmus sorts interpretation out of core, and §12.2 locks 'the verdict lands in the extension's own store, never in a core table'. The in-core exit exists but is a named phase-4-boundary owner call, not a default.

steps.title: Scaffold extensions/judge/ + rubric-v1 wire types: standalone package (own package.json, bun.lock, tsconfig, Dockerfile, README) on the audit-log conventions, env contract (WARREN_BASE_URL, WARREN_API_TOKEN, JUDGE_PROVIDER/JUDGE_MODEL, per-provider model credentials as the pi SDK expects — ANTHROPIC_API_KEY, OPENAI_API_KEY, etc., only the configured provider's key required — and the JUDGE_* knobs), and src/wire.ts encoding the locked §12.3 verdict shape — the 15-class enum, low/medium/high bands, evidence ranges {fromSeq,toSeq}, 200-char note cap, provenance block (provider + model id, rubric-version hash, judged-at, cost) — with parse/validate functions enforcing clean exclusivity and range-presence, plus __golden__ fixtures pinning the verdict JSON shape

Warren read client + fake-warren double: hand-rolled client over docs/openapi.yaml for GET /runs (terminal-run discovery), GET /runs/:id (run facts: outcome, failure reason, cost, pr_state ground truth), and GET /runs/:id/events bounded pages (?since=<seq>&limit=<n>, never a held follow stream — FRICTION §1 pattern); token held in closure and never logged (audit-log client.ts pattern); fake-warren test double serving canned runs and event pages

Append-only verdict store: extension-owned SQLite (bun:sqlite) with verdicts + unjudged markers; dedupe key (runId, rubricVersion, judgeModelId) with ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING so replay is a no-op; re-judge under a new rubric version appends and never overwrites; rowid is the export paging sequence (audit-store.ts pattern); write path accepts only wire.ts-validated verdicts; query surface for per-rubric-version reads and the calibration join

Rubric v1 authoring: the judge system prompt rendering the 15-class §12.4 taxonomy with per-class definitions and evidence-pointability instructions; the report_verdict tool schema (TypeBox parameters) derived from wire.ts — schema-validated at the tool layer, multi-label, banded confidence, ranges + capped note — plus the tool promptGuidelines snippet making report_verdict the mandatory final action (the pi session API surfaces no provider tool_choice forcing); rubricVersion computed as a hash over a canonical serialization of prompt + taxonomy so an intentional edit forks the version and whitespace churn does not; prompt goldens pinning the rendered rubric

The judge loop: bounded pi-SDK agent loop — createAgentSession (@earendil-works/pi-coding-agent) with noTools: 'builtin' stripping the coding toolset, customTools registering exactly two read tools (get_run_facts; page_events cursoring NormalizedEvent rows via the client) plus report_verdict, whose execute returns terminate: true to end the loop; verdict emission is prompt-enforced via the tool's promptGuidelines (no provider tool_choice forcing exists at the session API — a judgment ending in plain text counts against the retry budget); model resolved via ModelRuntime from JUDGE_PROVIDER/JUDGE_MODEL with per-provider env keys (cheap tier default, no hardcoded vendor); transcript paging with a hard cap on pages per judgment so oversized event tails degrade to a lower-confidence verdict instead of unbounded spend; per-judgment token/cost accounting from session.getSessionStats() into provenance (provider + model id); malformed-or-missing-verdict retry (bounded) then unjudged — a judgment returns a validated verdict or an unjudged marker, nothing else

Collector daemon + budget gates: poll GET /runs for newly-terminal runs (cursor store, checkpoint only after the verdict store accepts — audit-log delivery discipline), drive one judgment per terminal run idempotently under the current rubric version; enforce JUDGE_MAX_COST_USD per judgment and JUDGE_DAILY_BUDGET_USD fleet-wide — on breach skip and write a visible unjudged marker with reason budget_exceeded, never degrade silently (§12.5); graceful shutdown finishes the in-flight judgment

Calibration re-judge: periodic strong-model pass (JUDGE_CALIBRATION_PROVIDER/JUDGE_CALIBRATION_MODEL, cross-provider capable) over a random sample of judged runs, appending verdicts under the same rubric version with the strong model's provider + id; per-class and overall band-agreement rate computed between cheap and strong verdicts, stored per rubric version as a queryable metric (§12.5 — the disagreement rate is itself the tracked signal that drives any future taxonomy narrowing); sample size and cadence as JUDGE_CALIBRATION_* env knobs

Export surface, smoke, and docs: token-gated GET /verdicts.jsonl paging by ?since=<id> (audit-log export pattern) plus an agreement-rate summary endpoint; end-to-end smoke against fake-warren proving terminal run → judged → validated verdict exported, the budget-skip path, and the re-judge append path; README covering deploy beside warren, env contract, and the Goodhart guard (verdicts never enter agent context raw — no mulch write exists in v1, §12.5); new missing-surface friction logged in extensions/audit-log/FRICTION.md

risks: Discovery polling waste: FRICTION §1 quantifies O(1 + active runs) requests per poll cycle. The judge only cares about terminal transitions, so the collector polls the runs list alone (no per-run tails until judging) — but a busy instance still pays a full re-list per cycle. Accepted cost until warren-f566; do not invent a private delivery channel.

Pi is a coding-agent harness, not a bare completion client. Verified against the installed SDK 2026-08-15 (via pi itself): noTools: 'builtin' strips the coding toolset while keeping customTools; defineTool + terminate: true ends the loop on the verdict call; ModelRuntime resolves per-provider env keys; getSessionStats() yields exact USD cost for catalog models. The one confirmed gap: no first-class tool_choice forcing at the session API — a judgment that ends in plain text without calling report_verdict must count against the bounded retry then mark unjudged. If that proves too lossy in practice, the escape hatches are an extension tool_call hook (block non-verdict endings) or StreamOptions.onPayload at the pi-agent-core layer — never a return to a single-vendor SDK.

Transcript scale: event tails routinely exceed a judge context window, and the tool-calls rollup is not on the wire for extensions. The page cap per judgment bounds spend but risks verdicts formed on a truncated read — the loop must record pages-read in provenance so a capped judgment is distinguishable from a full one.

Rubric hash instability: if rubricVersion hashes a non-canonical serialization, whitespace or key-order churn forks the corpus into unjoinable versions. Canonicalize before hashing and pin with a golden.

Cheap-model band calibration: haiku-tier judges may cluster on medium confidence, starving the Goodhart high-confidence door. The calibration pass measures this from day one; the answer is prompt/model iteration under new rubric versions, never post-hoc relabeling.

Export leak surface: verdicts are interpretations of possibly-private repos. The export endpoint is bearer-gated from birth; there is no public projection of verdicts, and adding one later is an owner call with allowlist classification.
bun install in a fresh git worktree rewrites bun.lock with unrelated churn (mx-956e6b) — agents working children in worktrees must not commit lockfile noise outside extensions/judge/.

Corpus pollution recursion: the judge never judges its own activity because it produces no runs (§12.2). Keep it that way — any future 'dispatch a judge run' convenience reintroduces the recursion guard problem the function shape was chosen to avoid.
acceptance: extensions/judge/ exists as a standalone package importing zero src/ or scripts/ modules; bun run check:all at the warren root stays green with the extension in the tree (check:layers holds both directions).

Against the fake-warren double: a terminal run produces exactly one validated rubric-v1 verdict in the store — multi-label with banded confidence, clean exclusive, every non-clean class carrying at least one event-sequence range, notes at most 200 chars, provenance complete (provider + model id, rubric-version hash, judged-at, cost) — and the verdict pages out over token-gated GET /verdicts.jsonl.

Re-running the collector over an already-judged run under the same rubric version writes nothing (idempotent replay); re-judging under a bumped rubric version appends a second verdict and both remain readable, keyed by version.
A judgment whose cost gate trips, or whose model output fails validation after bounded retries, yields a visible unjudged marker with a reason — never a partial verdict, never a silent skip.
The calibration pass produces a stored band-agreement rate between cheap and strong judges for the sampled runs, queryable per rubric version.
Swapping JUDGE_PROVIDER/JUDGE_MODEL to a different provider requires no code change in the extension — the judge loop has no vendor-specific SDK import outside the pi SDK itself.
No verdict content is written to any core warren table, to mulch, or into any agent-visible context; the only egress is the extension's own gated export.
New friction hit against warren's HTTP surface is logged in extensions/audit-log/FRICTION.md with the future-mechanism statement the house form requires.

sections.context: The 2026-08-16 operator decision (ROADMAP 'Now') queues the self-host push: Next items 2, 3, 4 in that order. The home-server install is warren's headline pitch and today's quickstart falsifies it — a fresh operator needs four bwrap security flags, SYS_ADMIN, and a hand-minted burrow token pair before the first dispatch. Root cause is the burrow dependency: the 2026-07-30 absorption decision ('Decisions already made') established that burrow was scaffolding built to build warren, that agent-runtime logic is internal to warren, and that the end state is warren importing zero burrow code. The decision's origin — the pi event-volume investigation tracing a pi parser gap (tool_execution_update) into burrow library code inside warren's k8s pods — is exactly the detour this campaign ends. Current state verified at HEAD: bucket 3 (domain vocabulary leakage) is already eliminated (eviction commits a2fa66e4..36d58c95, warren-c80e amendment 2026-08-13); the live burrow import surface is src/burrow-client/, src/runtime/local/**, src/runtime/registry.ts, and the k8s in-pod trio (agent-entrypoint/agent-io/agent-stdin-hold). PR #887 (v0.16.0) shipped the adapter registry and both tenant moves (GH#846 items 1-3), so src/runtime/adapters/ exists as the home phase 2 lifts code into. This plan realizes warren-c80e steps 4-6. It runs concurrent with the dogfood tech-debt queue (~27 issues), so every child names a file set disjoint from that queue's territory (plan-run coordinator, merge gate, reap close hook, and the in-flight k8s pod-watcher/cancel/status files).
sections.approach: Three phases in strict ROADMAP order (2 then 3 then 4), decomposed into single-agent single-PR children, each naming its file set. Phase 2 is a SOURCE LIFT, not a rewrite: burrow's pi + claude-code buildSpawnCommand, parsers (with their golden RPC fixtures), and steering encoders move into src/runtime/adapters/, then the k8s in-pod trio rewires onto them and a check:layers rule pins the exit criterion (src/runtime/k8s/ imports zero burrow code) per PHILOSOPHY rule 4. Phase 3 lands lift-then-wire: the bwrap/sandbox-exec/cgroup profile generation lifts into a new warren-owned src/sandbox/ module (binding a real writable $HOME separate from the workspace — the designated warren-c865 fix per its 2026-08-16 decision block), then LocalProvider swaps its burrow-daemon client for an in-process spawn + the same host-side drive loop the k8s entrypoint runs; preview sidecars re-home; the supervisor stops spawning burrow serve; and the excision child deletes src/burrow-client/, both package pins, the version-sync burrow assertions, the two burrow layer rules, and rewrites the burrow doc sections. No intermediate raw-exec daemon mode — the absorption decision retires that contract. Phase 4's two token wins ship FIRST as early children (ROADMAP item 4 explicitly allows front-loading): first-boot WARREN_API_TOKEN minting and supervisor-internal burrow channel-token minting are immediately dispatchable and deliver operator value before any excision. DockerProvider and the acceptance:container scenario close the campaign, followed by the solo wire/column rename that supersedes warren-c4f3. GH#846 items 4-5 (runtimeId union typing + lint guard) stay a published good-first-challenge, NOT a plan child: the contributor who shipped #887 has publicly claimed them as a separate PR, and no phase-2 child depends on them — the lift keys off the existing adapter registry, not the runtimeId type.
