sections.context: Warren has finished its inward phase: every seam except IssueTracker is live, the burrow absorption and self-host push shipped in v0.17.0, and the judge/calibration loop is running on GKE. The next phase is outward — detached public mirrors of foreign OSS repos and the corpus flywheel (docs/design/corpus-flywheel.md). Three things stand in the way. (1) Corpus-flywheel step 2 is unstarted: every dispatch made today without a decision log is unrecoverable training data for the future dispatch policy. (2) The IssueTracker seam is the last uncut seam; foreign setups must not be seeds-shaped, and the 2026-08-04 decision requires trackers to arrive through a RemoteTracker bridge. (3) The 2026-08-18 mirror-fleet code audit found concrete external-repo blockers: the agent image is bun+node only, PR base = run.ref breaks base-commit pinning (SHA base → GitHub 422), builtin prompts assert .seeds/.mulch/bun as facts, no per-project onboarding context reaches the prompt, and the shared host clone races under concurrent dispatch. v0.18.0 clears all three fronts plus the open reliability backlog, so that post-release focus can turn entirely to external projects.
sections.approach: Five tracks, forward-chained. Track A (steps 1-5): the dispatch-context log as a core insert-only dispatch_context table keyed by run_id, written fire-and-log inside spawnRun (the verified single choke point covering all 8 dispatch sites), after provenance plumbing (dispatchOrigin, dispatcherHandle, scheduled-seed seedId loss) and queue-state/runtime-kind introspection land; exported via a created_at-windowed analytics endpoint. Facts only, no interpretation, per agent-analytics §6.1; verdicts are never read (warren-9236 tripwire not triggered). Track B (steps 6-14): the IssueTracker cut — promote neutral DTOs into src/core (the 'seed' wire stem is already guarded), define the contract (getIssue/listIssueStatuses/closeIssue + capability flags supportsPlans/supportsMetadata/supportsScheduledIssues/isGitNative), wrap the existing src/seeds-cli facade as SeedsTracker, swap ServerDeps.seedsCli for deps.issueTracker, port read paths (plan-runs domain, HTTP handlers, the pr-context.ts hardcoded-sd leak), port write paths behind capabilities, add ordered-issue-list plan-runs for supportsPlans:false trackers, then build the RemoteTracker bridge speaking warren-tracker/v1 to an external container (extension holds its own credential; warren stores none) with a published conformance suite and FakeTracker reference. Linear defers to 0.19. Track C (steps 15-19): external-repo readiness — base-commit pinning (baseCommit dispatch field split from ref; PR base stays branch-shaped; ref validated at the HTTP boundary), per-project host-clone serialization + detached-HEAD-safe materialization, multi-stack agent image with a per-project agentImage override, tracker-neutral builtin prompts gated on project capabilities, and a per-project repoContext onboarding block injected at composeDispatchPrompt. Track D (steps 20-37): the adopted reliability backlog, chained where items share wire vocabulary or files. Step 38 is the release-readiness docs sweep. All owner decisions are locked in the seeds themselves; no step carries an open decision.

Two concurrent dispatches against one project with different base refs do not corrupt the host clone (serialization test).

A Python mirror repo with no .seeds/.mulch/.warren dispatches end-to-end: the agent image can run pytest, the prompt contains no false .seeds/.mulch/sd/ml assertions, and repoContext from the host-clone .warren/config.yaml reaches the prompt.
All adopted reliability seeds are closed with their fixes merged; bun run check:all passes 12/12; acceptance:container passes.
ROADMAP marks the IssueTracker seam Live and the release-readiness step leaves CHANGELOG/ROADMAP ready for the /release flow.

sections.context: The owner approved OpenClaw as the first target for a repository-generic GitHub upstream-contribution controller. Warren already executes bounded agent runs, pushes branches, monitors same-repository PR outcomes, and repairs CI, but it cannot represent a bot-owned fork targeting a separately owned upstream repository and it does not consume upstream review comments. The EOD objective is a dry-run-only vertical slice: explicit approved issue work is dispatched against warren-run-bot's fork, cross-fork PR intent is rendered but never posted, GitHub review/check/comment state is read and deduplicated without mutations, and all actions are durably journaled and inspectable. No credential may be discovered from GKE or written to repository state as part of this plan.
sections.approach: Build a standalone extensions/campaign-controller package that uses only Warren's published HTTP API and an extension-local GitHub client. Keep Warren core and the Forge contract unchanged for V0. The controller owns an immutable campaign manifest, repository policy, SQLite state, action-intent journal, approval digest, Warren/GitHub correlation, and an operator CLI. OpenClaw is data in a repository policy profile, not hard-coded behavior. Every external mutation is represented as a planned dry-run action; the V0 GitHub transport exposes reads plus pure PR-request rendering and has no callable write method. Use fake Warren and fake GitHub servers to prove dispatch, restart reconciliation, event deduplication, and the no-mutation boundary before any live read-only dry run.

alternatives.name: Expand Warren core Forge first
alternatives.rejected_because: The controller design requires extension-local GitHub friction to pay for provider-neutral promotion; V0 can prove cross-fork behavior without a core contract change.

alternatives.name: Build a general extension loader first
alternatives.rejected_because: A standalone controller can ship against published APIs, so a manifest/loader/catalog would add platform work before the first payer is proven.

alternatives.name: Use GitHub webhooks as the primary event source
alternatives.rejected_because: Warren cannot install its App on arbitrary upstream repositories; authenticated participating-notification polling plus authoritative reads works for the bot's PRs.

alternatives.name: Enable automatic discovery, claiming, PR posting, or replies in V0
alternatives.rejected_because: The owner approved dry-run only, and each mutation needs repository-specific evidence and an explicit later policy.

steps.title: Scaffold the standalone campaign-controller extension package
Define the V0 campaign manifest and OpenClaw repository-policy schemas
Implement the controller SQLite state store and action journal
Implement the controller Warren HTTP client and fake Warren server
Implement the read-only GitHub client and fake GitHub server
Implement immutable campaign validation, approval, and admission
Implement durable Warren dispatch and restart reconciliation
Render and journal dry-run cross-fork pull-request intents
Poll and deduplicate upstream PR reviews, comments, and checks read-only
Compose the dry-run tick, status, and attention CLI workflows
Prove the OpenClaw V0 end-to-end dry run and publish its operator runbook

risks: A GitHub credential with mutation authority could accidentally make dry-run code live; V0 must make mutation methods absent, not merely disabled by convention.
Lost Warren dispatch responses can duplicate paid work because server idempotency is not durable across restart; persist intent first and fail closed as dispatch_uncertain.
GitHub notifications are wake-ups rather than authoritative history; every notification must lead to current PR/review/comment/check reconciliation and node-id deduplication.
OpenClaw contribution policy can change; the repository-policy snapshot and source URL must be explicit and no live PR may be authorized from stale policy data.
Issue and review text is untrusted; it must never mutate controller policy or expose Warren/GitHub credentials.
The working tree already contains an unrelated .seeds change; preserve it and do not fold it into implementation commits accidentally.
acceptance: extensions/campaign-controller builds and tests as a standalone package without importing Warren src/** or scripts/**.
An immutable approved manifest can name OpenClaw upstream, warren-run-bot fork, explicit issue work, policy limits, agent/provider/model, and spend caps; changing a bound field invalidates approval.
Every dispatch and prospective GitHub mutation writes an action intent before I/O; restart reconciliation never blindly repeats an uncertain dispatch.
The controller can dispatch an explicit OpenClaw issue to Warren against the configured fork using fake infrastructure and correlate the resulting run and branch.
The controller renders the exact cross-fork PR request and persists it as dry-run evidence while the production V0 transport contains no GitHub mutation operation.
Review comments, issue comments, reviews/requested changes, and checks are polled read-only and deduplicated into durable PR events and attention items.
A CLI exposes validate, approve, tick/dry-run, status, and attention workflows with machine-readable output and no secret echoing.
An end-to-end fake-server acceptance test proves campaign approval through dispatch, terminal reconciliation, PR-intent rendering, review-event ingestion, restart, and stable no-duplicate state.

A read-only OpenClaw dry run may inspect public repository policy and issue/PR metadata but performs no GitHub mutation, secret discovery, GKE secret read, or real Warren paid dispatch unless separately authorized.
The operator runbook states the exact V0 boundary, required future credential setup, dry-run evidence review, and the explicit approval required before the first real PR.

sections.context: The Paper canvas 'Warren · Direction C — Operator Console' (43 artboards) is the approved replacement for the current src/ui. The design's premise: an agent run is a workload, and the interface behaves like an infrastructure console — one fixed shell carrying instance health, tables as inventories, event rows as evidence, green marking operability. The canvas ships a complete oklch token set (dark + light), Inter + JetBrains Mono, 17 desktop screens in both themes, 7 mobile screens, and a login screen. The canvas index artboard documents the IA. Design coverage is complete for every current UI surface: a dedicated Dispatch plan screen (dark + light) covers the plan-run dispatch flow, and the Run detail side column carries a Preview panel matching the existing preview-environments feature. The remaining gap is server-side only: the Operations dashboard (control-plane service health, lifecycle snapshot, spend rate, delivery stats, operator interventions), a global Event explorer, an Instance facts page, and the Telemetry Judge tab all need API surface that does not exist yet.
sections.approach: Rebuild src/ui in place, shell-first then page-by-page, against the existing React + Vite + Tailwind stack. The Paper token set becomes tokens.css, the single theming source. New server surface (ops overview, global events query, instance facts) lands as thin ROUTE_TABLE handlers over domain modules, each before the page that consumes it, with docs/openapi regenerated in the same PR. Every page is exported from Paper via get_jsx/get_computed_styles (never screenshots) and translated into repo conventions: kebab-case files, 500-line budget, wire types re-exported from src/core/wire.ts, client paths matching ROUTE_TABLE (check:client-contract). Each page issue replaces and deletes its legacy counterpart in the same PR so the bundle-size ratchet and dead-code guards stay honest at every merge. Light/dark theming and the spectator (public auth) projection are invariants on every page; acceptance scenario 39 remains the leak guard. Dependencies are forward-chained: pages block only on the shell, on the API they consume, and on the sibling page whose components they reuse, so independent pages stay dispatchable in any order.

alternatives.name: Greenfield second UI package alongside the old one, cut over at the end
alternatives.rejected_because: Doubles the bundle and the client-contract surface for the whole migration, and the check:bundle-size ratchet plus knip dead-code guard fight a parallel tree the entire time.

alternatives.name: Ship the redesign as pure CSS/token reskin of existing pages
alternatives.rejected_because: Direction C changes the IA (Operations-first, Telemetry consolidation, Event explorer, Instance page), not just the skin; a reskin cannot deliver the manifest the canvas documents.

alternatives.name: Build all API additions in one server milestone before any UI work
alternatives.rejected_because: Shell and inventory pages need no new API; front-loading server work serializes the plan for no reason. Each endpoint is its own issue, unblocked from day one, gating only its consuming page.

alternatives.name: One issue per screen pair (desktop + mobile together)
alternatives.rejected_because: The mobile artboards cover seven screens with one shared degradation pattern (collapsed nav, stacked rails, table-to-row-card); a single responsive pass after the pages exist is smaller than seven half-passes and avoids re-touching every page twice.

name: UI revamp: Direction C operator console

sections.context: Multiple warren users report the setup path is too hard for a casual, non-technical person: it assumes fluency in k8s/docker/bwrap, requires git-cloning the repo for a compose file, curating a 420-line .env, creating a GitHub PAT plus a machine account with a hand-composed noreply address, and grepping structured docker logs for the minted operator token. Two spikes on 2026-08-27 de-risked the target path: (1) a warren run on the macOS local runtime authenticated ONLY by CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN (Claude Max subscription, no ANTHROPIC_API_KEY) succeeded end-to-end and pushed branch burrow/run_zqf52t76x4m3 to jayminwest/warren-oauth-spike; (2) the GitHub App manifest flow (/github-app/register -> callback -> installed) renders a valid manifest with setup_url and clean single-use-nonce error paths, but deliberately persists nothing — it ends at a copy-these-env-vars-and-restart page. The spikes also surfaced two sharp edges: sandbox toolchain resolution follows the server PATH (a nix-provided git failed inside sandbox-exec with a dyld error, reaping the run as dropped_commit), and costUsd renders an API-priced estimate for subscription runs, which reads as a real bill.
sections.approach: Compose the casual path from primitives that already exist rather than building a new surface: `warren serve` already boots the full server natively on Bun (no Docker on macOS), the GitHub App manifest flow already eliminates PATs and machine accounts, and CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN is already forwarded into the sandbox by the anthropic provider profile. The target experience is: (1) curl -fsSL https://warren.run/install | sh, (2) `warren up` — detects the runtime, boots, auto-logs-in, opens the browser via a one-time setup code, (3) credential wizard offers 'use your Claude subscription' via claude setup-token before asking for an API key, (4) 'Connect GitHub' drives the existing App manifest flow with new opt-in credential persistence + forge hot-activation so the flow ends working, not at an env-var copy page, (5) a first-run UI checklist takes the user from connected forge to a repo picked from the App installation list to a dispatched starter run. Operator-grade paths (compose, k8s, PAT, explicit env) remain unchanged and documented in a separate operators section; the casual path is additive and opt-in at every point where it softens an existing security posture.

alternatives.name: Hosted SaaS onboarding (warren.run signs you up, no install)
alternatives.rejected_because: Contradicts the self-hosted trust model in README/SECURITY; warren's unit of trust is the operator's own deployment.

alternatives.name: One central marketplace GitHub App owned by the project
alternatives.rejected_because: Rejected by standing ROADMAP decision 2026-08-03: each deployment registers its own App via the manifest flow; the deployment, not a shared app, is the unit of trust.

alternatives.name: Docker-first casual path (require Docker Desktop on macOS)
alternatives.rejected_because: Docker Desktop install + login is itself the kind of friction the feedback names; kept as the fallback when sandbox-exec is unavailable and as the Linux operator path.

alternatives.name: Desktop app wrapper (Electron/menubar)
alternatives.rejected_because: Heavy new surface that duplicates the existing web UI; revisit only if the CLI-launched browser flow measurably fails casual users.

steps.title: npm package ships the built UI: publish src/ui/dist, wire release-time build, resolve WARREN_UI_DIST_DIR for the npm layout
warren up: runtime autodetect (darwin sandbox-exec / linux bwrap / docker fallback), data dir + boot defaults, automatic operator-token client login
One-time browser auth handoff: single-use setup code minted at boot, /setup redemption route logs the browser into the UI, warren up auto-opens it
Credential wizard in warren up: Claude subscription via claude setup-token or pasted API key, GitHub token via gh detection or paste, persisted 0600 under ~/.warren
Honest cost display for subscription-auth runs: costBasis wire field (api | subscription_estimate), UI badge, cap semantics documented
Sandbox git preflight: verify the resolved git executes inside the sandbox profile at project-add and doctor --local; clear error instead of dropped_commit
GitHub App credential persistence + forge hot-activation (opt-in): store the app triple under the data dir from the callback/installed flow and activate GitHubApp forge without restart
Default run-branch prefix warren/ for fresh installs (replace legacy burrow/ default, existing deployments keep their configured value)
First-run UI onboarding: zero-project instances render a setup checklist (connect GitHub, add repo, dispatch) instead of the empty operator console
Repo picker: Add Project lists the App installation's repositories when the GitHubApp forge is active; PAT mode keeps URL paste
Starter-task dispatch: after the first project registers, the onboarding checklist offers a prefilled low-risk starter run
Install script: scripts/install.sh (bun bootstrap + npm i -g @os-eco/warren-cli) served at warren.run/install, with CI smoke coverage
Docs restructure: casual path above the fold in README + quickstart rewrite; runtime topology, compose, k8s, PAT, machine-account content moves to an operators section

risks: macOS sandbox-exec is Apple-deprecated and toolchain-sensitive (spike: nix git dyld failure inside the profile); if it proves too fragile the casual Mac path degrades to requiring Docker Desktop, which weakens the whole pitch — step 6 is the mitigation and must land early.

Subscription tokens only serve the claude-code harness; pi and other providers still need API keys — the wizard must not imply otherwise. Anthropic rate limits are the subscription's own, and long-lived setup-token semantics could change upstream.

The App-flow credentials page today promises 'warren keeps no copy'; step 7 deliberately weakens that for opt-in local deployments — the opt-in boundary and 0600 storage need review-grade care and an explicit SECURITY.md note.

The manifest conversion POST against live github.com was exercised only to the boundary in the spike (state nonce + error paths verified; real code redemption not clickable headlessly); first human walk-through of step 7 may surface GitHub-side surprises.
Publishing the built UI grows the npm package and adds a build step to release.yml; a publish that skips the build ships a UI-less package — needs a pack-and-serve smoke gate.
check:bundle-size, check:size, and gen:docs/openapi/cli-ref gates all bite UI and route-table changes across steps 3, 7, 9, 10, 11 — each child must run bun run check:all before PR.
acceptance: On a fresh macOS machine with only the install script run and a Claude Max subscription: `warren up` reaches a browser tab already logged into the warren UI without the user reading a log line, editing an env file, or creating an API key.

The first-run UI takes that user from Connect GitHub (App manifest click-through, no PAT, no machine account) to a repository picked from the installation list to a dispatched starter run whose branch is pushed, with the App forge active without a manual env edit or restart.
A run authenticated by CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN displays its cost as a subscription estimate, not a bill.
A sandbox with a non-executable git fails at project-add or doctor with an error naming the binary, never as a dropped_commit run failure.
Existing operator paths (compose, k8s, PAT forge, explicit env config) behave identically with none of the new opt-ins enabled, and bun run check:all passes on every child PR.
README and quickstart present the casual path first; runtime topology and credential internals live in an operators section.

sections.context: The Direction C operator-console rebuild (pl-7e38) is live but carries release-blocking UI bugs reported from a page-by-page walk of a real deployment: a half-width topbar on every page, double carets on the /runs filters, frozen live-run durations on the 45s-poll list pages, overlapping event-kind labels and a fixed-height event stream on /runs/:id, a stale placeholder in the Operations 'Control Plane Events' panel even though its two blockers (warren-5eec global event query API, warren-24b9 Event explorer) both shipped and closed on 2026-08-26, horizontal chart overflow on every /telemetry tab, full-float difficulty scores on /telemetry behavior, and a /telemetry judge tab that claims the judge extension is not deployed against an instance where it is running. Operators are the affected users; several of these read as broken-on-arrival and block the release.
sections.reproduction: Against a live instance with running runs and the judge extension deployed: (1) Open any page at md+ width — the topbar border and figures stop roughly mid-viewport instead of spanning the page. (2) /runs — with filters at rest, State/Agent/Project/Trigger each show an inline '⌄' next to the label plus the browser's native select arrow. (3) /runs — the Duration cell of a running run stays frozen until the 45s refetch or a manual refresh; /operations durations tick every second. Same freeze on /plan-runs Elapsed. (4) /runs/:id — an event like reap.workspace_destroyed paints over the summary text in its row; the event stream box is a fixed ~561px tall, leaving large dead space above the bottom while the steer box sits far below it. (5) /operations — 'Control Plane Events' shows the warren-5eec/warren-24b9 placeholder paragraph instead of events. (6) /telemetry (all tabs) — the widest horizontal bar row overflows the page and creates document-level horizontal scroll; on behavior, 'Where runs die' overflows and DIFFICULTY renders values like 0.8333333333333334 into the FAIL SHARE column. (7) /telemetry judge tab — shows 'The judge extension is not deployed against this instance.' despite a healthy judge; expected: verdict evidence.
sections.root_cause: Five independent clusters, all with exact locations. (A) Shell: console-shell.tsx:54 wraps ConsoleTopbar in a row-flex div ('hidden md:flex'); the topbar <header> (console-topbar.tsx:119) has no w-full/flex-1, so as a row-flex item it sizes to max-content — the internal flex-1 spacer contributes zero intrinsic width. The mobile arm nests the same header inside another flex row (console-shell.tsx:50) with the same defect. (B) /runs: a literal '⌄' glyph is baked into the placeholder option labels (runs.tsx:188,245,253,262 — carried over from the static design export docs/ui-revamp/screens/runs.jsx) on top of the native select arrow; and formatDuration (runs/runs-format.ts:19) defaults now=Date.now() evaluated per render, with re-renders only from a 45s refetchInterval — /operations works because operations.tsx:31-39 keeps a 1s useState/setInterval 'now' and threads it as a required arg (operations/operations.helpers.ts:41). plan-runs/walk-state.ts:47-54 has the identical defect. (C) /runs/:id: event-tail.tsx:53 gives the kind cell w-[108px] shrink-0 with no truncate — dot-separated kinds have no break opportunity, so ~16 server-emitted kinds (reap.* family worst, up to 36 chars) paint over the summary; event-explorer.tsx:379 already does this correctly with truncate. The stream body is h-[520px] (event-tail.tsx:185) and its section lacks flex-1 (:122), so the card declines the flex-1 row height while every shrink-0 sidebar panel (uncapped PromptPanel included, side-panels.tsx:152) sets the row height — dead space = sidebar height minus a constant 561px. The expanded-payload ml-[117px] at :62 is an underived offset coupled to the column widths. (D) /operations events panel: operations/events-panel.tsx:24-26 placeholder and :2-8 doc comment are stale — GET /events shipped (route-table.ts:163, readPublic) and eventsApi.list exists (api/client.ts:271-287); the Event explorer page shipped at /events (app.tsx:148) but is orphaned: no console-nav.ts entry and zero links to it. (E) /telemetry: warren-7197 rebuilt tabs with hand-rolled bars where the mark div takes a percentage width that resolves against the WHOLE row while fixed-width labels sit beside it and shrink-0 forbids correction — four sites (loop-tab.tsx:84-107, behavior-tab.tsx:99-113 and :21-38, judge-tab.tsx:161-178) plus loop-tab.tsx:148's min-w-[3px] column floor; the rebuild also dropped the old .toFixed(2) on difficultyScore (behavior-tab.tsx:33,36; the deleted run-analytics/directory-struggle.tsx:73 had it) and deleted the shared format.ts, duplicating formatDuration into loop-tab.tsx:15-22 and economics-tab.tsx:131-138. Judge tab: judge-verdicts.ts:63 fetches VITE_JUDGE_BASE_URL ?? '' — same-origin to warren, which serves the SPA index.html with HTTP 200 for unmatched GETs (src/server/ui.ts:71-79), so res.ok passes, every HTML line fails the swallowed JSON.parse (:98-100), rows.length===0 maps to {available:false, reason:'error'} (:103), and judge-tab.tsx:32-35 prints 'not deployed' for it. Behind that: the judge is a separate process/Service with its own JUDGE_EXPORT_TOKEN (extensions/judge/src/server.ts:83-90) that the browser must never hold, warren's CSP is connect-src 'self' (src/server/response.ts:22-23) so a cross-origin base URL is blocked anyway, and a legitimately empty verdict page is also misclassified as failure.
sections.approach: Minimal class-level fixes where the defect is a class (topbar w-full, truncate, flex-1); shared primitives where duplication caused the bug (a useNow hook for all ticking durations with 'now' made a required parameter so call sites cannot silently freeze again; one MeterBar primitive with a flex-1 min-w-0 track for all four telemetry bar sites; a shared telemetry format module restoring toFixed and deduplicating formatDuration). The Operations events panel binds the already-shipped GET /events via the existing eventsApi.list and the event-explorer-format helpers rather than any new API, and the orphaned /events page gets a nav entry. For the judge tab the fix is architectural: a warren-side operator-gated reverse-proxy route for the judge export keeps the browser same-origin (satisfying CSP), holds JUDGE_EXPORT_TOKEN server-side (extensions seam intact per the audit-log FRICTION list), and is registered ahead of the SPA catch-all; the client then gets honest state classification (empty page = healthy-empty, HTML/wrong content-type = misconfigured, distinct copy per state) so the SPA fallback can never masquerade as a verdict feed again. Steps are forward-chained: same-file steps are serialized (runs.tsx, event-tail.tsx, telemetry tabs, judge proxy before its consumers) and everything converges on a final build-and-gates verification sweep. Alternatives rejected: VITE_JUDGE_BASE_URL cross-origin (CSP-blocked, leaks the judge token to the browser); per-page setInterval copies (the drift that caused this); hand-tuning each bar row (four sites already diverged).

The mocks specify a shared mobile chrome (48px brand bar, 34px four-figure status strip, 54px five-tab bottom nav) that does not exist — the shell ships a hamburger + drawer instead. Beyond divergence, the audit found bug-grade mobile breakage: /runs, /plan-runs, and the operations Active Workloads panel trap their loading/error/empty states inside hidden md:block, so phones see a bare empty box; the operations two-column rows never stack at 375px (min-w-0 + zero flex-basis children never trigger flex-wrap) and render as two crushed columns; the dispatch resolved-manifest rail is a fixed w-[350px] that overflows the 347px content box and silently clips values; the event-explorer row's 208px of fixed columns leaves ~83px (~13 chars) for the summary; the run-detail event-tail header holds ~410px of non-wrapping controls in ~347px under overflow-clip; and every form control is sub-16px, triggering iOS Safari focus auto-zoom — the shared responsive contract in src/ui/src/components/ui/responsive.ts (warren-3315) landed with ZERO consumers (the warren-42ba application pass never happened). sections.approach: Three layers, forward-chained. (1) Foundations first: hoist the trapped mobile loading/error/empty states (pure bug), build the mock's shared chrome (brand bar + 34px status strip, then the 54px bottom tab nav with the '·· More' tab re-targeting the existing drawer), adopt the already-shipped responsive.ts contract (responsiveFormControl / responsiveFooterActions) as its first real consumers to kill iOS focus-zoom and undersized touch targets, and extend the shared InventoryRowCard to the mock's card contract (optional dot-only state column, optional meta row, 12/9 padding, reachable neutral tone, warning figure tone) so every screen's card arm conforms by construction. (2) Per-screen conformance in mock order: operations (stack the crushed rows, gate services/lifecycle to md+, 2x2 capacity grid, in-card thead headers, dot-only workload rows with footer + cost tint), runs (two-line card anatomy, pill filter strip, thead column strip + Load-more footer), run detail (compact connector phase rail, event-tail mobile degradation, mock section order with Prompt/RunDefinition/Preview collapsed, header/steering scale), dispatch (rail overflow fix, card-per-section arm with 7-line manifest summary + admission band, ported to plan-dispatch), event explorer (two-line row, chip filter strip), instance (2-up field grid with inset value boxes, fixed-label fact rows), telemetry (stacked-panels arm without tabs below md per the mock, 2x2 metric grid, table->meter/card arms, judge stacked segment bar). (3) The no-mock pages (plan-run-detail, project-detail, projects) get the shared degradation pattern by analogy, and one verification sweep at 375/390/768 closes the plan. Same-file steps are serialized via blocks; cross-plan blockers on pl-3ce8 issues (warren-1b58 topbar, warren-1c7b nav, warren-4cf8 events panel, warren-7f85 carets, warren-b610 durations, warren-7264/warren-6f3e event tail, warren-67f2/warren-18f3/warren-f927 telemetry) are added as seed dependencies so no agent pair edits the same lines concurrently.

sections.context: The first live cross-fork PR (openclaw#131131) proved the open-a-PR half of the loop and immediately exposed the missing half. The upstream review bot (ClawSweeper) blocked the PR with actionable feedback — a P1 config-contract finding, a real-behavior-proof requirement, and a body-update-triggers-re-review protocol — and the controller can only watch: every mutation except createPullRequest is off, warren runs cannot push to an existing branch, and the agent prompt carried no repo design norms, so the agent claimed public config surface and missed an existing fallback mechanism. Separately, the PR-body headings were hardcoded to one repo's CI gate, manifest revisions produced six unresolved attention items in a day, and stale failing_checks attention never auto-resolves. Phase 3 must close the respond-iterate-land loop while keeping every repo-specific behavior in profile data, not controller conditionals, so the same controller works against any target repository.
sections.approach: Three tracks, forward-chained. (1) Generalize: everything openclaw-shaped moves into the repository profile as versioned, digest-bound data — the PR-body section contract, an agent-guidance prompt block encoding contribution design norms, evidence-tier declarations, and review-bot grammar (bot logins, marker formats, re-review commands). (2) Respond: warren core gains dispatch-onto-existing-branch so a follow-up run can extend a live PR; the controller gains the phase-3 mutation vocabulary (updatePullRequest, postComment, updateBranch, follow-up pushes) each individually policy-gated and journaled-before-I/O exactly like createPullRequest; a follow-up coordinator turns classified review feedback into follow-up runs, body refreshes, and comment replies, with untrusted-comment discipline throughout. (3) Operate: attention auto-resolve, a manifest amendment flow that stops the supersession churn, merged/closed terminal accounting with cost-per-merged-PR metrics, and a second non-openclaw profile driven through the fake-GitHub e2e to prove nothing is hyperfit. Chosen over a monolithic response engine because each mutation stays separately approvable and auditable, and over openclaw-specific fixes because the next target repo must be a data edit.

alternatives.name: Keep the controller observe-only and shepherd every PR manually
alternatives.rejected_because: Does not scale past one PR; the operator becomes the response loop, which is exactly the toil the controller exists to remove. Review bots already define machine-followable protocols the controller can speak.

alternatives.name: Encode openclaw's rubric (headings, ClawSweeper commands) directly in controller code
alternatives.rejected_because: Hyperfits to one repo; if openclaw becomes a headache the whole investment strands. Profile-as-data keeps the exit cheap and matches the existing 'openclaw is data, never conditionals' design rule.

alternatives.name: Long-lived run pods that stay alive to react to review feedback
alternatives.rejected_because: Burns budget idling, fights the ephemeral-run model, and a pod that outlives its run is an unbounded liability. Fresh follow-up runs on the existing branch get the same result with bounded cost and a journaled intent per iteration.

alternatives.name: Give the review bot's comments direct command authority over follow-up runs
alternatives.rejected_because: Upstream comments are untrusted input. They may only ever be classified into evidence; every mutation still requires the owner-approved policy digest to enable it and a journaled intent to execute.

steps.title: profile: PR-body contract as data — section names, order, footer, disclosure block per repository profile (kill hardcoded headings)
profile: versioned agentGuidance block injected into every dispatch prompt (minimal-diff, no new public config surface, no fail-closed validation on previously-valid config, cite existing mechanisms)
profile+manifest: evidence tiers — declare local-provable vs external-proof-required per issue; render the known-gap / operator-proof slot in the PR body
reconcile: review-feedback classifier — normalize upstream events into actionable categories via profile-declared bot grammar (untrusted-input discipline)
warren core: dispatch a run onto an existing branch — run checks out and pushes back to a named head branch instead of composing warren/run_<id>
mutations phase 3: individually policy-gated updatePullRequest / postComment / updateBranch / followUpPush flags, transport methods, and journaled intents
follow-up run coordinator: classified feedback -> journaled follow-up intent -> warren run on the existing PR branch -> reconcile the push, under budget caps
mutation: updatePullRequest body refresh — re-render the body contract with new evidence and response summary after a follow-up lands
mutation: postComment — finding-response replies and profile-declared re-review commands, never echoing untrusted comment content
branch freshness: detect behind-base/conflicted PRs on reconcile; journaled updateBranch when clean, conflict-repair follow-up run when not
attention hygiene: auto-resolve failing_checks on green, resolve superseded-manifest items on approval, dedupe review-bot placeholder noise
manifest amendment flow: append issues / adjust budget via digest-re-approved amendment without spawning a superseded campaign row per edit
terminal accounting: merged/closed PR -> work-item outcome + campaign report (PRs opened/merged, cost per merged PR, iterations per PR)
second-profile proof: onboard a non-openclaw repository profile and drive the full respond-iterate-land loop through the fake-GitHub e2e with both profiles

risks: Dispatch-onto-existing-branch touches warren's workspace composition, which every provider shares — a regression there breaks all runs, not just follow-ups; keep the new path opt-in behind an explicit dispatch field.
A follow-up loop that reacts to bot reviews can ping-pong (push -> re-review -> new findings -> push). Cap follow-up iterations per work item in policy and stop on repeat findings.

Prompt-injection via upstream comments: classified feedback flows into follow-up prompts. The classifier must pass through only structured fields (check names, file paths, finding titles) with provenance marked untrusted, never raw comment bodies as instructions.
Renderer or contract changes alter request digests, so they only affect intents journaled after deploy — sequence deploys so no planned-unexecuted intents exist (same hazard warren-743f hit).
Budget: each feedback iteration is a paid run; without per-work-item iteration caps a hostile or chatty reviewer drains the campaign budget.
Profile grammar for review bots will drift as upstream bots change format; provenance-stamped profile snapshots with staleness bounds (already the policy pattern) must cover the grammar too.
acceptance: No repository-specific string (heading, bot login, command, path rule) remains in controller source — grep proves openclaw appears only under profiles/ and test fixtures.

A follow-up run dispatched from classified review feedback pushes commits to the existing PR head branch, and the journaled intent chain (feedback -> intent -> run -> push -> body refresh) is replayable from the action journal alone.

Every phase-3 mutation is individually disabled by default, enabled only by a fresh owner-approved manifest digest, and journaled planned-before-I/O; the e2e proves a disabled flag makes the mutation structurally impossible, not just skipped.
The fake-GitHub e2e runs the full loop against two different repository profiles with different body contracts and bot grammars, green.
Attention items for a check that later passes auto-resolve within one reconcile tick; manifest amendments produce zero superseded attention rows.
Campaign status reports PRs opened, PRs merged, cost per merged PR, and follow-up iterations per PR.

sections.context: Supabase egress for the warren-dogfood project reached 659 GB against a 250 GB Pro allowance in the current billing cycle, while the database itself is only 385 MB. The egress is warren's own doing: the read-time cost hydrator (src/runs/usage-hydrate.ts, warren-ab18) re-reads every kind=state_change/stream=system event for terminal runs whose cost_usd is null on every GET /runs, /analytics/runs and /analytics/behavior call, never persists the result, and drags in agent_end envelopes averaging 103 kB. 27 permanently-null runs make that ~4,800 rows / ~6 MB per list call; the UI polls every 45 s; Supabase (AWS us-west-1) to GKE (GCP us-west1) is cross-cloud egress. pg_stat_statements shows ~102 M event rows returned in the 15 days since the Aug 17 rename. Separately, GCP spend is dominated by a 1 TiB Filestore Basic HDD instance (~$200/mo, warren-repo-cache, created 2026-08-27 for the openclaw 2.9 GB clone) that an Aug 1 decision had rejected on cost. Agent run pods run on standard Autopilot capacity although they are ephemeral and retry-safe. Operator intent: fix the egress bug regardless, leave Supabase for an in-cluster Postgres on GKE with real backup layers, move run pods to Spot, replace the Filestore cache with a blobless clone, and land infra spend near $75/mo from ~$340/mo.
sections.approach: Five forward-chained tracks, each a data or manifest change first and a human-timed live action second. Every step is labelled either agent-ok (a single warren agent can do it end-to-end from the repo, gates green, PR opened) or human-only (touches live GCP/Supabase state, needs a timing decision, or spends money). (A) Egress: make the hydrator write derived totals back to runs so a run is hydrated once, and narrow the usage query to the two envelope types it reads; the human then confirms the egress curve flattens. (B) Postgres on GKE: ship an opt-in kustomize component (postgres:17 StatefulSet on a 10 GiB standard-rwo claim, ClusterIP Service, NetworkPolicy admitting only the warren pod, nightly pg_dump CronJob to GCS via Workload Identity, restore Job) plus a DSN-to-DSN parity script and a rewritten runbook section; the human provisions the bucket and snapshot schedule, rehearses a restore, then cuts over at an idle window by dump/restore, parity check, secret rewrite, scale-up. Postgres-to-Postgres was chosen so the drizzle journal and every migration carry over untouched. (C) Spot: an env-gated pod-spec knob adds the gke-spot nodeSelector and toleration to run pods only, preemption is classified as an infra-lost retryable cause, and the human enables it on the live overlay through the same GitHub repo-variable pattern warren-8175 used for the repo cache. (D) Filestore: workspace-init falls back to a blobless partial clone when no cache PVC is set, the human flips the openclaw project off the cache and deletes the 1 TiB instance. (E) Sizing: an analysis step documents actual run-pod peak memory against the 16 GiB live request and Autopilot's 1:6.5 CPU:memory billing ratio so the operator can right-size. The plan closes on a 30-day billing review.

alternatives.name: Keep Supabase Pro and only fix the hydrator
alternatives.rejected_because: Fixes the overage but keeps a $25/mo cross-cloud dependency the operator has explicitly decided to outgrow; every future read path is one bug away from another egress bill.

alternatives.name: Cloud SQL db-f1-micro
alternatives.rejected_because: Zero-ops and same-region, but ~$10/mo for a 385 MB single-replica database, plus a private-IP/VPC setup the cluster does not have today. In-cluster Postgres with a snapshot schedule and a nightly dump to GCS costs about the same in pod requests and keeps everything in the manifests warren already ships.

alternatives.name: SQLite on the existing warren-data PVC
alternatives.rejected_because: Cheapest possible, and the runbook says nothing forces Postgres under k8s, but there is no Postgres-to-SQLite export tooling in the repo and the events corpus is an RL asset that must survive intact. Postgres-to-Postgres is a pg_dump/pg_restore with no translation risk.

alternatives.name: Keep the Filestore cache but shrink it
alternatives.rejected_because: Basic HDD has a 1 TiB minimum and Basic SSD a 2.5 TiB minimum; there is no smaller RWX tier. A blobless clone brings a 2.9 GB repo down to a fraction of that without shared storage.

alternatives.name: Spot for every pod including the control plane
alternatives.rejected_because: The warren, judge, campaign-controller and Postgres pods are stateful or long-lived; a preemption there is an outage, not a retry. Only run pods are retry-safe.

steps.title: hydrator: persist derived cost/tokens back to runs so a terminal run is hydrated at most once (write-through in hydrateRunsUsage + backfill on terminal reconciliation; write 0 when no envelopes exist)

HUMAN: deploy the hydrator fixes, confirm pg_stat_statements rows-per-call for the events IN(...) query drops below 100 and the Supabase egress curve flattens over 48h

postgres: opt-in kustomize component deploy/k8s/components/postgres (postgres:17 StatefulSet, 10Gi standard-rwo PVC, ClusterIP Service, Secret template, NetworkPolicy admitting only the warren pod, 250m/1Gi requests, standard capacity)
postgres: backup layer manifests — nightly pg_dump -Fc CronJob to a GCS bucket via Workload Identity, a parameterised restore Job, and a ServiceAccount for both; document retention expectations

HUMAN: provision the live backup substrate — GCS bucket (versioning, 30-day lifecycle), Workload Identity binding for the backup SA, apply the postgres component to the warren namespace, patch its PV reclaimPolicy to Retain, attach a daily PD snapshot schedule to the disk

postgres: migration tooling — scripts/pg-migrate/ with dump (public + drizzle schemas only, --no-owner --no-privileges), restore, and a DSN-to-DSN parity check (row counts per table, max(events.id), drizzle journal hash) plus a rewritten RUNBOOK-K8S §1.5 cutover procedure

HUMAN: rehearsal — restore the latest Supabase dump into the in-cluster Postgres, run the parity script, boot a shadow warren against it over port-forward, run one dispatch end-to-end, then verify a restore from the GCS backup and from a PD snapshot

HUMAN: cutover at an idle window — scale warren to 0, final dump/restore, parity check, rewrite warren-secrets/warren-db-url to the in-cluster DSN (no sslmode flags), scale up, smoke-test a dispatch; keep Supabase untouched as the rollback for 7 days

postgres: strip Supabase from the repo — pooler/sslmode notes in RUNBOOK-K8S become a tombstone, secrets.yaml comments, k8s-migration design record §6.1 scope-status, deploy/k8s/README DB section; keep check-rls and the Postgres test path unchanged

HUMAN: decommission Supabase after the 7-day rollback window — take a final archival dump beside the July one, pause then delete the warren-dogfood project, remove the supabase MCP entry from .claude/settings.local.json, drop the DB URL from any .env

spot: WARREN_K8S_SPOT env knob in pod-spec.ts that adds nodeSelector cloud.google.com/gke-spot=true and the matching NoSchedule toleration to run pods only; document in RUNBOOK-K8S §3 and the env contract; unit tests for both states

spot: classify Spot preemption (pod status.reason Terminated / node-shutdown message, or pod vanished with a deleted spot node) as an infra-lost retryable cause so infra-lost retry redispatches it; add a warren_run_preempted_total metric next to the eviction counter

HUMAN: enable Spot on the live overlay via a GitHub repo variable rendered by deploy-gke.yml (same pattern as WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC), watch a week of runs, confirm at least one preempted run retried and the run-pod cost line falls in the billing report

filestore: workspace-init falls back to a blobless partial clone (--filter=blob:none) when WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC is unset; prove push from the partial clone still works in the finalize path; measure init time on a ~3 GB repo and record it in the PR

HUMAN: unset the WARREN_K8S_REPO_CACHE_PVC repo variable, redeploy, verify an openclaw run initialises in under 3 minutes, then delete the warren-repo-cache PVC and confirm the 1 TiB Filestore instance is gone from gcloud filestore instances list

filestore: docs — RUNBOOK-K8S §5.3/§7.5 and deploy/k8s/README repo-cache section record that Filestore was tried and removed, blobless clone is the default, and the cache stays opt-in for single-node clusters only

sizing: analysis of actual run-pod peak memory across August runs versus the 16 GiB live request, with Autopilot's 1:6.5 CPU:memory billing ratio and minimums documented in RUNBOOK-K8S; propose a request/limit pair with the cost delta, operator decides
HUMAN: 30-day cost review — GCP billing report for the warren project and the Supabase invoice; confirm infra spend near the $75/mo target and record the outcome on the plan

risks: Persisting hydrated totals changes runs.cost_usd from null to a number for 27 historical runs; anything that treated null as 'unknown' (analytics, judge cost caps) must accept a computed value. Keep cost_basis untouched and add a test for the zero-envelope case.

pg_restore of a Supabase dump can fail on Supabase-only roles, extensions, or RLS policies if the dump is not restricted to the public and drizzle schemas with --no-owner --no-privileges. The parity script exists to catch a partial restore before cutover.

A single Postgres pod restarts during Autopilot node upgrades; warren requests fail for one to two minutes. Acceptable for dogfood; the runbook must say so, and CloudNativePG is the upgrade path if it stops being acceptable.

All existing PVs use reclaimPolicy Delete. Deleting the namespace or the claim destroys the disk. The Retain patch plus PD snapshots plus GCS dumps are three independent layers; the rehearsal step must prove a restore from each.
Spot preemption gives 25 s notice. A run mid-finalize can lose an unpushed branch; infra-lost retry redispatches from scratch, so the retry cost is the run's model spend, capped by maxCostUsd.

A blobless clone lazily fetches blobs on checkout and on git operations that touch history; an agent that runs git log -p or blame across the whole repo triggers many small fetches. Measure on openclaw before flipping the live overlay.
The GKE cluster fee ($73/mo) is only waived if this is the sole cluster on the billing account; the cost target assumes it is.
acceptance: pg_stat_statements on the live database shows the events IN(...) hydration query returning fewer than 100 rows per call, and the Supabase egress meter stops growing before decommission.
Warren runs against an in-cluster Postgres reachable only from the warren pod; the parity script reports zero differences between the final Supabase dump and the live database at cutover.
Three restore paths were exercised before cutover: from a GCS pg_dump, from a PD snapshot, and via the retained PV after a simulated claim deletion.
The warren-dogfood Supabase project is deleted and no repo file, secret, or workflow references a supabase.co or pooler.supabase.com host.

Run pods carry the gke-spot nodeSelector and toleration when WARREN_K8S_SPOT is set; a preempted run finalizes with a retryable infra-lost cause and is redispatched; control-plane pods stay on standard capacity.
gcloud filestore instances list is empty for the warren project and an openclaw run initialises in under 3 minutes via a blobless clone.
A 30-day GCP billing report shows total infra spend (cluster, pods, disks, LB, backups) at or below roughly $75/mo excluding the cluster fee, and the plan outcome is recorded.

sections.context: A page-by-page operator review of the console on 2026-09-03 found roughly forty defects. Seven read-only scouting passes traced each one to a root cause. The recurring shapes: (1) the Direction C header shipped as a static artboard and BURN / RUNTIME are still hard-coded placeholders even though GET /ops/overview and GET /instance now serve the figures; (2) copy across every page explains warren's architecture ('control plane', 'materialize', 'harness definitions', 'this instance') instead of labelling the UI; (3) the public projection removes fields that the UI types declare as required, so /plan-runs and /plan-runs/:id crash for spectators on formatCostUsd(undefined).toFixed; (4) the run-detail phase rail derives every stage from a dead event-kind probe plus terminal fallbacks because the runs table has no stage timestamps, so the strip is untrustworthy; (5) /operations carries an interventions panel whose only writer is k8s steering and whose rows flip out of 'unread' within seconds, an unwindowed Delivery card beside a 24h Spend card, and a spectator projection that strips everything but run counts; (6) /telemetry renders one of the seven cost breakdowns /analytics/cost already returns, reads the oldest 500 judge rows instead of the newest, has no project filter although every analytics endpoint accepts ?projectId, and prints judge infrastructure failures under a 'FAILING CLASS' header.
sections.approach: Twenty children grouped by page, with UI-only fixes first and additive wire changes stacked behind them so the visible defects land in the first PRs. Each child title carries the file:line sites and the root cause so a dispatched agent can start without re-scouting. Copy fixes ride inside the page child that already touches the file; a final sweep child covers the pages no other child opens. Spectator exposure follows the existing classification pattern (PUBLIC_*/REDACTED_* field lists + pickFields + the public-projections partition test), and every widening is fenced by scenario 39. Two policy calls are made explicitly rather than by omission: spend in USD stays operator-only on /ops/overview (the analytics redaction lists and scenario 39's FORBIDDEN_FIELD_NAMES already say aggregate USD is private; spectators get delivery counts and runs-in-window instead), and the overall cost-per-merged-PR ratio becomes public on /analytics/runs with the buckets kept redacted and scenario 39 hardened to walk that subtree. Stage timing gets real columns (workspace_ready_at, agent_ready_at, agent_ended_at, reaped_at) written at the moments the runtime already observes, rather than more event-stream heuristics. The judge extension's malformed_verdict flood is filed as a live investigation child, not guessed at from the repo.
